Within the right hemisphere, higher-order auditory regions neighboring the STS preferentially responded to social visual features whereas lower-level visual features were represented broadly across the auditory hierarchy. These results suggest that proximity and connectivity principles govern anatomical expansion of information encoding in sensory loss.

papers.title: Early Increases in Hippocampal Synchrony Predict Chronic Epileptiform Burden in a Temporal Lobe Epilepsy Model
papers.abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE), the most common focal epilepsy, is often drug-resistant and arises predominantly in the hippocampus. Disease severity is conventionally assessed by seizure frequency and duration, yet epileptiform activity outside discrete seizures may also track disease progression. Whether this activity reflects hippocampal network reorganization as part of epileptogenesis, and whether such reorganization predicts chronic severity, is unknown. Here, we combined longitudinal two-photon calcium imaging of hippocampal CA1 neurons with repeated 24-hour EEG recordings that quantified epileptiform burden in the same pilocarpine treated mice over 16 weeks. CA1 firing and synchrony rose acutely, subsided during a latent period, and increased again chronically, with synchronized firing organized into brief waves that propagated in a consistent direction. Epileptiform burden followed a similar temporal trajectory and increasingly contained electrographic seizures. CA1 synchrony correlated with epileptiform burden and stratified mice into groups with distinct neuronal and electrographic outcomes. CA1 synchrony measured within three weeks of pilocarpine induction predicted chronic epileptiform burden, identifying early hippocampal synchrony as a candidate imaging biomarker and pointing to an early window for intervention in TLE.

papers.title: Epigenetic reprogramming by promoter hypomethylation is linked to aberrant gene expression and transcriptomic plasticity in colorectal cancer
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) has high phenotypic plasticity, but regulatory mechanisms of aberrant cell states are not well described. We investigated DNA methylation-based regulation of cancer cell-intrinsic transcriptomic heterogeneity in 1,183 multiregional primary tumor samples, liver metastases and tumor organoids. Most genes with strong methylation-transcriptomic association reflected canonical promoter hypermethylation and expression repression related to the CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP). However, promoter hypomethylation and overexpression of APOLD1 and ELF5 identified two largely non-overlapping subgroups of canonical CIMP-negative CRCs enriched with stem-like and transit-amplifying cell states. APOLD1 tumors were further highly proliferative while ELF5 tumors were slow-cycling and associated with good survival in early-stage disease. Target genes showed patient-specific expression changes in matched primary-metastasis samples, and ELF5 aberrant metastases showed ex vivo sensitivity to putative targeting of stem cells by PI3K/mTOR inhibition, fetal de-differentiation and transition into non-canonical intestinal states. This implicates focal promoter hypomethylation in phenotypic plasticity in CRC metastasis.

papers.title: Clinical-Anchored Incremental Survival Learning: A Stability-Constrained Framework for Molecularly Enhanced Survival Prediction in Lung Adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Accurate survival prediction in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains challenging because high-dimensional molecular data can introduce overfitting and unstable feature selection. We developed Clinical-Anchored Incremental Survival Learning (CAISL), a framework that integrates a sparse molecular risk correction with a clinical baseline to improve prognostic discrimination while constraining model complexity and prediction variability. CAISL was evaluated using The Cancer Genome Atlas LUAD cohort comprising 470 patients and 119 observed deaths. Performance was compared with clinical Cox, molecular-only, and unanchored multimodal models using five independently seeded, event-stratified five-fold cross-validation runs. CAISL achieved a mean concordance index (C-index) of 0.7246, compared with 0.6970 for clinical Cox, yielding an absolute improvement of 0.0276 (95% bootstrap confidence interval [CI], 0.005 to 0.050). Time-dependent discrimination was higher at three years (AUC, 0.742 vs. 0.712) and five years (AUC, 0.721 vs. 0.691), while the integrated Brier score was lower for CAISL than for clinical Cox (0.164 vs. 0.181). Ablation analysis identified clinical anchoring as the component associated with the largest reduction in discrimination when removed. Stability analysis showed a mean pairwise Jaccard similarity of 0.46 between selected feature sets and a mean Spearman correlation of 0.86 between molecular correction scores. These findings support the potential of clinically anchored, stability-constrained molecular learning to improve internal survival-risk prediction in LUAD. Independent-cohort validation is needed to establish generalizability.

papers.title: Sexual interactions and local selection shape reproductive gene diversity and divergence
papers.abstract: Genes involved in genotype x genotype coevolution display unique patterns of nucleotide diversity and population divergence. In Drosophila melanogaster, Sex Peptide is a key sperm competition gene that is an outlier for both pi within populations and Fst between populations. This pattern is not predicted by current theoretical expectations of selective sweeps highlighting the need to develop predictions to identify genes experiencing balancing selection. We compared pi and FST in D. melanogaster populations to identify other genes following a co-evolutionary model that generates divergence and diversity. Multiple male and female genes that interact with Sex Peptide exhibited elevated FST x pi values. Genome-wide analyses also revealed an enrichment of genes critical for neuronal development, pointing to courtship evolution. Specifically, fruitless, its interacting genes, and a female behavior gene were identified as outliers. These parallel findings indicate that both sperm competition and mating behaviors are subject to co-evolutionary selection.

papers.title: An open-access neuroimaging-compatible virtual town task for assessing human spatial navigation
papers.abstract: Spatial navigation is a cognitive skill that draws on multiple processes such as learning, decision-making and memory, which are often updated on a second-by-second timescale. However, many existing virtual paradigms designed to assay spatial navigation cannot target these processes as they unfold or are not designed for integration with concurrent neurophysiological recording. Here, we present and demonstrate our open-access task for neuroimaging: NAturalistic Virtual Assessment of Navigation (NAVAN) combining high-resolution behavioural tracking and integration with electroencephalography. We report data from this task, in which fifty-three participants completed a wayfinding navigation paradigm across twenty-four trials. Navigational efficiency improved significantly following repeated exposure to the environment, although efficiency declined across trials within each block. Self-reported spatial ability (assessed by the Santa Barbara Sense of Direction) predicted performance during early environmental exposure, suggesting concurrent validity. We demonstrated the feasibility of recording electroencephalography during the task, with in-game events streamed and aligned to the neural recording. The task provides researchers with access to detailed behavioural measures and can be adapted by modifying features such as trial number and difficulty. We also provide a step-by-step implementation guide to support reuse and customisation across experimental settings.

papers.title: Receptor-proximal phosphoform organization precedes β2 integrin activation
papers.abstract: Receptor signaling is often framed as protein recruitment after stimulation, but whether receptor-proximal environments are organized in composition and phosphorylation state beforehand remains unclear. We used CD18-APEX2 proximity labeling and a spatial membrane reference to quantify proteins and phosphosites near leukocyte {beta}2 integrins. At rest, receptors, adaptors and Rap GTPases were preferentially represented relative to several catalytic classes. Parent-protein correction revealed spatial phosphoform organization, with 32% of 4,564 phosphosites deviating significantly from the distribution center and 56% of proteins with multiple quantified sites showing divergence beyond measurement error. Sustained activation altered 31% of phosphosites while 95.9% of proteins remained equivalent within {+/-}0.5 log2 and spatial phosphoform organization largely persisted. Most phosphorylation responses were shared across both labeling environments, whereas receptor-preferential changes were dominated by phosphosites. These findings suggest that receptor signaling can regulate pre-existing molecular states without extensive protein redistribution.

papers.title: Feedback Valence, Prediction Error, and the Limits of Computational Attribution in Symptom-Related EEG
papers.abstract: Feedback-locked electroencephalography (EEG) responses are often interpreted using model-derived prediction errors (PEs), although signed PE can be strongly coupled to feedback valence in binary-outcome tasks. We revisited a published anxiety-related EEG association using two open probabilistic-learning datasets to examine measurement reliability, predictor separability, and participant-level recovery. In the primary dataset, greater trait anxiety was associated with a larger negative-minus-positive FCz theta response among 46 participants with elevated depressive symptoms after adjustment for depression severity. The association also differed between the sampled depression-symptom groups. The feedback contrast showed useful within-session reliability, but matched delta and P3-minus-N2 analyses did not establish theta specificity. Within participants, feedback valence and signed PE were highly correlated (r = -0.964). Exact-design simulations showed that population-level model discrimination could succeed despite poor recovery of individual neural slopes. Participant-specific learning-model refits recovered overall signed PE more consistently than the within-valence variation needed to distinguish it from feedback valence. An independent dataset reproduced the FCz feedback contrast in untreated and placebo cohorts but lacked trait-anxiety scores. Adding signed PE to valence yielded a small held-out predictive improvement under one reinforcement-learning specification, with limited support across sessions and no comparable support under the dual-rate model or in placebo. Together, these findings support a symptom-related feedback EEG association while constraining its theta-specific and participant-level computational interpretation.

papers.title: Functional Assessment and Extended Culture of Human Pediatric Cardiac Tissue Slices for Preclinical Testing
papers.abstract: Background: Living human myocardial slices preserve native tissue architecture, but their application to pediatric cardiac physiology or prolonged functional testing remains limited. We adapted a passive culture method for small surgical myocardial specimens obtained from patients with congenital heart disease (CHD). Methods: Atrial and ventricular specimens were obtained from 41 cardiac surgery patients (7.7{+/-}11.1 years; 1 day-49 years). Myocardial tissue was sectioned into slices and studied acutely, or maintained under free floating, rocking cell culture conditions without electrical or mechanical stimulation. Calcium transients were recorded in response to external pacing (0.2-2 Hz) at baseline, and after isoproterenol or norepinephrine exposure. Selected preparations underwent viability, histological, and gene expression analyses. Results: Pacing evoked calcium transients were recorded from all four cardiac chambers, exhibiting expected frequency-dependent shortening. Mean interslice and intraslice coefficients of variation were 11.1% and 7.6%. Viability was 85.8 {+/-} 5.6% post-slicing and 78.8 {+/-} 5.0% after 3-5 hours. Calcium transients remained detectable through 178 days in atrial and 119 days in ventricular slices. Calcium transient durations were relatively stable during extended culture. Beta-adrenergic agonists shortened calcium transient durations (isoproterenol: 32% atrial, 25% ventricular at 0.3 Hz); responses to isoproterenol persisted to approximately 120 days in selected atrial slices and 60 days in ventricular slices. Selected histological features were preserved, although some extracellular matrix and apoptosis related transcripts changed. Conclusions: Small surgical specimens support repeated physiological measurements and pharmacological testing during extended passive culture, providing a platform for human developmental and disease-specific cardiac research.

papers.title: A Urinary Metabolomic Signature Associated with Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth in Children with Short Bowel Syndrome
papers.abstract: Direct sampling of the small intestinal microbiome is challenging. Urinary metabolites may offer a noninvasive approach to studying microbial functional activity. We used clinically available gas chromatography/mass spectrometry to profile urinary organic acids in 94 children with short bowel syndrome, comparing those with clinically defined small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO; n=21) with those without SIBO (n=73). SIBO-associated metabolites included microbial fermentation products, dietary derivatives, and host metabolic intermediates. Metabolites enriched in SIBO mapped to aromatic amino acid metabolism, including tryptophan and tyrosine pathways, consistent with altered microbial fermentation. Many associations persisted after adjustment for intestinal anatomy, age, antibiotic exposure, and nutritional composition. These findings identified a urinary metabolic profile associated with clinically defined SIBO in children with short bowel syndrome and support further evaluation of urinary metabolomics as a noninvasive approach to studying small intestinal microbial function.

papers.title: Long-read shotgun metagenomics identifies distinct urogenital microbial community states associated with functional potential and urinary tract infection during pregnancy
papers.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are among the most common bacterial infections during pregnancy and are associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Although previous studies used enhanced culture, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and/or short-read shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize the urogenital microbiome of adult females, few have assessed the urogenital microbiome during pregnancy and thus this microbiome remains poorly understood. Here, we applied Oxford Nanopore long-read shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize urogenital microbial composition, functional potential, metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), and the urogenital virome of pregnant females. Taxonomic profiling identified three distinct microbial community states predominated by Lactobacillus crispatus, Gardnerella species, and L. iners. The Gardnerella-predominated community was associated with a higher frequency of UTI during pregnancy. Functional profiles strongly reflected these community states, demonstrating that taxonomic differences were accompanied by distinct functional potential. Genome-resolved analysis recovered 415 MAGs, including 29 high-quality genomes, revealing substantial genomic diversity among urogenital microbes. Viral sequences, predominantly bacteriophages, also were detected in most samples, highlighting an additional component of the pregnancy-associated urogenital microbiome. These findings demonstrate that pregnant females possess distinct urogenital microbial community states and show that they differ not only in taxonomic composition but also in their functional potential.

papers.title: Clonally Convergent Tph/Tfh-like CD4+ T Cells are Shared Across Recovery and Recurrence in Experimental Periodontitis
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease of the tooth-supporting structures (periodontium) that requires life-long maintenance to prevent progression. Using a sensitized model of recurrent periodontitis in mice (SeRPD), in which regulatory breakdown was induced by temporary Treg depletion concurrent with disease, we mapped the gingival T cell imprint across each disease phase. Transient regulatory breakdown left a durable mucosal imprint after clinical recovery, characterized by enrichment of local and regional CD4 T cells. Paired single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing of gingival immune cells identified a convergent clonotype expanded from recovery into recurrence that carried a Tfh/Tph-like transcriptional identity. An analogous CD4 T cell population was detected in human periodontitis lesions by single-cell transcriptomics. Together, these findings support a paradigm in which clinical recovery does not ensure a local T cell repertoire reset; instead, a reservoir of antigen-experienced, tissue-adapted CD4 T cells persist in the mucosa and participate in recurrence.

papers.title: European LD proxies lose tagging for 43% of GWAS leads in the African panel: a chromosome 22 analysis with SwiftLD, an 826-fold faster, byte-identical vcftools LD
papers.abstract: SwiftLD is a drop-in replacement for the pairwise linkage disequilibrium (LD) modes of vcftools 0.1.17, --hap-r2 and --geno-r2, which population-genetic pipelines use to compute r2, D and D' between nearby variants. On three regions of 1000 Genomes chromosome 22 with 503 to 2,504 samples it wrote the same output as vcftools, byte for byte, and was 826-fold faster (geometric mean at two threads on an AVX-512 CPU). It was also 7.6-fold faster than PLINK 2, the fastest alternative, from VCF input to LD output on all five regions tested; PLINK 2 writes a different file, although its r2 values agree with vcftools' within 10^-6. One megabase with 503 samples took vcftools 29 s and SwiftLD 0.049 s, and on an ordinary AVX2 laptop SwiftLD was 102-fold faster than vcftools at 12 threads. vcftools was slow because it repeatedly re-reads genotypes from a temporary file, counts haplotypes individually and flushes every output row. I built SwiftLD with correctness-gated coding agents (Claude Opus 5.5): every change had to keep the output byte-identical to vcftools. No output byte differed in 167,749 differential tests on three machines. On chromosome 22, the best European LD proxy of a GWAS lead kept r2 >= 0.8 for 57.4% of leads in the African panel and 85.6% to 92.7% in other panels (98.1% in a European split-half control). Code and a two-command reproduction: https://github.com/joe-b-christensen/swiftld.

papers.title: 40 Hz visual stimulation increases gamma-band functional connectivity between visual, parietal and frontal regions
papers.abstract: Visual stimulation at 40 Hz is being investigated as a non-invasive intervention for Alzheimer's disease. Its neural responses have been reported in regions beyond the visual cortex, and concurrent cognitive tasks have been shown to increase their spatial extent. However, it is unclear whether these responses reflect increased functional connectivity between regions or a common response to the stimulus, and whether a concurrent task changes this connectivity. We recorded EEG from 29 healthy young adults during Regular 40 Hz flicker and Irregular 30-50 Hz flicker, each with and without a target-counting task (2 x 2 within-participant design). Source-space connectivity between visual, parietal, and frontal regions was estimated with the debiased squared weighted phase-lag index (dWPLI). Regular stimulation increased 38-42 Hz connectivity for all three region pairs, with the largest increase between visual and parietal regions (increase in all 29 participants). The increase was specific to the stimulation frequency and was observed with two source reconstruction methods and in sensor space. The visual-parietal increase remained significant after correction for source leakage (spatial mixing between reconstructed sources) and after removal of the estimated stimulus-locked component, whereas the increases in visual-frontal and parietal-frontal connectivity did not. The concurrent task did not modulate the visual-parietal effect. For visual-frontal and parietal-frontal connectivity, the stimulation-by-ask interaction was not significant. These results show that 40 Hz visual stimulation increases gamma-band connectivity beyond the visual cortex, and much of this increase reflects a common stimulus-locked response, and connectivity beyond this response was observed mainly between visual and parietal regions.

papers.title: Light-dependent conversion of body color change pattern during zebrafish development
papers.abstract: Zebrafish (Danio rerio) shows body color change in response to light: when light comes, it whitens body color. Our previous study has shown that larval zebrafish as early as 5 days post-fertilization (dpf) have this capacity fully developed whereas 2-dpf larvae exhibit light-induced darkening in sharp contrast (Shiraki et al. 2010). Here, we discovered that the conversion in body color change pattern between 2 dpf and 5 dpf is light-dependent: larvae reared in darkness exhibited light-induced darkening of body color, reminiscent of 2-dpf larvae. We also found that a 14-h light exposure on 3 or 4 dpf is sufficient to trigger this conversion, and that the conversion by light on 4 dpf still occurred after ablation of most exorh-expressing pineal photoreceptor cells. The dark-reared larvae had significantly lower transcription levels of pmch and pmchl, which encode melanin-concentrating hormone precursors, than the LD-reared larvae. However, the levels in larvae that had undergone the conversion (3-L and 4-L) were not significantly different from those in dark-reared larvae, indicating that the reduced pmch/pmchl expression alone does not account for the conversion. In conclusion, light exposure in rearing is indispensable for the maturation of body color change ability in larval zebrafish through a regulatory mechanism independent of exorh-expressing pineal photoreceptors.

papers.title: Human lymphatic organoids reconstruct convergent developmental routes to functional lymphatic vessels
papers.abstract: The lymphatic vasculature maintains fluid balance, regulates immune surveillance, and supports tissue repair, yet how human lymphatic vessels arise and acquire specialized functions remains poorly understood. Here, guided by single-cell and spatial analyses of human embryos, we found that both lateral plate and paraxial mesoderm converge on venous endothelial intermediates with cardinal vein-like characteristics prior to lymphatic specification. Informed by these developmental trajectories, we generated three-dimensional lymphatic organoids from human pluripotent stem cells through two distinct mesodermal routes. The organoids formed capillary-like vascular networks with emerging button-like junctions and distinct endothelial and stromal programs. The lymphatic organoids were transcriptionally benchmarked to human fetal lymphatic endothelium. The organoids supported immune-cell interactions and antigen accumulation and, following transplantation, exhibited interstitial tracer uptake and transport. These findings establish a platform for investigating how distinct developmental origins shape human lymphatic specification, vascular organization, and function, with applications to lymphatic disease modeling and tissue repair.

papers.title: Optimal compositions of potent sliced-siRNA with DNA bases substitution and insights of Ago2 slicing actions
papers.abstract: We have previously characterized the nucleotide compositions of single-stranded ago2-sliced small interfering RNAs (sliced-siRNA, sliRNA), a novel type of potent RNAi trigger designed based on the biogenesis mechanism of miRNA-451. sliRNAs have on par antisense mediated silencing activity but about 1000-fold reduced passenger strand activity compared to siRNA. In the current study, to further characterize sliRNAs to facilitate their in vivo application, we have investigated the effects of substituting RNA nucleotides (nts) in sliRNA with DNA nts (sliDRNAs), which will allow us to study the potential effects on their processing, maturation, and silencing activity from individual or multiple nts at different positions. Our results showed sliDRNAs have distinguished composition from siRNA with DNA nts (siDRNA), indicated that, in addition to their different biogenesis mechanisms, these two types of RNAi triggers may also have adopted additional different silencing mechanisms. Our results also revealed some mechanism related to how Ago2 executes its slicer activity and the effects on sliRNA potency by trimming and tailing during sliRNA maturation. These results have paved the way for using other chemically modified nts in sliRNAs that may enhance their in vivo stability and transportability to facilitate their in vivo applications.

papers.title: The Test Used to Choose Between Pesticide Survival Models Tracks Lesion Persistence, Not Hazard Structure
papers.abstract: Aquatic pesticide risk assessment predicts survival with toxicokinetic-toxicodynamic models that offer two hazard structures, cumulative or peak-based, which disagree about which exposure patterns are dangerous; for imidacloprid, published choices differ across eight species. The choice is made from one observation: deaths after transfer to clean water are taken to refute the peak-based structure. That inference holds only if damage is falling, which is not measured in these tests but taken from a fitted model. The observation responds to the compound and design, not the hazard structure. Across thirty-two Gammarus pulex treatments the post-exposure death rate places anticholinesterases above uncouplers, in the order of lesion persistence. For diazinon, one series returns opposite verdicts over its sixteen-day window and its first four days. For imidacloprid in Daphnia magna, one damage stage favours the cumulative structure by 78 likelihood units and two stages the peak-based one by 7. Four conditions make a design informative; thirteen of thirty-six treatments in a thirteen-compound archive meet them. Spreading a fixed exposure over longer intervals raises mortality in one of five species, which no repair law reproduces with the kinetics of the models. For neonicotinoids, predictions for such patterns are unvalidated, not conservative.

papers.title: Variation in the embryonic cell lineages of Caenorhabditis elegans natural populations
papers.abstract: Developmental variation has often been appreciated as a major phenotypic substrate of evolutionary innovation in multicellular organisms. Although quantification of developmental variation in isogenic populations has a long history, it has been difficult to accomplish across natural populations until recently. Given its invariant cell lineage, Caenorhabditis elegans represents an ideal model system for studying how natural diversity in development is expressed at the resolution of single cells, cell lineages, and the whole embryo. Using embGAN, a deep-learning pipeline that enables label-free lineage tracing without the bottleneck and potential confounding effects of generating transgenic strains, we reconstructed the early embryonic lineage of 78 embryos spanning eight genetic backgrounds, including six wild strains, and quantified cell-cycle timing with a lineage-aligned graph metric that separates global rescaling of developmental rate from localized changes in lineage structure. We found that cell-cycle timing differs reproducibly among genotypes, with between-strain variation consistently exceeding within-strain variation. The magnitude of this variation was itself genotype-specific and not correlated with levels of genetic divergence. Unlike the global shifts in the tempo of development that dominate divergence between species, these differences are predominantly in lineage patterning, changing the timing of specific divisions, and they align to cell fate. Thus, the invariant lineage of C. elegans is built on a structured, genotype-specific landscape of developmental variation, a potential source of trait variation from which drift in developmental systems can emerge.

papers.title: Ferroptosis of selective progenitor cell types during embryogenesis ensures proper organ morphogenesis
papers.abstract: Ferroptosis, a form of non-apoptotic cell death, is induced by lipid peroxidation resulting from an intracellular accumulation of labile iron (1). While apoptosis is involved in embryonic development (2), the role of ferroptosis in embryogenesis is unknown. Here, we report that the ferroptosis process occurs in the embryonic lung and kidney at mid- and late-gestation. In these tissues, pro-ferroptotic cells include subpopulations of the Sox9+ distal lung epithelial cells and the Flk1+ vascular progenitors in the kidney glomeruli. Lipidomic analysis reveals mixed lipid peroxidation as the driver for ferroptosis. The role of ferroptosis in the morphogenesis of these organs was confirmed by triple positivity of TfR1, 4-HNE and TUNEL, mitochondrial defects, cell membrane breakage, dead cell remnants, single-cell RNA-sequencing of a ferroptosis gene signature. Genetic manipulation of Gpx4, an endogenous inhibitor of ferroptosis. Further, genetic knockout or transgenic overexpression of Gpx4 affects lung and kidney development and results in cystic lungs and kidneys. Notably, conditional deletion Gpx4 results in hypoplasia of the lung epithelia and of the renal glomeruli, while transgenic overexpression of Gpx4 resulted in atelectasis with collapsed lung alveoli and hypertrophic glomeruli. Together, these findings show that ferroptosis regulates lung and kidney morphogenesis by acting in key progenitor cell populations during gestation. Supplementation of iron or polyunsaturated fatty acid during pregnancy has implications for organogenesis.

papers.title: Human-caused ignitions and plant invasion drive fire-regime change in a dryland biodiversity hotspot
papers.abstract: Dryland ecosystems cover much of Earths terrestrial surface and are increasingly affected by climate warming, land-use change, and biological invasion. The Sonoran Desert of western North America, a biodiversity hotspot that historically experienced infrequent fire, exemplifies how these global-change processes are driving ecosystem transformation through the emergence of novel disturbance regimes. Using records of more than 73,000 wildland fire events, we quantified anthropogenic and environmental controls on fire ignition, size, and spread across the Sonoran Desert. Human-caused ignitions accounted for 95.5% of all recorded fires since the early 1990s and were concentrated near roads, buildings, and other areas of human activity, particularly during late spring. In contrast, lightning-caused ignitions were rare within the Sonoran Desert and occurred primarily in adjacent montane forests during late summer months. Consistent with broader trends across the western United States, fires were typically largest when they ignited far from roads, where access is limited, and fire management often relies on indirect attack strategies. Pre-fire annual and perennial herbaceous vegetation both promoted fire spread, with detectable effects at cover values as low as 5%, while bare ground reduced fuel connectivity and constrained fire growth. Rather than exhibiting a distinct threshold response, fire spread increased linearly with herbaceous cover, suggesting that even modest increases in fine fuels can alter fire behavior in this historically fuel-limited ecosystem. Together, our results illustrate that human ignitions determine where fires occur, whereas herbaceous fuels determine whether those ignitions spread, driving fire-regime transformation across an iconic North American desert. Managing and adapting to this novel fire regime will require coordinated efforts to reduce human-caused ignitions, limit invasive herbaceous fuels, maintain bare-ground interspaces, and rapidly suppress fires. More broadly, our findings identify the mechanisms controlling fire regime change in dryland ecosystems and provide a framework for anticipating ecosystem transformation under ongoing global change.

papers.title: BCL10 Gain-of-Function Impairs Germinal Center Participation by Naive B Cells and Cooperates with BCL6 to Drive Extrafollicular Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
papers.abstract: BCL10 gain-of-function (GoF) mutations occur in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) cases of the BN2/C1 molecular subgroup. These alterations activate CARD11-BCL10-MALT1 (CBM) signaling and drive resistance to multiple drug classes, but their role in disease pathogenesis is incompletely understood. In particular, interactions between BCL10 GoF and additional DLBCL oncogenes are undefined. Here, we show BCL10 GoF in naive B cells blocks their participation in germinal center (GC) reactions and permits transformation to DLBCL with a non-GC B-cell phenotype. Most clinical cases with BCL10 GoF also carry translocation of the BCL6 proto-oncogene, and we show that co-activation of these two lesions together promotes pronounced oncogenic synergy. Detailed single-cell analyses of underlying premalignant B-cell populations revealed expansion of extrafollicular memory B cells whose gene-expression program remains prominent in resulting lymphomas in both the mouse and corresponding human tumors. We therefore define a novel role for BCL10 activating mutations in enabling BCL6 lymphomagenesis.

papers.title: Compartment-Resolved Matrisome Shifts During Postnatal Tendon Maturation in Mice
papers.abstract: Tendons acquire their load-bearing capacity during the first month of postnatal growth, driven by the extensive remodeling of the extracellular matrix (ECM). While the role of specific individual components to this process have been well characterized, a comprehensive assessment of how the tendon matrisome changes during this critical window is lacking. This, in part, is due to the challenges associated with solubilization of mature ECM, which is underrepresented by conventical proteomic approaches. To address this, we performed compartment-resolved proteomics on murine Achilles and plantaris tendons at postnatal days 0 (P0), P14, and P28. Sequential extraction methods leveraged a CHAPS-soluble fraction, capturing cellular and soluble matrisome proteins, from the insoluble mature ECM fraction, solubilized by guanidine hydrochloride and hydroxylamine hydrochloride and separately analyzed by label-free quantitative LC-MS/MS. Analysis shows that the two compartments followed distinct trajectories during maturation. The insoluble matrix was dominated by collagenous proteins, which increased from 95% to over 99% of the identified signal intensity, and its composition was largely established by P14. Within the soluble matrisome compartment, collagens increased from 50% to over 60% by P14, accompanied by dynamic regulation of proteins implicated in collagen processing (P4HA1, PCOLCE), crosslinking (LOX, LOXL2), and regulators of collagen fibril assembly and growth (DCN, BGN, FMOD, THBS3, THBS4). Beyond these established regulators, we observed dynamic regulation of less-characterized fibril-associated proteoglycans (KERA, OGN, CHAD), matricellular (COMP, POSTN, MATN2), and angiogenic regulatorily proteins (SERPINF1, ECM1). Together, this work establishes a comprehensive protein-level reference for postnatal tendon maturating, provides new insights into the molecular regulation of functional tendon development.

papers.title: Jade1S SUMOylates tau and targets oligomers for degradation
papers.abstract: The accumulation of insoluble tau aggregates is a pathological hallmark of tauopathies, including Alzheimer's disease. While molecular chaperones and clearance pathways regulate tau homeostasis, the mechanisms governing tau oligomerization and degradation remain incompletely defined. Recent genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have linked the JADE1 locus to tauopathy, and the PHD zinc finger protein Jade1S has been identified in complexes with tau in post-mortem brain tissue, prompting investigation into their biochemical relationship. Here, we characterize the reciprocal interactions between Jade1S and 0N4R tau stability and turnover. Covalent labeling mass spectrometry and co-immunoprecipitation mappings reveal that Jade1S binds wild-type 0N4R tau through redundant sites within its N-terminal and plant homeodomain (PHD) zinc finger domains. In vitro assays demonstrate that Jade1S functions as a SUMO E3 ligase, utilizing its PHD domains to mediate tau SUMOylation. Cell-based cycloheximide chase assays reveal a reciprocal stabilization dynamic: tau co-expression extends the overall physiological half-life of Jade1S from less than an hour to ~17 hours, arresting its turnover specifically within sarkosyl-insoluble fractions. Conversely, Jade1S selectively accelerates the degradation of sarkosyl-insoluble tau without altering the turnover of the soluble monomeric pool over chased time. Mechanistically, Jade1S redirects the clearance of SUMO2/3-modified tau oligomers away from basal autophagic-lysosomal pathways and toward proteasome-dependent degradation. Furthermore, Jade1S exhibits intrinsic molecular chaperone activity, inhibiting arachidonic acid-induced tau oligomerization in vitro. Together, these data characterize Jade1S as a dual-function SUMO ligase and chaperone that regulates tau stability, prevents oligomer assembly, and promotes the targeted proteasomal clearance of aggregated tau.

papers.title: Gene regulatory architecture in antibiotic resistance is optimized for specific dynamic regimens
papers.abstract: Cellular responses to antibiotics face a fundamental trade-off: resistance must be deployed quickly enough to prevent the accumulation of drug inside the cell, but expression of resistance genes is costly in the absence of the drug. Therefore, antibiotic responses are typically regulated, controlling not only whether resistance is expressed, but also when, how strongly, and for how long. These regulatory strategies are implemented through the strength and arrangement of promoters and operators. However, it is still not clear how the dynamics of drug exposure select for specific regulatory strategies. Here, we develop a dynamical model of a typical antibiotic response, where a transcriptional repressor senses the drug and regulates expression of a resistance protein, coupled to the effects of the drug on cell growth and gene expression. We define a cost function that weighs the different burdens imposed on the cell over the course of the response, and perform in silico optimization of the regulatory parameters under different selective pressures for three architectures of increasing complexity: constitutive expression of resistance, repression by a constitutively expressed repressor, and repression by a self-regulated repressor. We find that strong drug exposures favor constitutive expression of resistance, high costs of basal expression favor repression by a constitutive repressor, and self-regulation of the repressor is favored only when the response must provide protection while also restraining overexpression of resistance. Stochastic simulations further show that self-regulation of the repressor protects cells against fluctuations in repressor levels, which cause unnecessary induction of resistance before exposure and failed induction after exposure. This framework links the dynamics of the environment to the evolution of gene regulation, providing a basis to predict which regulatory strategies are expected to arise under specific selective pressures.

papers.title: Genomic prediction of resistance to Phytophthora megakarya in cacao from a sparse host-pathogen screen
papers.abstract: Black pod rot caused by Phytophthora megakarya is a major disease impacting cacao (Theobroma cacao L.) production in West Africa. Resistance is influenced by genetic variation in both host and pathogen populations. While genomic prediction approaches have been widely applied in plant breeding, most studies incorporate only host genomic information. The value of explicitly modeling pathogen genomic relatedness in quantitative disease prediction remains largely unknown. We genotyped 947 clones from the International Cacao Collection at CATIE using a 10K-SNP panel and characterized 67 P. megakarya isolates by sequencing 3,505 virulence-associated genes and 2,774 SNP loci. Cacao clones were extensively admixed, while isolates formed three geographically structured subpopulations. Mixed linear models were fitted to lesion diameters on detached pods of 350 genotyped clones inoculated with 58 isolates in 30 bioassays, covering 5% of possible clone-by-isolate combinations. Differences among isolates explained a larger share of lesion-size variation than differences among clones (0.34 and 0.27 of phenotypic variance, respectively). After accounting for broad pathogen subpopulation structure, incorporating within-subpopulation genomic relatedness among isolates improved neither model fit nor prediction, whereas incorporating genomic relationships among cacao clones improved model fit and enabled prediction of phenotypically untested clones with a predictive ability of 0.41. Clone rankings were stable across pathogen subpopulations (genomic correlation 0.86 {+/-} 0.06), whereas clone-by-isolate interactions accounted for little phenotypic variation and were not resolved with confidence in the sparse design. An exploratory ancestry analysis associated several Upper Amazon ancestry components with smaller predicted lesions. These are the first genomic predictions of resistance to P. megakarya in cacao. In this strongly structured host-pathogen system, genomic relationships among hosts carried most of the predictable signal beyond broad pathogen subpopulation effects, and the predictions provide a starting point for prioritizing screening and selection efforts.

papers.title: A protein language model for domain, functional site, and variant effect prediction
papers.abstract: Protein sequence databases are growing far faster than experimentally curated annotations, limiting functional interpretation of newly identified proteins and coding variants. We developed PALM, a protein annotation language model that jointly predicts domain and functional-site occurrence, while preserving overlapping and nested annotations through a soft-target objective. PALM integrates ESM2 with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), learned layer aggregation, and a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) encoder. PALM was trained on ~15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences spanning 17,951 domain and 1,383 site classes. Across 2.3 million held-out proteins, PALM achieved domain- and site-occurrence F1 scores of 0.941 and 0.877, respectively, and retained substantial performance in proteins with <20% sequence identity to the training and validation data. PALM also substantially outperformed ESM3 annotation baseline. Without training on variant-pathogenicity labels, PALM embedding disruption distinguished 151,823 ClinVar missense variants more accurately than ESM2 embedding disruption (AUROC 0.835 versus 0.710), and combining PALM embedding disruption with the ESM2 likelihood-ratio signal reached an AUROC of 0.877. The same combined zero-shot score outperformed AlphaMissense on a benchmark dataset on 128,161 missense variants, that were derived from literature but not present in ClinVar database. At the protein level, PALM embeddings showed stronger CATH-Gene3D superfamily organization than frozen ESM2 and ESM3 embeddings, and improved prediction of experimental activation and repression effects when combined with ESM2. In a downstream case study, we demonstrated the ability to use PALM-derived embedding as proxy of deep mutational scanning (DMS), showcasing the broad application of PALM. Together, PALM converts curated residue-level knowledge into transferable and mechanistically interpretable representations that connect protein sequence, function, and variant consequence.

papers.title: RNA-triggered Cas12a2 antibacterial activity and resistance plasmid degradation
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) necessitates programmable antibacterial strategies with novel mechanisms. Here, we evaluated an inducible intracellular CRISPR/Cas12a2 system in engineered Escherichia coli targeting a chloramphenicol-resistance (Chl) transcript. Cas12a2 activation significantly delayed bacterial growth and reduced recoverable colony-forming units (CFU) by 3-log10 in vitro, and reduced bacterial burdens in a mouse skin wound model. Transcriptomic profiling revealed upregulation of recA, a key mediator of the SOS response. We therefore designed a Chl-recA dual-targeting construct, which produced a greater growth delay than either single-targeting counterpart. The optimized dual-targeting system led to an approximately 4-log10 reduction in bacterial burden in vivo. Furthermore, exploratory qPCR of culture supernatants suggested a treatment-associated decrease in amplifiable plasmid DNA. Overall, this study provides proof-of-concept for resistance-transcript-guided Cas12a2 antibacterial activity and highlights the potential of co-targeting stress-associated transcripts to enhance programmable antimicrobials.

papers.title: Reconstruction of Cellular Trajectories with Biologically Interpretable States
papers.abstract: Elucidating the trajectories of cellular evolution provides biologists with deeper insights into biological systems and disease progression, ultimately facilitating more informed discovery of mechanisms and therapeutic design. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is widely used to study cellular evolution. However, it faces two primary limitations. First, because the process destroys cells during gene-expression measurement, it is impossible to track the gene-expression profile of the same cell throughout the entire trajectory. Second, because scRNA-seq captures cells at discrete time points, it provides only static snapshots rather than continuous trajectories, limiting its ability to resolve the full dynamics of cellular transitions. Consequently, various computational approaches have been developed to address these challenges. However, existing models fail to capture the hidden state of each cell, which is essential for reconstructing gene expression at unobserved time points. As the gene expression profiles depend on the cell state, and may vary according to time, we propose a Latent Cell-State Model, where we approximate cell state transition as a Markov chain and obtain the gene expression of each cell at unobserved timepoints depending on the cell state, time, and a latent variable that represents the high-dimensional gene expression profile of a cell. Our model is able to infer biologically meaningful cell states and generate high-quality gene expression profiles at unobserved timepoints, showing potential for accurate trajectory reconstruction.

papers.title: FoldAbS: Repurposing the Protein Folding Model as a Foundation Encoder for Antibody Screening
papers.abstract: Therapeutic antibody screening requires prioritizing antibody candidates across specificity, affinity, and developability. Current pipelines typically silo these objectives and underuse structural information that governs antibody-antigen recognition. To address these inefficacies, we introduce FoldAbS, a unified supervised screening framework that reconceptualizes protein folding models as frozen foundation encoders, exploiting their internal representations to capture rich sequence, geometric, and interaction dynamics well beyond basic structure prediction. By coupling the folding model with lightweight, task-specific heads, FoldAbS seamlessly evaluates all three therapeutic criteria within a single architecture. Instantiating this framework with the open-source Protenix model (FoldAbS-Px) yields consistent improvements over baseline approaches, achieving significant performance gains of up to 13.1%, 9.2%, and 6.2% in specificity, affinity, and developability, respectively. Collectively, these results reposition protein folding models from structure predictors and confidence scorers into reusable foundation encoders for comprehensive and supervised antibody screening. Our code is available at https://github.com/nohandsomewujun/FoldAbS.

papers.title: Phenotypic and Molecular Characterization of Potentially New Shigella boydii Serotype in Bangladesh
papers.abstract: Objective: Shigella is a major cause of bacillary dysentery among children under 5 years of age, especially in low- and middle-income countries. At Dhaka hospital of icddr,b, every year around 3% of Shigella isolates from patients with diarrhea are identified as Shigella-like organisms (SLOs). These isolates do not react with any of the existing and provisional Shigella antisera. The major aims of the present study were to characterize a unique cluster of SLOs using phenotypic and genotypic methods. Methods: A cluster of 6 SLOs was characterized using biochemical tests, serotyping, antimicrobial susceptibility, and virulence assay by using the Sereny test, PCR and compared their pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) patterns with known serotypes of Shigella spp. Antisera against the isolate were raised in a rabbit model to determine cross-reactivity with known serotypes. Results: All six SLOs were mannitol fermenting, have invasive properties, positive for ipaH and Shigella enterotoxin 2 gene along with possession of virulence plasmid of ~ 140 MDa. All isolates were resistant to ampicillin, tetracycline, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, but were sensitive to mecillinam, nalidixic acid, and ciprofloxacin. Plasmid and PFGE profiles showed that the genomic patterns of these isolates were identical but were different from all other S. boydii serotypes. Antiserum prepared against one of the isolates agglutinated with all isolates but did not cross-react with other Shigella and E. coli reference strains. Conclusion: This unique cluster of isolates might belong to a new provisional serovar of S. boydii and further analysis is required to incorporate it into the stereotypic scheme of Shigella.

papers.title: PartiDesign: A structure-sequence co-design paradigm for practical all-to-all biomolecules design
papers.abstract: Engineering interactions among biomolecules offers a route to creating new biological functions. Although unified models have advanced biomolecular structure prediction and design, efficient and controllable generation across molecular modalities remains challenging. A key challenge is to couple three-dimensional structure generation with sequence or chemical-identity design across chemically diverse systems. Here, we introduce PartiDesign, a unified structure-sequence co-design model that extends the partially latent framework of La-Proteina to proteins, nucleic acids and small molecules. PartiDesign jointly generates molecular structures and their corresponding sequences or chemical identities, while providing fine-grained control over secondary structure, chemical bonding and amino acid preferences. Across diverse benchmarks for the de novo design of proteins, nucleic acids and small molecules against specified targets, PartiDesign achieved the highest estimated successful-design throughput among the evaluated methods on most benchmarks under the adopted compute-budget protocols. Its configurable constraints further support cyclic peptide and antibody design, allowing generation to be tailored to specific structural and chemical requirements. PartiDesign was developed using 128 Huawei Ascend 910B accelerators, each with 64 GB of memory. The source code is available at https://github.com/MegaGatlingPea/PartiDesign-official, and a freely accessible web server at https://cadd.zju.edu.cn/partidesign/ enables users to generate binding partners without programming expertise. Together, these capabilities provide a versatile and accessible framework for all-to-all biomolecular design, with applications in molecular engineering and drug discovery.

papers.title: 1D model simulations suggest biofilms can suppress cathodic H2 bubble formation
papers.abstract: Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) electrochemically generates H2 for the reduction of CO2 into acetate by acetogens. So far, the importance of a biofilm on the cathode of such systems remains under debate. Here, we investigated the role of cathodic biofilms through computational modelling. We developed MES-BIOFILM, a comprehensive one-dimensional model to simulate steady-state H2 and CO2 concentration gradients within cathodic biofilms, while accounting for the limited solubility of H2. The effects of key biofilm properties, including thickness, cell density and H2 consumption rate were analysed. Overall, our simulations indicate that cathodic biofilms play an important role in (1) minimizing H2 loss from the system through H2 consumption within the biofilm; and (2) suppressing H2 bubble formation by maintaining the H2 concentrations at the cathode surface below saturation. Our model predicts that the current density at which H2 bubbles begin to form can be increased by 5.5-fold relative to a bare electrode when biofilms exhibit a high cell density and high H2 consumption rate. This effect requires biofilms of at least 50 m thickness, whereas CO2 diffusion limitations arise above 200 m. These findings highlight the critical role of biofilms to increase MES performance, while requiring further experimental validation.

papers.title: A Binuclear Cluster Supports Functional Asymmetry in Dark-Operative Protochlorophyllide Reductase
papers.abstract: Many photosynthetic bacteria rely on the nitrogenase-like dark-operative protochlorophyllide oxidoreductase (DPOR) to sustain (bacterio)chlorophyll synthesis in the dark. DPOR couples ATP hydrolysis to electron transfer from a reducing component (L-protein) to a catalytic component (NB-protein) that reduces protochlorophyllide. NB-protein is an 2{beta}2 heterotetramer, and each heterodimeric half contains an active site and a [Fe4S4] cluster. Although the two halves are identical, they react sequentially rather than in parallel. How the two halves communicate has remained unknown. Here we show, using Cu K-edge x-ray absorption spectroscopy and cryo-EM, that the NB-protein tetramer interface holds a binuclear, sulfur-bridged [Cu2S2] cluster. Each Cu is reduced and three-coordinate, with short Cu-S and Cu-Cu distances (2.26 and 2.62 &Aring). Mutagenesis excludes the nearest cysteine as the bridging ligand, supporting inorganic sulfide as the most likely sulfur donor. To our knowledge, this is the first sulfide-bridged dicopper cluster identified in a protein. The cluster is conserved in three purple non-sulfur bacteria and connects the BchB C-terminal helices that contact opposing active sites. Loss of Cu abolishes DPOR activity and asymmetric L-protein binding without disturbing overall fold. We propose that the cluster relays substrate-binding information between active sites, suggesting a metal-mediated mechanism for cooperativity in nitrogenase-like enzymes.

papers.title: Structural basis for inefficient G protein coupling by Frizzled receptors
papers.abstract: Frizzleds (FZDs) are class F G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) that primarily signal through Dishevelled (DVL) to initiate Wnt signalling, with evidence for context-specific coupling to heterotrimeric G proteins. Every FZD-G protein structure to date has been determined without an agonist, implying that agonist binding is not required for stable complex formation in vitro and directly contradicting the difficulty of demonstrating G protein coupling in cells. All these structures contain unassigned density between the receptor and the heterotrimeric G protein. From structures generated by single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) of FZD7-Gs and FZD5-Gq, we identify this density as the detergent lauryl maltose neopentyl glycol (LMNG), which bridges the receptor and G protein to stabilise a weak, shallow interface. Absence of LMNG - in biochemical preparations and molecular dynamics simulations - destabilises the complex, showing that constitutive FZD-G protein engagement is intrinsically weak. The weak G protein coupling is governed by a conserved intracellular interface that when mutated differentially influences DVL and G protein signalling. Our findings show that LMNG has masked the instability of purified FZD-G protein complexes and provide the structural basis of FZDs as inherently weak G protein activators that are predisposed to DVL signalling.

papers.title: Genome evolution and glycosyltransferase diversification shape asperosaponin biosynthesis in Dipsacus asperoides
papers.abstract: Deciphering the genomic and enzymatic features associated with high-abundance specialized metabolism is important for understanding and engineering bioactive natural product biosynthesis. Asperosaponin , a hederagenin-based saponin, accumulates at exceptionally high levels in Dipsacus asperoides roots and is by far the predominant triterpenoid saponin. Here, by integrating a chromosome-level genome assembly with comparative genomics, transcriptomics, metabolite profiling, and biochemical characterization, we reconstructed a major biosynthetic route to asperosaponin and identified diversification of triterpenoid-associated gene families. Functional analyses revealed an ordered glycosylation sequence in which DaUGT73GZ2 preferentially accepts C-3-glycosylated substrates retaining a free C-28 carboxyl group, thereby establishing a C-3-before-C-28 glycosylation order during asperosaponin biosynthesis. Phylogenetic and biochemical analyses further uncovered functional differentiation among UGT85CA enzymes involved in C-3 arabinosylation, while genomic and expression analyses revealed lineage-specific patterns of pathway gene duplication and transcriptional regulation. Together, these findings identify genomic, enzymatic, and transcriptional features associated with the distinctive, high-abundance triterpenoid saponin profile of D. asperoides roots and provide a framework for understanding and engineering triterpenoid saponin biosynthesis.

papers.title: Platycodin D2 Targets Vimentin to Suppress Fibroblast-Myofibroblast Transition: A Novel Therapeutic Strategy Against Pulmonary Fibrosis
papers.abstract: Background Pulmonary fibrosis is a progressive lung disease characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition and irreversible decline in lung function with limited effective therapeutic targets. Vimentin, a type III intermediate filament protein, plays a critical role in fibroblast activation and fibrogenesis, representing a promising drug target. Methods Novel vimentin ligands were screened via virtual screening. SPR assay verified compound-vimentin binding affinity. CETSA and CD spectroscopy analyzed protein structural changes after compound binding. In vitro FMT model and in vivo bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis model were used to assess antifibrotic effects, and mutagenesis assays identified key binding amino acid residues. Results Platycodin D2 (PD2) from Platycodon grandiflorus was identified as a novel high-affinity vimentin ligand (Kd = 392.8 nM). PD2 binds vimentin directly, alters its secondary structure and induces insoluble aggregation. It effectively inhibits TGF-{beta}1-induced FMT in vitro and mitigates bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis in vivo, reducing collagen deposition and improving animal survival. Critically, mutagenesis validation confirmed that key residues (Glu138 in chain A, Glu132 and Glu143 in chain B, as well as Glu50 and Arg54 in chain C) are essential for this interaction. Conclusions Our findings establish PD2 as a novel pharmacological inducer of aberrant vimentin aggregation, presenting a distinct target-driven strategy for antifibrotic drug development.

papers.title: Physiological mapping and prediction reveal stress-responsive translation initiation landscapes
papers.abstract: Translation initiation defines the protein output of the transcriptome, but its physiological dynamics in cells and tissues remain incompletely characterized. Here we develop TISCA2, an inhibitor-free method that captures eIF5B-associated initiating ribosomes to map translation initiation sites genome-wide. By directly identifying start sites rather than inferring translation from elongating-ribosome periodicity, TISCA2 improves the detection of short and overlapping translons. Translation of a subset of TISCA2-identified translons is supported by N-terminal proteomics and HLA-I immunopeptidomics. The arsenite-induced integrated stress response broadly redistributes start-site usage, reducing upstream initiation in favor of downstream initiation. TISCA2 further reveals tissue-specific initiation landscapes in vivo, with increased detection of downstream candidate start sites in the testis. Finally, we develop IncepTIS, a sequence-based deep learning model that predicts position-resolved and condition-dependent initiation landscapes. IncepTIS-guided optimization generates de novo mRNA 5' leaders with stress-responsive initiation patterns. Together, TISCA2 and IncepTIS provide an experimental and computational framework for mapping, predicting and engineering translation initiation in mammalian cells and tissues.

papers.title: Salinity adaptation in date palm (Phoenix dactylifera): evidence for selective sweeps at Salt Overly Sensitive (SOS) genes
papers.abstract: The date palm is a high salinity tolerant fruit tree grown mainly in the region spanning from North Africa to parts of South Asia. Climate change models of this region indicate the possibility of increasing salinity in the future. The Salt Overly Sensitive (SOS) pathway is crucial for salinity tolerance in plants, serving as a primary defense mechanism by facilitating sodium exclusion. To better understand date palms' salt tolerance, we analyzed variation in SOS pathway genes in a set of 197 date palm genomes collected from across the range of cultivation. Here, we show evidence for selective sweeps in multiple SOS pathway genes. A single major pdSOS1 haplotype is at very high frequency in Eastern and Western subpopulations, with a minor, likely ancestral haplotype still present in both geographical locations. Allele-specific gene expression analysis showed differences in salt-treated roots between swept and ancestral haplotypes. Interestingly, sequence-based analysis of the pdSOS1 haplotype suggested a second, much earlier introgression event between P. theophrasti and date palm, though direction is unclear. This event happened before both the selective sweep and the previously reported recent introgression to date palm. We identified a MITE transposable element inserted into a pdSOS1 intron on the swept haplotype, and a similar insertion was found in an intron of the SOS2 paralog pdCIPK8. Both insertions are unique to date palm among Phoenix species. The pdCIPK8 haplotype containing the MITE is also at high frequency in both populations. Further analysis showed evidence for a selective sweep spanning the pdSOS3 region in the western population that shares similarity to an Eastern haplotype spanning the promoter region only. Slower extended haplotype homozygosity decay surrounding the genes in the western population suggests that the swept haplotype originated in the East and spread to the West in all cases. Altogether, our data provide evidence of selective sweeps in the date palm SOS pathway and may go to explaining how this species has developed such high salinity tolerance.

papers.title: A timeline for evolution of metabolism in early microbes
papers.abstract: The metabolism of early microbes shaped our planet's chemistry and enabled more life to evolve. However, it remains uncertain when many forms of metabolism arose and which organisms carried them out. Here we combine machine learning, metabolic networks, and phylogenomics of microbes to date 14 forms of metabolism and 6 other traits. We find that metabolism evolved in three waves, starting >3.4 billion years ago (Ga) with fermentation and sulfur compound respiration. A second wave began ~3.2 Ga with aerobic respiration and growth, while a third began ~1.4 Ga with further specialization. We compared these predictions with independent dates from the geochemical record, and agreement with conservative dates was good (CCC = 0.81 to 0.89). Several forms of metabolism are invisible in the geochemical record, and our approach dates these forms, too. Our results reconcile different lines of evidence for microbial evolution and provide a fuller picture of early Earth.

papers.title: OncoSpot enables benchmarking of cancer spatial transcriptomics methods across tumor evolutionary modes
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) is increasingly used to map clonal architecture within tumors, yet methods for analyzing cancer ST data are difficult to evaluate because real tumors lack ground truth for copy-number alterations (CNAs), subclonal identity, and malignant cell fraction. Existing ST simulators model normal tissue and do not represent tumor evolution, CNA-driven expression, or the spatial organization of malignant subclones. We present OncoSpot, a cancer-aware simulator of Visium-like spot-based ST data. OncoSpot combines a spatial evolutionary scaffold from DEMON, CNAs generated along the resulting clonal phylogeny with CNAsim, cancer-type-specific malignant transcriptional programs, and spatially clustered nonmalignant cell types, and aggregates cells into spots with known malignant fraction, subclone, and copy-number profiles. We demonstrate OncoSpot on high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, colorectal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma, which represent three distinct modes of tumor evolution. Simulated subclones were spatially clustered and showed stronger phylogeny-space concordance than those generated by scCube under matched subclone populations. Benchmarking CopyKAT, CancerFinder, Clonalscope, and RCTD revealed cancer-dependent performance: Clonalscope recovered copy-number signals more accurately in ovarian and colorectal cancer, whereas CopyKAT performed better in hepatocellular carcinoma, reflecting both the assumptions of each method and the copy-number landscapes of the three cancers. OncoSpot's ground truth also exposed a failure mode in Clonalscope's malignant spot identification, in which tumor and normal labels were inverted, and allowed us to trace its cause. These method-dependent behaviors would be difficult to detect in real data. OncoSpot provides a framework for benchmarking CNA inference, subclone detection, malignant spot identification, and normal spot deconvolution, and its modular design and guidelines allow extension to additional cancer types. OncoSpot is freely available at https://github.com/compbio-mallory/OncoSpot.

papers.title: T cell transcriptomes in simulated microgravity in vivo
papers.abstract: Spaceflight exposes astronauts to a combination of stressors, among which microgravity remains the least well characterized at the level of human immune cell function. We examined the in vivo effect of long-term simulated microgravity (SMG) on T cell transcriptomes in ten healthy male volunteers who completed a three-week dry immersion protocol without countermeasures. Peripheral blood was collected at five time points covering a pre-immersion baseline (day -7), three intra-exposure time points (days 7, 14 and 21) and a recovery time point one week after the end of exposure (day 28). CD3+ T cells were isolated and analysed by RNA-seq, with differential expression assessed per volunteer and KEGG pathway enrichment used to identify the most affected gene networks. SMG was associated with transcript-level changes in genes mapping to key molecular pathways, including those involved in cell proliferation, cell-cycle regulation, maintenance of genome integrity, and oncogenic and tumour-suppressor networks. Hub genes shared across the most significant pathways were differentially expressed in the majority of volunteers. A notable finding was pronounced inter-individual heterogeneity: samples clustered primarily by volunteer identity, yet a coordinated temporal shift during exposure and a partial return toward baseline by day 28 were detectable across donors, and these changes occurred in the absence of detectable systemic inflammation. These results indicate that SMG is associated with altered T cell transcriptional programs in vivo and that the response is sufficiently variable between individuals to favor personalized rather than uniform countermeasure strategies.

papers.title: Simple, static, spiking nonlinearities can account for seemingly complex interactions between visual, motor and cognitive variables in the visual cortex.
papers.abstract: Neural activity in the visual cortex is driven by the stimulus and modulated by multiple task-related variables, including spatial attention, eye movements, and perceptual decisions. These multiple influences are each typically described as nonlinear interactions such as gain or normalization, raising the question of how these diverse signals can be combined through cellular or circuit mechanisms. Here we address this problem by examining neuronal responses in macaque visual areas V2 and V3 during a visual discrimination task that dissociates spatial attention from motor planning and microsaccadic eye movements. Using a statistical modeling framework, we show that attentional, microsaccade-related, and choice-related influences on neural activity are best explained by a simple additive stimulus-independent input modulation, which manifests as a gain via a spiking nonlinearity. In addition to explaining how interactions between variables might be accomplished mechanistically, this framework also resolves a controversy about the relationship between microsaccades and spatial attention. We find that neither microsaccade direction nor microsaccade-related neural activity accounts for attentional modulation, although these variables are often correlated, leading to apparent interactions. Thus, visual cortex can integrate sensory, motor-related, and cognitive signals through a parsimonious mechanism that preserves stable stimulus representations while supporting flexible, context-dependent modulation.

papers.title: Genetic Variation in Photosynthetic Maintenance and Post-Chill Recovery for Early Season Maize Plantings
papers.abstract: Earlier maize planting could extend the growing season and improve synchronization of crop nitrogen demand with biogenically available soil nitrogen in spring, but seedling photosynthesis and development are strongly constrained by chilling. Eleven genetically diverse maize inbred lines were evaluated under a spring-like controlled environment regime containing five days of chilling stress followed by a recovery period, and across four early-spring field environments. Gas exchange, chlorophyll fluorescence, chlorophyll status, immature-leaf growth, vegetative stage, biomass, and visible cold injury were quantified to characterize physiological and developmental responses during chilling and recovery. Chilling substantially reduced net CO2 assimilation and rapidly decreased {Phi}PSII, while stomatal conductance responded slower. Genotypic differences in assimilation and {Phi}PSII were compressed during prolonged chilling but reemerged during recovery. Chilling also slowed immature-leaf elongation and largely arrested vegetative developmental progression; both resumed rapidly after warming, and advanced recovery stage development was associated with a greater fraction of mature leaf biomass. Assimilation and {Phi}PSII were most tightly associated during recovery and remained positively associated across field environments, although the strength of this relationship depended strongly on environment. Field expression of genotype effects was highly environment dependent, but broad-sense heritability was moderate to high for a variety of measured photosynthetic and physiological traits. Compared with the benchmark chilling-tolerant C4 grass Miscanthus, the maize panel exhibited similar photosynthetic performance, underscoring the accession dependence of this comparative benchmark. Taken together, these results identify photosynthetic maintenance and recovery as separable components of early-season cold performance and characterize physiologically informative and heritable traits associated with chilling stress resilience.

papers.title: Aggregate Deep Visual Proteomics reveals selective organization of α-synuclein inclusions
papers.abstract: -Synuclein inclusions, the lesions typical of Parkinson's disease, have been interpreted as protective deposits, toxic species or failed degradation products, each predicting a different composition and correlating that enrichment with neuron dysfunction and eventual degeneration. Distinguishing them requires measuring what an inclusion concentrates relative to the cell that built it. Here we developed Aggregate Deep Visual Proteomics, which uses ultrasensitive mass spectrometry to profile laser-microdissected inclusions against the remainder of the same cell or a matched host. In HEK293 cells, iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons and post-mortem patient brain, each inclusion concentrated a selective subset of its cell's proteome, independent of abundance and dominated by membrane, in neurons largely presynaptic. Inclusions took up whole assemblies, with subunits moving together in 421 of 438 complexes, and the V-ATPase alone was enriched in all three systems. Degradation cargo stayed with the receptors that route it, consistent with sequestration and failed degradation acting together. Neuritic and somatic inclusions differed, the former rich in UBQLN2 and the latter in intermediate filaments. In the cell line, phosphorylated -synuclein was tenfold higher in the inclusion than in the rest of the cell, with about one third of the rise already present before an inclusion was visible. Measured against its host, the composition of an inclusion becomes a readout of how it formed and a source of candidate markers and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: A comparative transcriptomic framework across kidney organoid, assembloid, and transplantation models
papers.abstract: Human kidney organoids recapitulate key aspects of renal development and have emerged as valuable platforms for disease modeling, nephrotoxicity screening, and therapeutic development. The field now includes a wide range of emerging protocols with distinct cellular compositions and maturation states, which complicates systematic comparison and model selection. Here, we integrated single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomes from 11 studies spanning kidney organoid and assembloids, both in vitro and following transplantation, benchmarked against fetal and adult kidney references. Transcriptional maturation toward adult identity is compartment specific and does not correlate with protocol complexity. Assembloid protocols show the most adult-like podocyte and distal nephron signatures, transplantation is associated with enhanced tubular oxidative metabolic features, only protocols incorporating ureteric progenitors reliably generate collecting-duct lineages, and no protocol achieves mature adult proximal tubule identity. Annotating against either fetal or adult kidney reference alone leads to misassignment, because early fetal nephron epithelium transcriptionally resembles injury-dedifferentiated adult proximal tubule cells. Assembloid and transplantation models share elevated mechanosensing pathway expression independently of vascularization. Together, these findings provide a framework for kidney organoid model selection.

papers.title: Genome-wide chromatin accessibility during early embryogenesis in a generalist cichlid fish
papers.abstract: Background Lake Malawi's haplochromine cichlids are one of the most rapid and species-rich vertebrate adaptive radiations known, generating hundreds of species within < 1 million years, yet how regulatory regions shape their embryonic development remains poorly understood. Astatotilapia calliptera, a generalist riverine lineage and proxy for the ancestral stock that seeded this radiation, offers a developmental chromatin baseline against which regulatory divergence in specialised lineages can be compared. Results We generated genome-wide ATAC-seq profiles of A. calliptera embryos across three developmental stages (3, 7 and 12 days post-fertilisation, dpf), identifying 550,876-701,889 accessible chromatin peaks per stage. Accessible chromatin was enriched at gene promoters and at both highly conserved and accelerated conserved noncoding elements at every stage. The functional repertoire of accessible-promoter genes shifted across development, from early patterning at 3 dpf to the broadest regulatory repertoire at 7 dpf, and an increasingly neural- and locomotory-behaviour-enriched repertoire by 12 dpf, coinciding with post-hatching motor maturation. Differential accessibility showed that chromatin opening, rather than closing, dominates the earliest transitions (3 vs 7 and 3 vs 12 dpf), driven mostly by general metabolic genes, whereas the smaller, later 7 vs 12 dpf transition combined targeted gains at tissue-remodelling and apoptosis genes with losses at genes governing early neural and retinal patterning; almost all of these losses (96%) were at promoters that had opened between 3 and 7 dpf, indicating transient rather than sustained opening. Transcription factor (TF) footprinting identified stage-specific regulatory activity among developmentally important TFs, while the broader TF-promoter network remained topologically stable across all three stages, built around conserved hub regulators of core neural and sensory patterning genes e.g., SOX2, FOXG1, PTF1A, SOX10. This suggests that wiring is established early and largely maintained, following the hourglass model, with developmental progression driven by changes in activity of this conserved programme. Conclusions Together, these findings establish the first embryonic epigenomic resource for A. calliptera, revealing a developmental chromatin landscape of broad early opening and progressive functional specialisation, and providing a comparative framework for understanding how regulatory evolution has shaped Lake Malawi cichlid diversification.

papers.title: Classifying tumors from broad category to hierarchical molecular subtype: an interpretable hierarchical framework for precision oncology
papers.abstract: Precise tumor subtype classification is important for guiding personalized treatment, characterizing tumor heterogeneity, and investigating molecular mechanisms. However, most existing multi-label classification models use flat architectures and do not fully exploit the inherent hierarchical relationships and biological constraints among tumor types, which limits their performance and interpretability in complex, fine-grained pan-cancer classification.
