papers.abstract: Living systems operate far from thermodynamic equilibrium, sustaining complexity through continuous free-energy influx and heat dissipation. Yet the higher-order functional constraints imposed by non-equilibrium dynamics remain largely unexplored. To formalize how changes in cellular entropy production constrain intracellular organization across proliferative state transitions, we developed a stochastic-thermodynamic model linking reduced dissipative drive to transient increases in intracellular configurational entropy. Within this framework, we examined abundance-weighted predicted RNA folding stability as a transcriptome-level projection of the intracellular configurational remodelling. Consistent with the model, transcriptome reorganization across the cell cycle produces coordinated, phase-dependent changes in the distribution of transcript-level RNA folding free energies. Extending this analysis to stress adaptation, we find that human cancer cells exposed to molecularly targeted agents and nutrient-limited Escherichia coli converge on expressed RNA pools enriched for transcripts with less negative RNA folding free energies, despite marked heterogeneity in the transcriptional responses within each system. Opposing shifts during acquired resistance under continued drug exposure and bacterial recovery from starvation further support an association with growth state. Together, these findings suggest that transcriptome organization extends beyond gene-regulatory programs to collective biophysical properties that may reflect non-equilibrium constraints shaping cellular-state transitions.

papers.title: Peptorama: Structure creation and exploratory data analysis for non-ribosomal peptides
papers.abstract: Non-ribosomal peptides (NRPs) are a diverse family of compounds with many clinical and biotechnological uses. NRP biodiscovery increasingly focuses on biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), and NRP structures can generally be predicted from BGCs. Despite their chemical connection, there is no individual research tool which quickly analyses NRPs and BGCs in combination. Here, we present Peptorama, which simplifies drawing diverse NRP structures and allows rapid comparisons between known and predicted NRPs. We show the utility of peptide comparisons and interactive analysis for biodiscovery, exemplified by retrospective analysis of calcium dependent antibiotics and biodiscovery of novel pyoverdine producing candidate strains. Peptide comparisons are computationally more efficient than BGC comparisons, substantially cutting runtimes without loss of biodiscovery functionality. Peptorama can therefore enhance existing pipelines with a rapid method for comparing peptide-level diversity. It is available online at https://peptorama.com/ and is also available to be run locally.

papers.title: CARTnet: Template-guided B-cell Epitope Prediction with Contact-aware Attention
papers.abstract: B-cell epitope prediction remains challenging due to the limited availability of experimentally characterized data and the incomplete understanding of antibody-antigen recognition. Here, we present CARTnet, a novel contact-aware deep learning framework that integrates multimodal features and template-derived epitope information. CARTnet demonstrated superior performance when compared to the existing state-of-the-art methods across most evaluation metrics on both the internal and external test datasets. In particular, CARTnet achieved an AUPRC of 0.243 on the internal test set, compared with 0.220 for DiscoTope-3, 0.140 for BepiPred-2, and 0.198 for BepiPred-3. This improvement was also observed on the external test set, where CARTnet achieved an AUPRC of 0.267, compared with 0.192, 0.111, and 0.215 for DiscoTope-3, BepiPred-2, and BepiPred-3, respectively, supporting its generalizability. CARTnet also supports template-guided prediction, in which limited prior epitope information can improve the identification of additional epitope residues; a single template residue increased the AUPRC of the template-based variant from 0.225 to 0.403 on the internal test set. Furthermore, we demonstrated that epitope information from closely related viruses can be transferred across the genus Alphavirus to improve epitope prediction accuracy. These results establish CARTnet as an accurate framework for both de novo and template-guided B-cell epitope prediction.

papers.title: Representation-aware calibration enables statistically reliable protein structure search
papers.abstract: Searching large databases of predicted protein structures can reveal remote homologs, but reliable discovery requires accurate significance estimates. We show that native E-values reported by protein structure search tools such as Foldseek and Reseek can be unreliable, leading to false discoveries or missed homologs. To address this problem, we introduce Struct-Caliper, which provides reliable query-specific p-values for protein structure search. The method uses representation-aware query randomization to generate background queries and compares observed alignment scores with the highest scores from randomized searches of the same database. In simulations, SG p-values generally kept reported false positive at or below the chosen cutoff under the evaluated randomization procedures. In searches of 15,177 ASTRAL40 structures, SG p-values increased Foldseek homolog recovery by 18.2% with slightly fewer false discoveries compared with native E-values at a cutoff of 0.01. For Reseek, false discoveries even decreased by 99.5%. Across 73 queries searched against more than two million AlphaFoldDB structures, SG p-values increased the mean recovery of DALI-supported matches by 23.5% at the same cutoff. These results show that Struct-Caliper can improve the reliability of structure searches and help prioritize discoveries for further biological analysis.

papers.title: Multispecies transport shapes electrochemical environments in perforated cells
papers.abstract: Cells maintain asymmetric electrochemical environments across selectively permeable plasma membranes. Ion channels on plasma membranes redistribute small ions, whereas large openings such as gasdermin pores allow both ions and proteins to cross the membrane, generating a multispecies transport regime. The transport of charged ions and proteins shapes electrochemical environments, leading to osmolarity changes, which in turn promotes water influx and cell swelling. Although biologists have observed the phenotypic progression from pore formation to cell swelling for decades, the molecular transport events underlying this progression remain elusive. To elucidate how pore formation drives downstream cellular effects, we establish quantitative multispecies transport frameworks to investigate gasdermin-perforated cells. We start by developing a reductionist model and benchmarking it against analytical Donnan predictions. We then explore three-dimensional geometries containing individual pores or pore clusters that form either simultaneously or sequentially. We reveal that ion-protein timescale separation generates non-canonical Donnan-like states, pore and cargo properties tune local transport, pore clustering modulates osmotic gradients, and sequential pore formation produces feedback-dependent dynamics. This work deepens our mechanistic understanding of cellular responses to membrane damage and informs the therapeutic design of pore-forming proteins with tunable cellular effects.

papers.title: Discovering compositional, interpretable structure in social behavior
papers.abstract: Quantitative assessment of behavior is vital for rigorous analysis of how animals interact in the world and how behavior is generated from brain activity. Recent advances in automated pose detection have made possible data-driven discovery of movement action sequences. While many algorithms have been developed for this purpose, their categorical nature, i.e., the assumption that behavior is one action at a time, prohibits expressive quantification of social behavior. Such behavior is combinatorial and compositional, with multiple animals performing actions that may be either independent or coordinated over time. Here we show how developments in decomposed linear dynamical systems (dLDS) can instead represent action-generating dynamics as a signed, graded mixture of shared linear operators acting directly on keypoint positions. We demonstrate our approach across both single-mouse and two-mouse datasets, comparing against a state-of-the-art switching model, keypoint-MoSeq. In single-mouse data, we find that a composition of three operators can capture the full repertoire of 21 keypoint-MoSeq syllables, showing that even for a single animal, the action space is more parsimoniously described by a continuous subspace than clustered motifs. In a two-mouse resident--intruder assay, we identify, without behavioral labels, separate primitives for self-action, inter-animal-geometry, and social-action. The latter couples an animal's action to its partner's relative bearing, enabling the action to incorporate the social geometry in which it occurs. dLDS further decodes human-labeled social behaviors (i.e., "attack", "investigation", "mount", and "other") more accurately than behavior-selective keypoint-MoSeq syllable sets using fewer units. Together, these results demonstrate that compositional, time-varying linear dynamics can provide a path towards flexible and interpretable modeling of action-level behavior for both individual and social behavior.

papers.title: A new Serratia taxon found in a trombidiform mite shows genomic evidence of host adaptation but is phylogenetically distinct from Serratia symbiotica
papers.abstract: Abstract The evolutionary transition from free-living bacteria to host-adapted symbionts is typically accompanied by substantial genomic changes. Within the genus Serratia, this transition has so far been documented only in the aphid-associated species, Serratia symbiotica, whereas all other Serratia species are free-living. In this study, we identify a putatively new Serratia taxon using metagenomic approaches in the trombidiform mite, Halotydeus destructor. We provide genomic evidence for a possible transition to a host-adapted lifestyle in this new Serratia sp., which sits phylogenetically within a clade of free-living Serratia species. The genomic signatures of evolving toward a host-adapted lifestyle include a reduced genome size and coding capacity, an elevated transposase fraction, and detectable chromosomal rearrangements, relative to other free-living Serratia species. However, the species does not show the same structure of genome reduction as S. symbiotica. Functional gene content analyses including COG categories and virulence factor repertoires also showed that our new Serratia sp. had a distinct gene profile from both free-living Serratia and S. symbiotica. Additional genomic screening suggests that infections of the new Serratia sp. are common in wild populations of H. destructor across its invasive Australian range, warranting future investigations on the possible role this symbiont plays in the evolutionary ecology of its mite host. Our work not only highlights a potential parallel transition to a host-adapted lifestyle in the Serratia genus, but also represents the first characterisation of a possible host-adapted Serratia taxon in a trombidiform mite.

papers.title: Non-equilibrium cyclic conformations of DNA under electrokinetic confinement
papers.abstract: Classic nanofluidic devices harness geometric confinement to modulate single polymer conformation and control chain dynamics. While classic nanofluidic devices have given rise to a range of applications, they are fundamentally limited by the static nature of their construction, which restricts real time control over molecular conformations. The reversible electrokinetic confinement (RECON) technique enables time-dependent control of DNA conformations in nanowells via dynamic modulation of field-induced confinement. Here, we demonstrate that applying dynamically varying confinement using stochastic and periodic signals can drive the confined polymer to access a range of non-equilibrium states, with the distinct configurations quantified via their radius of gyration tensor. For periodic driving, the device allows controlled cycling across conformational states, with distinct hysteresis observed in the shape anisotropy modulation. We quantify the interplay between the driving frequency, driving amplitude, and resulting hysteresis. Overall, our results establish RECON as a platform for active manipulation of single molecules, opening new avenues for studying non-equilibrium polymer physics and developing high-throughput, dynamically tunable nanofluidic devices.

papers.title: Comparative Transcriptomic Analysis of Gene Expression Patterns in Neutrophils from Rheumatoid Arthritis and COVID-19
papers.abstract: Background: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disorder characterised by chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation, and neutrophils play a key role in its progression. COVID-19 also involves neutrophil hyperactivation that contributes to severe immune responses. Emerging evidence links COVID-19 to increased incidence or exacerbation of RA, potentially through overlapping immune mechanisms. Objective: To compare neutrophil transcriptomic profiles in RA and COVID-19 and identify shared immune pathways and disease-specific features. Methods: Publicly available neutrophil RNA-seq count data from the Gene Expression Omnibus were analysed: RA versus healthy controls (GSE116899) and COVID-19 versus healthy controls (GSE212041). A second COVID-19 comparison (severe versus convalescent) was assembled from GSE272381 and GSE227116. Differential expression was analysed with DESeq2, pathway enrichment with fgsea (Hallmark gene sets) and topGO (Gene Ontology biological process and molecular function). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were compared between diseases by direction of change. Results: In RA neutrophils, 11,355 DEGs were identified, of which 90 had an absolute log2 fold change of at least 2 with p<0.05 (70 upregulated, 20 downregulated). Twenty-four Hallmark gene sets were positively enriched at adjusted p<0.05, led by interferon alpha and interferon gamma responses, and Gene Ontology analysis highlighted type I interferon, antiviral and double-stranded RNA terms. In COVID-19 neutrophils, 420 DEGs were identified (37 upregulated, 383 downregulated), and no Hallmark gene set reached adjusted p<0.05. Of the 90 RA DEGs, 46 changed in the same direction in COVID-19 without reaching significance, and 27 changed significantly in the opposite direction, including CAMK1G, SIGLEC1, OAS1 and OAS3. In the second COVID-19 comparison, several of these genes, including OAS1, OAS3 and SIGLEC1, changed in the same direction as in RA. Conclusions: RA neutrophils show a transcriptional programme enriched for interferon and antiviral-response pathways. Part of the RA signature is shared with COVID-19 neutrophils, while a subset of genes diverges, and this divergence depended on the COVID-19 comparison used. These findings are hypothesis-generating and provide candidate genes for experimental validation.

papers.title: Hazard Structure and Repair Kinetics: A 2x2 Classification that Resolves the Stochastic-Death / Individual-Tolerance Dilemma
papers.abstract: The two variants of GUTS (General Unified Threshold model of Survival), stochastic death and individual tolerance, disagree about no-effect concentrations under time-variable exposure, and no standard test separates them. Each variant fixes two independent choices, which form a 2x2 classification: whether the hazard accumulates while damage exceeds a threshold (cumulative) or is set by the highest damage reached (peak-based), and whether repair is proportional or saturating. Calibration fit cannot choose: each structure fits by adjusting its own damage recovery, the cumulative one faster in twelve of fourteen compounds. For two identical pulses separated by complete recovery, the cumulative hazard predicts equal survival through both whatever the parameters, so a carry-over ratio (second-to-first survival) above one excludes it; in Gammarus pulex fourteen of fifteen ratios are at or above one, seven significantly. The peak-based hazard predicts the ratio's maximum, approached as intervals lengthen in five of six compounds. For organophosphates, whose recovery outlasts the published pulse intervals, the one test on measured damage favours the peak-based hazard: diazinon-exposed Daphnia magna stopped being immobilised once acetylcholinesterase, still inhibited, began to recover. The peak-based hazard is the appropriate default for toxicokinetic-toxicodynamic risk assessment of narcotics and uncouplers, and provisionally of organophosphates.

papers.title: Monoaminergic changes are associated with impaired neurogenesis along the longitudinal axis of the hippocampus in ageing and dementia
papers.abstract: Neurogenesis persists in the adult human hippocampus and is thought to support memory and emotional regulation. Both normal ageing and Parkinson disease dementia (PDD) are associated with reduced hippocampal neurogenesis, but why this occurs and how this might change across the across the hippocampal axis remains unclear. Here, we quantified the expression of genes regulating neurogenesis from stem cell production to neuron maturation and examined their relationship with monoaminergic activity throughout the post-mortem hippocampus in young and aged individuals, as well as in individuals with PDD. DCX and MKI67 expression were markedly reduced in PDD cases throughout the hippocampus, while GFAP and GFAP{delta} were elevated in aged control individuals but not in PDD. Dopamine and serotonin levels were unchanged but reduced levels of the dopamine metabolite DOPAC, and increased levels of the serotonin metabolite 5-HIAA, were present across the hippocampal axis in PDD. Hierarchical regression analysis identified DOPAC and 5-HIAA as significant predictors of DCX and MKI67 expression independent of diagnostic group. Coupling between stem cell markers and proliferative output was preserved in the hippocampus of young controls but was absent in aged controls and in PDD. These data suggest changes in monoaminergic systems are linked to stage-specific deficits in neuronal proliferation and maturation, identifying a potential mechanistic bridge to cognitive decline in PDD.

papers.title: Gene expression in Anolis sagrei suggests conservation of patterning mechanisms drives formation of two high acuity areas
papers.abstract: As humans we enjoy high acuity color vision. A specialized area in our retinas, the fovea, endows us with this ability. Some vertebrates, such as the Anolis sagrei (brown anole), have two such areas. Whether different species use conserved developmental mechanism(s), and whether the same mechanism is used in one organism to pattern both foveae, are herein addressed in the brown anole. We observed that the expression of canonical axis patterning genes is conserved in the anole retina. Retinoic acid and Fgf signaling pathways were found to define two discrete domains corresponding to emerging foveae. Comparative spatial analyses of early gene expression patterns among anole, chick, and human revealed conserved patterns in the anlage of the high acuity areas of each species. Variation in foveal number could arise through spatial redeployment of conserved patterning programs.

papers.title: Atmospheric pollution contributed to destabilizing a small mammal community amid four decades of environmental changes
papers.abstract: In the recent decades, climatic and land-use changes paralleled major decreases in atmospheric pollution, but unclear is how these concomitant changes shape ecological dynamics. We analyzed 39 years (1986-2024) of semiannual abundances for six small-mammal species in the Black Triangle of Europe (Czechia), a region historically-marked by acidic rains causing forest diebacks and toxic lead (Pb) deposition. We combined these small-mammal data with monthly time series of atmospheric pollution, vegetation index (NDVI), meteorology and soil moisture. We used Empirical Dynamic Modelling (EDM) to infer chaos, recover species-species and environment-species causal relationships, recover time-varying interactions, and perform out-of-sample forecasts. Small mammal populations were causally affected by atmospheric pollution, and its abrupt decline in the late 1990s likely triggered a delayed critical transition of community composition. Pollution primarily affected the dominant omnivores and strengthened the interactions among species, a hallmark of instability. We identified a second route to chaos with a role of vegetation dynamics and soil moisture that was especially strong on shrews. Our feedback-loop analysis suggests how pollution and other environmental changes favored destabilizing, positive feedbacks. Forecasting of these chaotic dynamics improved when adding the relevant environmental predictors, demonstrating that the unpredictability of chaotic systems can slightly improve when we identify the main drivers of interactions in a network, offering hope for anticipating the future of complex ecosystems. Our study offers a unique retrospective of the destabilizing effects of pollution, an overlooked macro-ecological driver.

papers.title: Sarrella massiliensis gen. nov. sp. nov., a new gut genus isolated from the stool of a healthy donor
papers.abstract: Strain Marseille-QA0792 (=CSUR QA0792, CECT 31199) was isolated from the feces of a healthy person using the culturomics method. The fecal sample originated from leftover material collected for a fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) procedure, obtained during a routine screening in accordance with the guidelines of the French National Agency for Medicines and Health Products Safety (ANSM). This strain is Gram-stain-negative, rod-shaped, non-motile, and non-spore-forming. It is strictly anaerobic, with optimal growth at 37{degrees}C. Strain Marseille-QA0792 presented its highest 16S rRNA identity, 96.2%, with ''Merdibacter massiliensis'' strain Marseille-P3254 (not validly published) (accession number LT598590) and ANI similarity of 75.0% with the same species. Among validly published species, strain Marseille-QA0792 showed its highest 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity (91.5%) with Faecalicoccus acidiformans strain 37-2a (accession number HQ452864), whereas all computed average nucleotide identity (ANI) values were below 75%. Genome sequencing revealed a genome size of 2.67 Mb and a G+C content of 50.01%. This species is classified within the Erysipelotrichaceae family in the Bacillota phylum. Thus, we isolated for the first time a novel genus named Sarrella massiliensis gen. nov., sp. nov., strain Marseille-QA0792. This discovery highlights the importance of continuing culturomics efforts to explore the human microbiome.

papers.title: Immersion as inference: An active inference account of induced realities and its relation to the two-competitor model
papers.abstract: Immersive technologies are designed for a single target: the human perceptual system. Engineers of virtual and augmented reality have long recognized that a display does not have to replicate the physical world, it only has to provide the inputs that satisfy the senses at the level at which the brain samples them. This engineering intuition is, in fact, a statement about brain function. Here we develop it into a formal account of immersion within the active inference framework. We treat an induced reality (a virtual, augmented, or mixed reality, but also a book or a daydream) as a candidate generative model that competes with the model of the actual reality for the explanation of a shared sensorium and for the control of action. Immersion is then defined as the ensuant belief that the induced reality best explains the current sensory signals and supports the current perceived reality of the winning model, despite any break in immersion by Bayesian model switching driven by a high-precision prediction error that the induced model cannot absorb. Exogenous and endogenous attention, implemented as weights governing stream selection in our earlier two-competitor model, which treated attention as necessary but not sufficient for immersion, appear as two routes of precision allocation: likelihood precision of evolutionarily entrenched sensory events, and precision that follows the expected free energy of policies. Affect and motivation enter through the pragmatic and epistemic value of remaining in the induced reality and through the rate of change of free energy. We show that the two-competitor attentional focus vector and its angle are recovered from the active inference variables, and we reproduce the two scenarios of the original model, a rewarding and a fatiguing activity interrupted by a slamming door, in a minimal simulation. The account links presence, embodiment, cybersickness, and narrative absorption to a single quantity, and it yields concrete predictions for the psychophysiological assessment and closed-loop control of immersion. We discuss implications for neuroergonomic design in which the evolutionarily entrenched core of perception is non-negotiable while its experience-dependent periphery can be trained.

papers.title: Inferring modularity in genotype-phenotype maps using patterns of epistasis and pleiotropy
papers.abstract: Methods for inferring the relationship between genotype and phenotype often search for low-dimensional structure, motivated by the hypothesis that genetic loci can be organized into a small number of groups representing biological processes. These methods typically group genetic loci based on which other loci they interact with (epistasis) or based on how their effects covary across environmental conditions (patterns of pleiotropy). Here, we present two complementary methods that combine epistasis and pleiotropy to infer modular structure. The first, Sparse, Low-dimensional, Epistatic Decomposition (SLED), parametrizes the genotype-phenotype map in terms of a small number of modules: loci contribute sparse additive and epistatic effects to modules, and modules contribute sparse additive and epistatic effects to multiple phenotypes. The second method, Graph Tensor Decomposition (GTD), represents the epistatic interactions in each environment as a combination of shared basis graphs, each capturing a pattern of epistasis that recurs across environments. Since GTD does not use additive effects, learned graphs are not restricted to include only loci whose additive effects covary across environments. We validate SLED and GTD on synthetic data, then apply both methods to an experimental dataset consisting of the growth rates of yeast segregants from an F1 cross, measured across 101 environments with a hub-and-spoke structure. We evaluate the biological structure of the inferred modules and show that both models generalize well to held-out environments. Finally, we compare the modules inferred by SLED, GTD, and a previously established method that infers sparse modular structure from a locus-by-environment matrix of additive effects (SSD) and find that all three methods yield highly similar modular architectures. This suggests that the genetic architecture underlying this dataset is consistent across additive effects (SSD), epistatic effects (GTD), and both jointly (SLED). Together, our methods provide a framework for combining two sources of information, epistasis and pleiotropy, to infer interpretable low-dimensional structure in genotype-phenotype maps, expanding on previous work that has traditionally treated each independently.

papers.title: MHCII+ cancer-associated fibroblasts promote antitumor immunity in pancreatic cancer
papers.abstract: The functions of major histocompatibility complex class II molecule-expressing cancer-associated fibroblasts (MHCII+CAFs) in pancreatic cancer remain controversial. MHCII+CAFs are primarily described as immunosuppressive, as MHCII allows for direct interaction with, and support of, regulatory T cells (Tregs). However, MHCII+CAF functions may be more complex depending on their origins and their cellular interactions within the tumor microenvironment. Here, using orthotopic models of pancreatic cancer, we show that conventional CD4+ T cells and their production of Interferon gamma (IFN{gamma}) increased MHCII+CAFs in tumors. Acute depletion of Tregs using Foxp3DTR mice revealed that Tregs suppress the abundance of MHCII+CAFs in tumors by inhibiting CD4 T cell responses that can directly control primary tumor growth and metastatic progression. Functionally, MHCII expression on fibroblasts was required for CD4 T cell control of PDAC progression upon Treg ablation. Collectively, our findings identify an IFN{gamma}-driven, antitumor activity of MHCII expression on CAFs and reveal that CAFs may be harnessed to promote adaptive immunity to PDAC.

papers.title: CryoID2: deep learning-enhanced identification of protein and RNA from cryoEM maps
papers.abstract: Identifying the molecular components of cryoEM/cryoET maps of endogenous or poorly characterized complexes remains a major bottleneck. CryoID2 addresses this by integrating deep learning-based feature prediction with sequence prioritization and structural evaluation. Three 3D U-Nets extract structure classes, key-atom positions, and reduced residue/nucleotide types from the input map. These predictions support backbone tracing and the generation of short sequence queries that rank candidates from a user-supplied pool-using BLASTp for proteins and a maximin strategy for RNA. Corresponding PDB or AlphaFold models are then retrieved, rigidly fitted using predicted features and experimental density, and ranked by map agreement. Module-level tests show high-recall feature prediction and resolution-dependent atom clustering, while a 52-case benchmark recovers near-reference fitting quality. In practice, cryoID2 correctly identified PfA-M17 from a 166-protein mass-spectrometry pool and the unannotated Ca-raiA RNA from a genome-derived non-coding sequence set, demonstrating a unified sequence-plus-structure route to molecular identification in cryoEM maps.

papers.title: Social copying drives spatial allocation in gregarious herbivores
papers.abstract: Resting patch selection in free-ranging social cattle (Bos taurus) inhabiting steep, rugged, mountain valleys is critical, because the recurrent use of flatter resting patches may reduce energetic costs and enhance fitness prospects. As these patches may constitute a limited resource, understanding their pattern of use dynamics may help explain resting patch selection. We therefore combine empirical data with a theoretical modelling framework to investigate the processes underlying resting patch selection. Using high-resolution GPS tracking data from 144 cows collected over three seasons, we identify several recurrently used resting patches located on significantly gentler slopes than expected in the valley. We then build a simple, memory-free agent-based model, which suggests that the dynamics of resting patch selection arise from social copying and, to a lesser extent, from individual heterogeneity. The model quantitatively reproduces three empirical observables: a slowing (sub-linear) discovery of new sites through time, heterogeneous occupancy across resting patches and similarity in patch use among individuals. These results suggest that collective dynamics in social species can emerge primarily from a simple social mechanism with weaker modulation from inter-individual heterogeneity, such as age, without explicitly incorporating individual memory to reproduce the aggregate patterns.

papers.title: Long read sequencing reveals changes in measured isoform structure and abundance due to RNA processing
papers.abstract: Oxford Nanopore Technology enables direct RNA sequencing without reverse transcription (RT) and cDNA sequencing without PCR amplification, allowing investigation of how RNA preparation protocols bias sequencing data. PCR amplification is known to introduce biases related to expression levels, transcript lengths, and GC content. However, biases introduced by RT have been described more recently and their quantification remains more elusive. Using seven cell line datasets from SG-NEx, we compared nanopore sequencing of direct RNA, direct cDNA, and PCR-amplified cDNA. We identified hundreds of differentially expressed genes and isoforms between protocols, indicating significant changes in observed expression. Differentially expressed isoforms displayed expected amplification biases, and further we observed decreased PCR counts associated with higher m6A methylation levels on native RNA. We also found differential transcript usage in hundreds of genes across cell lines, showing substantial changes in measured isoform proportions between protocols. Analysis of structural differences between isoforms that switch dominance revealed that while some events involve simple RNA fragmentation, most involve complex structural differences including novel junctions (e.g. exon skipping, intron retention). Compared to non-DTU genes, inserted introns (exitrons) were significantly more common after RT and amplification. Furthermore, visualisation of raw coverage data proved crucial for qualitative validation of experimental findings.

papers.title: Replication-coupled maturation of readthrough late transcripts by a polyomavirus small T antigen
papers.abstract: Productive polyomavirus gene expression requires the maturation of long, non-polyadenylated "wraparound" transcripts generated by late-strand readthrough of the polyadenylation signal on the circular genome, giving rise to structural protein mRNAs and microRNAs. In Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCV), small T (sT) antigen, along with large T (LT) antigen-mediated DNA replication, drives this process. Deletion of sT (MCV{Delta}sT) attenuates late gene transcription, abolishes splicing, eliminates VP1 expression, and traps unspliced transcripts in the nucleus. Exogenous sT restored transcription and splicing in an aphidicolin-sensitive manner, requiring domains that activate DNA replication and bind chromatin. RNA sequencing revealed that sT promotes splicing and polyadenylation of wraparound transcripts, thereby increasing cytoplasmic VP1 and VP2 mRNA levels. A dual-fluorescence reporter confirmed that the leaky late poly(A) signal (LpA) was used more efficiently upon sT expression, indicating enhanced polyadenylation. Co-expression with LT abolished this effect, likely by overwhelming the capacity of the polyadenylation machinery. sT from HPyV7 and HPyV9 could similarly rescue this defect, indicating that this regulatory activity is conserved in a subset of sT proteins. Together, these findings define sT as a replication-coupled regulator of late transcript expression, splicing, and polyadenylation, revealing how a compact DNA virus converts readthrough transcription into productive gene expression.

papers.title: Proteome-Wide Serology Identifies Secreted IgD against RSV Fusion Glycoprotein as a Signature of Broadly Elevated Antibody Response
papers.abstract: Serological evaluation of antibody response using conventional indirect immunoassays cannot capture the full depth, diversity, and functional complexity of human polyclonal antibodies. Here, we developed mass spectrometry-based Proteome-Wide Serology (ProWiSe) assays for the identification and absolute quantification of antigen-specific human antibodies across isotypes, subclasses, and variable-region repertoires. Using ProWiSe, we measured the depth and diversity of serum antibodies to multiple antigens of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a pathogen associated with repeated reinfections and skewed immune response. IgG1 antibodies targeting the fusion glycoprotein F (RSVF) dominated the antibody response, with a background-corrected median level of 1,700 ng/mL across 214 healthy maternal serum samples from the general population. ProWiSe identified reproducible co-enrichment of complement component 1q complexes, revealed the usage of several dozen IGHV variable-region germline genes in the anti-RSVF polyclonal response, and suggested limited IGHV repertoire diversity in some individuals. In addition to IgG1, we discovered a complex antibody response characterized by significantly elevated levels of nearly all human immunoglobulin isotypes and subclasses, including previously unexplored IgG4 and IgD. The identification of high-affinity IgD against prefusion and postfusion RSVF, but not against other antigens studied, was the most unexpected observation, occurring in 52% of the healthy maternal serum samples. ProWiSe unambiguously identified the secreted IgD isoform P01880-1 and supported the IgD paradox of preferential {lambda} light-chain usage in secreted IgD. Detectable anti-RSVF IgD levels ([≥]0.11 ng/mL) correlated with broadly elevated antibody responses across all other isotypes and subclasses, except IgE. ProWiSe assays offer a versatile platform for quantitative serological diagnostics, exploration of depth, diversity, and dynamics of polyclonal antibody response, and discovery of rare antibody isotypes.

papers.title: Scn2a-deficient mice exhibit serotonergic dysfunction and altered behavioral responses to psilocybin
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a prominent neurodevelopmental disorder affecting approximately 3.2% of children in the United States. Although ASD has traditionally been considered a polygenic disorder, advances in genetic testing have identified individual genes that can contribute to its development. Large-scale whole-exome sequencing has identified variants in SCN2A, which encodes the alpha subunit of the voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.2, as a leading monogenic cause of ASD. Social deficits are a core feature of ASD, and the serotonergic system has been implicated in the regulation of social behavior. Recent studies have demonstrated that serotonergic psychedelics, such as psilocybin, can increase sociability in mouse models of ASD. However, whether underlying genetic alterations associated with ASD influence behavioral responses to psilocybin remains poorly understood. Therefore, we investigated how Scn2a deficiency affects behavioral responses to psilocybin and whether these differences are accompanied by alterations in the serotonergic system. We found that Scn2a-deficient mice exhibited differential responses to psilocybin compared to wild-type (WT) mice. Specifically, psilocybin increased sociability in Scn2a-deficient mice without affecting anxiety-like behavior, whereas WT mice exhibited decreased anxiety-like behavior without increased sociability. Further behavioral evaluation revealed a reduced head twitch response in Scn2a-deficient mice following psilocybin administration compared to WT mice. To further investigate these differences, we examined serotonin levels and receptor expression in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), a brain region implicated in social behavior and psychedelic action. Although baseline serotonin levels in the mPFC did not differ between genotypes, Scn2a-deficient mice exhibited altered serotonin receptor expression. We further characterized the serotonergic system by evaluating neuronal activity in the Dorsal Raphe Nucleus, a major source of serotonergic projections to the mPFC, and found increased spontaneous firing in Scn2a-deficient mice. Together, these findings highlight serotonergic alterations associated with SCN2A deficiency and the potential for serotonergic interventions to alleviate social deficits associated with SCN2A-related ASD.

papers.title: Gain Control of Peripheral Input by Core Brain Thermosensors Drives Drosophila Thermoregulation
papers.abstract: Temperature affects all aspects of animal physiology, rendering thermoregulation critical for survival. In Drosophila larvae, well-established peripheral thermosensors detect temperature changes and mediate thermotaxis over a broad innocuous range, but how larvae seek a specific preferred body temperature within this range remains unknown. Here we show that core thermosensors in the brain (LPBT neurons) establish this setpoint by mediating warming-evoked turning at temperatures above it. LPBTs express the warmth-activated thermosensor TrpA1(A), but are not simply cell-autonomous thermosensors. Rather, sustained LPBT responses above setpoint require both peripheral thermosensory input and TRPA1-dependent thermosensing within LPBTs. TRPA1-dependent core thermosensing provides gain control that defines the homeostatic setpoint by tuning the behavioral weights of peripheral inputs. This new conception of thermal preference reveals parallels between Drosophila and mammalian thermoregulation.

papers.title: A microstructural analysis of water intake patterns associated with light phase food and water restriction in male and female rats.
papers.abstract: Water intake is influenced by both eating and circadian rhythms, and the available literature is mixed regarding which variable exerts greater control. Previous reports primarily focused on short term manipulations, however, one study using long term light phase food restriction found that water intake patterns primarily retained circadian characteristics in male rats. To further characterize this behavioral effect, water intake and lick microstructure was analyzed in male and female rats with food access restricted to the light phase. In addition, food and water intake and lick microstructure were analyzed when water access was restricted to the light phase. In support of the previous short term, but not long term, food manipulation studies, when food access was restricted to the light phase most water intake shifted to this time frame. This shift was medicated by increased lick burst number, suggesting altered satiety signaling underling this intake pattern. When water access was restricted to the light phase, food intake was equally distributed across the light and dark phases. There was no effect of sex on the patterns of intake during any test condition. These results further our understanding of the mechanisms underlying food and water-associated and circadian intake patterns by suggesting that altered satiety signaling underlies changes in water intake. Furthermore, these results show that the timing of food access has a greater effect on water intake patterns across the light-dark cycle than water access has on food intake patterns.

papers.title: CloneVI: A deep generative model for deciphering the relationships between cell state and mitochondrial genotype
papers.abstract: Cellular diversity arises from both genetic lineages and non-genetic regulation of cell states, and knowing which cell states are tied to lineages is central to understanding how clones shape disease. Single-cell multi-omics technologies measure mitochondrial DNA mutations together with gene expression or chromatin accessibility in the same cells, but clones are usually inferred from mutations alone, making such clones difficult to identify. We developed CloneVI, a deep generative model that infers clonal structure from a latent cell state derived from gene expression or chromatin accessibility. It estimates the clonal probability of each cell from this cell state, together with the allele frequency of each clone by reconstructing the observed mutation counts. In simulated data, CloneVI recovered the ground-truth clonal structure in both single-clone and mixed-clone cell populations. In clonal hematopoiesis single-cell RNA-seq data with enriched mitochondrial transcripts, the inferred clones were associated with specific mitochondrial DNA mutations, and some of them showed high expression of a T-cell receptor variable-region gene. In chronic lymphocytic leukemia mitochondrial single-cell ATAC-seq data, CloneVI separated populations with different heteroplasmy levels and identified increased PAX9 accessibility. In a multi-donor ovarian tumor cohort, CloneVI captured mutant-cell populations enriched in particular cell states, and a differential test weighted by the clonal probability revealed the transcription factor activity of the cell state in which the mutant cells concentrated. CloneVI thus identifies populations defined by mitochondrial DNA mutations and associated with cell states in single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data. CloneVI is available at https://github.com/TaichiHIBI/cloneVI.

papers.title: HOX13 factors shape cell developmental transcriptional program through multiple mechanisms that regulate chromatin accessibility.
papers.abstract: HOX transcription factors pattern embryonic tissues and organs and have post-developmental roles in adult tissue maintenance and function. They can bind inaccessible chromatin, but their roles in chromatin accessibility remain unclear. Using in vivo and in vitro approaches, we show that HOX13 factors promote both initial opening and maintenance of accessibility at subsets of target regulatory elements. Mechanistically, the HOX13-dependent chromatin accessibility involves both its homodimerization and the recruitment of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex. Our findings indicate that SWI/SNF contributes to the extent of opening but is neither sufficient nor the sole determinant of HOXA13 pioneering activity. In iPSCs, HOXA13 induction rapidly reduces pluripotency gene expression while activating an early osteochondrogenic transcriptional program, which, at least in part, corresponds to direct gene regulation by HOXA13. Together, these findings identify multiple, context-dependent contributions to HOX13-mediated chromatin regulation, resulting in early lineage-associated responses.

papers.title: XAMPGen: An Interpretable SI Pipeline For Novel Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are short peptides with a broad spectrum of activity against bacterial pathogens, representing a promising avenue for combating the growing threat of antibiotic resistance. This study focuses on two main components: 1) generating novel AMPs with desired properties using generative SI (GenSI) and 2) utilizing explainable SI (XSI) methods to validate the GenSI model and derive biological insights. In this work, we fine-tuned ProGen, a decoder-only protein language model, on known AMPs to generate novel peptide sequences with strong antimicrobial properties. To advance the interpretability and reliability of the generative model, we applied Explainable SI (XSI) techniques. Specifically, we used a probing classifier and a regressor to identify cornerstone layers that encode functionally critical information. Self-attention analysis within these layers revealed residue level interdependencies and patterns underlying antimicrobial functions, which we validated against well-characterized AMPs from the literature. Overall, these methods provide mechanistic insight into the model's decision-making process, offering a principled basis for trusting the sequences it generates rather than treating the model as a black box. Candidate sequences were filtered based on predicted Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) along with human insights into the structural activities of the AMPs in bacterial membranes, and a final set of peptides was selected for experimental testing. Biological assays for determining MIC confirmed antimicrobial activity in all generated and tested peptides, with fluorescence and circular dichroism measurements providing structural insight. With our XSI approach, we are able to reveal correlations between amino acid sequence patterns and binding properties of these sequences to bacterial membrane mimics, that directly correlate with biological activities in cell-based assays. This builds confidence in that the learned amino acid interdependencies as applied to AMPs carries physico-chemical meaning and is relevant for discoveries of novel AMPs with therapeutic potential. This work demonstrates that interpretable generative language models can serve as effective and transparent tools for rational AMP discovery.

papers.title: A Saliva-Inspired Model of Enzymatic Starch Hydrolysis by Alpha Amylase
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the enzymatic activity of alpha-amylase (AA) can serve as an effective physicochemical trigger for membrane remodeling in giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs). This work provides insight into how primitive protocellular reactions directly translate into the membrane's mechanical responses. Analysis of the potato starch utilized in this work is composed of ~26\% amylose and ~75\% amylopectin. Quantitative DNS analysis revealed time- and concentration-dependent accumulation of reducing sugars during starch degradation by AA. The HPLC-RID chromatograms demonstrated the synthesis of glucose, maltose, maltotriose, maltotetraose, maltopentaose, maltohexaose, and maltoheptaose, with maltose and maltotriose as the major products. The accumulation of these soluble hydrolysis products gradually increases the osmolarity of the extracellular medium surrounding the vesicles, leading to osmotic asymmetry across the membrane. This biochemical framework provides a quantitative basis for understanding membrane deformation, curvature generation, vesicle deflation, and budding. In addition to the specific starch--$\alpha$-amylase system studied here, our work uncovers a general mechanism by which external biochemical reactions control membrane shape transformations via osmotic coupling. Such enzyme-driven remodeling offers a simple yet powerful strategy for inducing dynamic structural changes in artificial cells. It may provide insight into primitive protocellular processes in which metabolic activity and membrane mechanics were inherently coupled.

papers.title: High-throughput, single-cell-encoded colony imaging reveals infection-linked heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Phenotypic heterogeneity within bacterial populations shapes adaptation, antibiotic tolerance, and infection dynamics, yet colony-level quantification remains difficult at scale and on dark/selective media. We present HeteroTyper, an automated, high-throughput time-lapse platform that measures colony phenotypes across >100 plates per run on both transparent and dark media. HeteroTyper includes a ready-to-use computational pipeline that can be deployed on common plate-imaging setups and across agar types, delivering appearance times as a proxy for lag times, growth trajectories, colony size, intensity, and morphology from routine image series. Automated counts closely matched manual counts, supporting accuracy and scalability. Using Yersinia pseudotuberculosis as a model, HeteroTyper resolves phenotypic heterogeneity in vitro, with early and late phases showing broader appearance time distributions than mid-log phases. It also reveals organ-specific heterogeneity in vivo, with mesenteric lymph node isolates displaying the broadest appearance time distributions compared to spleen and liver. Appearance time was negatively associated with final colony size and intensity, linking growth initiation to downstream colony outcomes. Together, these distribution-level measurements indicate that bacterial adaptation during infection is compartmentalized by tissue microenvironments and prior history, and establish HeteroTyper as a practical, generalizable route to quantify infection-relevant phenotypic diversity on solid media at routine, high throughput.

papers.title: RubisCO-encoding methanotrophs elicit a coordinated transcriptional response to carbon dioxide limitation.
papers.abstract: The methanotroph Methylococcus capsulatus encodes the carbon dioxide (CO2)-fixing enzyme ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (RubisCO), which, along with CO2 and methane (CH4), are required for growth of this bacterium. This unique, dual one-carbon metabolism is present in phylogenetically diverse methanotrophs and is likely widespread in nature, but the connection between organic and inorganic carbon metabolism in these methanotrophs is unclear. Here we used a systems approach to investigate the requisite role of CO2 in M. capsulatus metabolism and physiology. We show that atmospheric CO2 levels are sufficient for M. capsulatus cultivation, and that CO2 assimilation is linked to cellular redox balance. In the absence of CO2, M. capsulatus elicits a global transcriptional response that includes induction of RubisCO- and other inorganic carbon assimilation-encoding genes with a concomitant decrease in ribosome biogenesis and nitrogen assimilation genes typical of a bacterial stringent response. This CO2 starvation response balances biosynthesis with carbon availability. Genetic and biochemical evidence show that a LysR-type transcriptional regulator (CbbR) activates RubisCO and other CO2 assimilation gene transcription via direct promoter binding in response to elevated intracellular RubisCO substrate, ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate, in CO2-starved cells. These results offer insights into the essentiality of CO2 for M. capsulatus metabolism and establish a function for CbbR-family regulators in methanotrophs beyond their canonical association with CO2 fixation in autotrophic bacteria.

papers.title: gcat, its_a_scam: modular tools for single cell data processing and per-cellquality control
papers.abstract: Motivation: The era of designing bioinformatic pipelines using open source tools is giving way to monolithic, and often proprietary, tools designed for end-to-end analysis, especially in the context of single cell data. While these tools are convenient for going from sequencing data to an almost complete data analysis "in a few clicks", they can strongly limit data use beyond standard analyses Results: We developed Gene and Chromosome Analysis Toolkit (gcat) and It's a scam To Sell Another Single Cell Analysis Method (its_a_scam) for modular processing and quality control of single cell genomic data, freeing users from their reliance on proprietary tools. gcat is a C++ library for parsing genomic data and working with it over genomic coordinates. its_a_scam is built on top of gcat and provides a suite of tools for a wide range of single cell data processing and quality control. its_a_scam can be used in conjunction with commonly used open source tools for scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq count matrix generation, and for performing per-cell quality control directly from alignment files. These alignment-level per-cell metrics can be used for quality control of each cell or to understand celltype differences post-clustering or post-annotation. Using a peripheral blood mononuclear cell Multiome dataset, we show that the count matrices generated with the aid of its_a_scam are highly concordant with those generated by proprietary pipelines. The alignment metrics further demonstrate celltype differences in aligned genomic regions, metagene profiles, and genebody coverage. The modular nature of its_a_scam allows users to integrate it into their existing pipelines, while also enabling analysis beyond current pipelines. Availability: gcat (distributed as gcatlib) and its_a_scam are open source and available at https://github.com/rishvanth-kp/gcatlib and https://github.com/rishvanth-kp/its_a_scam. Detailed documentation is available at https://gcatlib.readthedocs.io/ and https://its-a-scam.readthedocs.io.

papers.title: Evaluating the Identifiability of Temporal Delay and Response Attenuation in Endometrial Decidualization
papers.abstract: Endometriosis is associated with impaired endometrial decidualization, yet conventional differential expres-sion analyses cannot readily distinguish delayed transcriptional activation from reduced response amplitude.These mechanisms may produce similar expression differences at individual time points while implying distinct biological interpretations. Establishing when they can be distinguished is therefore a computational identifiability problem.We implement an identifiability-aware analysis of temporal displacement and amplitude attenuation in longitudinal transcriptomic responses. The approach combines reference trajectories, constrained amplitude-only and amplitude-plus-delay models, analytical examples of observational equivalence, and simulation-based assessments of mechanism distinguishability. Held-out time-point evaluation and culture-level sensitivity analyses examine the stability of model-dependent conclusions.In GSE246591, a candidate-delay-dependent dynamic-range filter excluded 30.9 - 38.3% of initially dynamic features under a hypothetical 24-hour shift across four endometrial stromal cultures. A two-component diagnostic separating retained dynamic range from affine shape similarity revealed that small projection residuals can arise from either loss of observable dynamics or similarity of response shapes. These findings demonstrate why a single separation statistic may be insufficient for interpreting temporal identifiability.Complementary independent in vivo analyses provided biological context. In GSE51981, an endometrial progesterone-response-associated transcriptional score was reduced in endometriosis samples (phase-model estimate 0.155, 95% CI 0.222 to 0.088). GSE6364 showed a directionally consistent but statistically inconclusive difference (0.033, 95% CI 0.068 to 0.002). Neither observation independently establishes a temporal delay.Together, these results support selection-aware evaluation of temporal transcriptomic responses, distin-guishing structural ambiguity and loss of dynamic signal from evidence of a biological timing change.

papers.title: Effects of Reduced Watering Regimes on Hops Growth and Rhizospheric Microbial Communities
papers.abstract: Marked by shifts in historic climatic patterns, the effects of climate change have begun to disrupt biological life worldwide. In agricultural systems, the abiotic effects of climate change such as increased temperatures and reduced rainfall extend beyond crop yield and can be felt at the ecological level through microbial community shifts associated at the interface of the root/soil matrix, known as the rhizosphere. Shifts in rhizospheric community composition have been known to greatly impact crop health, making common garden studies examining the totality of climate related impacts on crops of the utmost importance. Using a combination of both phenotypic and metabarcoding data collected from the rhizosphere, we present a multi-month drought tolerance experiment using the cash crop Humulus lupulus (hops) and five of its cultivars; Cascade, Centennial, Chinook, Comet and CTZ. Statistical analyses of phenotypic data revealed that hops displayed a differential impact on reduced watering strategies while rhizospheric data revealed more consistent patterns of association between microbes and cultivar type. We hope results from our study can be used to further expand our knowledge on the impact of future climate change and necessary reduced watering strategies on agricultural systems, providing insight into potential mechanisms of response for drought tolerance in crop systems.

papers.title: FGF signaling induces disease-associated oligodendrocyte states and drives myelin pathology
papers.abstract: Myelin integrity is essential for normal central nervous system (CNS) function and is disrupted in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative disorders, including multiple sclerosis and Alzheimer's disease. In these settings, myelin-forming oligodendrocytes adopt a conserved disease-associated transcriptional state, termed disease-associated oligodendrocytes (DAOs). How DAOs arise, the signals that drive their induction, and whether they actively contribute to pathology remain poorly understood. Here we show that FGF signaling instructs mature oligodendrocytes to enter disease-associated states that are sufficient to trigger myelin pathology. By screening disease-linked secreted factors, we identify FGF1 and FGF2 as potent inducers of a DAO-like state in purified oligodendrocyte cultures, characterized by transcriptional reprogramming and myelin-membrane shedding. In vivo, activating oligodendrocyte FGF signaling is sufficient to elicit DAO programs and myelin disruption, whereas inhibiting FGF signaling suppresses DAO induction in a mouse model of multiple sclerosis. Finally, analysis of post-mortem multiple sclerosis tissue reveals a concordant DAO-like state associated with increased engagement of the FGF/FGFR axis. Collectively, these studies define a regulated mechanism of DAO formation linked to myelin disruption and position mature oligodendrocytes as active contributors to myelin pathology in CNS disease.

papers.title: Organ scale Three-dimensional atlas of developing pelvic innervation for the mouse lower urinary tract.
papers.abstract: Pelvic autonomic neurons are responsible for coordinating pelvic organ function, including storage and emptying of the urinary bladder. These neurons arise from sacral neural crest-derived progenitors which migrate to the developing urogenital sinus and undergo differentiation alongside pelvic organs, ultimately organizing into paired pelvic ganglia. To circumvent the complex morphological changes that occur during genitourinary organ development, we have optimized light sheet fluorescence microscopy imaging for three-dimensional mapping of the development and spatial distribution of pelvic autonomic neurons. To track neural crest progenitor migration, neurogenesis, and formation of mature pelvic ganglia morphology in mice, we imaged intact lower urinary tract tissue from mid-gestational to post-weaning stages at single-cell resolution. The resulting atlas identifies the precise timing and initial routes of neural crest progenitor migration, defines timing for pelvic ganglion neurogenesis, and reveals previously unrecognized neuronal cell bodies outside of the centralized pelvic ganglia structures. The analysis further highlights morphological changes to pelvic ganglion structure that occur in parallel with genitourinary maturation, including the divergence of the major pelvic ganglia and bladder-proximal accessory ganglia. This work acts as the first wholemount imaging atlas of pelvic innervation in the mouse spanning fetal and postnatal timepoints, and thus we present an informative tool for future studies of developmental neurourology and neurogenic bladder dysfunction.

papers.title: Evolution of Vesicle Shape Parameters Based on A Deep-Learning Based Image Analysis Framework Over Extended Time Periods
papers.abstract: A precise analysis of shape instabilities in cell-sized membrane compartments requires thorough quantification of the shape dynamics of individual components over extended periods. Herein, we have used phase-contrast microscopy to image giant unilamellar membrane vesicles (GUVs), which are widely used as model systems for cellular structures. GUVs were prepared in the fluid lamellar phase of 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine with and without cholesterol dissolved within a potato starch solution. The morphological changes and budding dynamics of individual GUVs with different chemical compositions were quantified using a deep-learning based image analysis framework over extended time periods, by using phase-contrast micrographs as input data. This automated framework integrates contour-based detection of the mother vesicle with precise segmentation of daughter compartments, thereby enabling explicit identification and tracking of mother and daughter vesicles at high temporal resolution. These findings further facilitate the measurement of the temporal evolution of vesicle morphometrics including area, and local membrane curvature during budding, that can be used as an input to develop computational models aimed at elucidating curvature-driven membrane remodeling in complex soft materials.

papers.title: Clustering instantaneous phase-locking states with a rank-two Bures-Wasserstein distance
papers.abstract: Instantaneous phase-locking (iPL) matrices, defined by the cosines of pairwise phase differences between band-limited signals, underpin widely used methods for time-resolved functional connectivity, including Leading Eigenvector Dynamics Analysis (LEiDA). Each iPL matrix has rank at most two and is fully characterized by its two nonzero eigenvalues and corresponding eigenvectors. Yet, existing methods retain different parts of this decomposition and compare them using distances that do not reflect the geometry of the underlying sample space. We show that weighting the two eigenvectors by the square roots of their eigenvalues recovers each channel's phase relative to the mean phase, and that optimal orthogonal Procrustes alignment of these weighted eigenvector pairs yields the Bures-Wasserstein distance between the corresponding iPL matrices. In EEG, where most channels oscillate nearly in phase, existing distances become insensitive to phase-lag size, whereas the Bures-Wasserstein distance preserves this sensitivity. In simulations, clustering with this distance recovered states differing in both lag size and spatial pattern that existing distances failed to distinguish.In resting-state EEG, it resolved distinct phase-gradient states that other methods merged into a single global in-phase state.

papers.title: The role of the fruitless P3 transcript in development in Drosophila melanogaster
papers.abstract: The generation of multiple transcripts from a single gene through alternative promoter usage and alternative splicing is a major source of functional diversity in eukaryotic genomes. The fruitless (fru) gene of Drosophila melanogaster is a classic example of transcript complexity, producing at least 15 transcript isoforms through the use of alternative promoters and terminal exons. While transcripts derived from the sex-specifically spliced P1 promoter have been extensively studied for their roles in sex determination and courtship behaviour, the functions of most non-sex-specific fru transcripts remain poorly understood. Previous studies suggested that transcripts originating from the P3 and/or P4 promoters may contribute to developmental viability, but their individual roles could not be resolved because available mutations disrupted multiple transcript classes simultaneously. Here, we used transcript-specific RNA interference (RNAi) and the Gal4/UAS system to investigate the function of fru P3 transcripts. Loss of P3 expression significantly increased developmental time to pupariation and resulted in complete lethality during pupal development despite normal survival to pupariation. Most mortality occurred during early and mid-pupal stages, indicating a critical requirement for P3-derived transcripts during metamorphosis. Notably, P3 knockdown did not phenocopy complete loss of fruitless, as knockdown individuals survived substantially later into development than fru null mutants, suggesting that additional fruitless transcript classes contribute essential functions during earlier developmental stages. Together, these findings establish an independent developmental role for the fru P3 transcript class and demonstrate that transcript-specific functions contribute substantially to the biological complexity of the fruitless locus.

papers.title: Paired-probe chemoproteomic strategy enables global site-resolved quantification of lysine redox states
papers.abstract: Site-specific quantification of lysine (Lys) redox states remains unexplored, as current approaches identify only a limited number of modification sites without determining their stoichiometry. Allysine, an oxidized form of Lys, provides a model posttranslational modification (PTM) for addressing this challenge by requiring selective enrichment and site-specific stoichiometric quantification. Here, we developed a quantitative chemoproteomic platform for paired redox-state isotopic stoichiometry mapping of lysine, termed PRISM-Lys. We used an Am-alkyne probe for allysine enrichment by reductive amination and developed a complementary Ald-alkyne probe to label Lys, with identical reactions generating the same chemical product. Coupling this paired-probe strategy with a quantitative chemoproteomic workflow enables global site-resolved quantification and stoichiometric analysis of Lys redox states across cells and tissues. Applied to ferroptosis, PRISM-Lys revealed bidirectional, site-selective remodeling of Lys oxidation events associated with ferroptotic progression. Together, PRISM-Lys establishes a paired-chemistry framework for global, site-resolved quantification of Lys redox states, providing a new quantitative perspective for investigating protein oxidation in biological systems.

papers.title: Lung Epithelial TLR7 is a Factor in Viral Replication and Pathogenesis
papers.abstract: Respiratory virus infections are the leading causes of morbidity and mortality of infants and the elderly worldwide. Currently it is not known how Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) vaccination of infants can cause enhancement of RSV disease, highlighting gaps in our understanding about how viruses like RSV interact with the immune system. Here we address this and show that ERK MAP kinase signaling from Toll-like Receptor-7 (TLR7) detection of RSV and influenza, but not human parainfluenza virus type 3 (HPIV3), infections in bronchial epithelial cells (BECs) drives replication of the viruses. Virus infection is detected by pattern recognition receptors like TLR7 that bind to single stranded RNA (ssRNA) viral replication intermediates in late endosomes. Here we report that TLR7 is expressed in BECs and detects RSV ssRNA, causing ERK MAP kinase signaling. RSV and influenza use this detection and signaling in BECs to drive its replication and infection, a mechanism that counters TLR7s role in antiviral defence. Experimental blockade of TLR7 binding or downstream signalling through ERK MAP kinase decreased RSV and influenza replication, but had no effect on HPIV3. RSV viral loads in mouse and human females were higher compared to males, consistent with higher sex-dependent expression of the TLR7 gene from two copies of the X chromosome in females. In a TLR7 gain of function mouse model there was a significant enhancement of RSV replication and RSV eosinophilic and Th2 disease markers like interleukin-5 (IL-5). In summary, TLR7 is expressed in human lung BECs in the lungs where it acts as a factor in RSV and influenza replication and disease pathogenesis. We propose that this is a major factor in determining the sex-disparity of viral disease.

papers.title: Developing synthetic auxin-based trans-kingdom signaling
papers.abstract: Synthetic trans-kingdom signaling systems with tunable transduction properties provide a unique avenue to explore how communication between organisms coordinate behaviors without the confounding complexity of natural systems. However, existing trans-kingdom signaling systems suffer from either toxic signal molecules, a need for rare precursors for signal generation, or transduction machinery which is either species-specific or cannot be easily tuned. This limits their capacity to be broadly applied across kingdoms and their utility as a model system to study trans-kingdom interactions. In this work we elucidate the design principles for a trans-kingdom signaling system based on the plant phytohormone, Indole 3-Acetic Acid (auxin), that overcomes these challenges. We demonstrate how auxin biosynthesis can be engineered into a model sender organism, the cyanobacteria Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942, and how this signal can be tuned with low leak and high dynamic range. We also show these signals can be connected to gene expression using tunable synthetic auxin-responsive signaling systems across multiple kingdoms. We demonstrate that S. elongatus generated auxin signals can tune gene expression in co-cultured Saccharomyces cerevisiae via auxin-induced degradation. Additionally, we show that when the S. elongatus are associated with the roots of the model plant, Arabidopsis thaliana, the auxin they generate can control gene expression via auxin-responsive synthetic transcription factors expressed from the plants genome. Taken together, our results demonstrate the design principles for a tunable auxin-based trans-kingdom signaling system that can be broadly applied across species.

papers.title: Distinct patterns of multisensory integration underly the expression of flavor preferences and aversions in rats
papers.abstract: Flavor is an inherently multisensory experience, combining gustatory and retronasal odor signals during consumption. Previous work has shown that rats weight taste and smell components of flavor mixture solutions to express flavor preferences. However, a comprehensive quantitative understanding of taste-smell integration is lacking. Here, we evaluated the validity of the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) framework for explaining multisensory integration of taste and smell signals toward hedonic flavor judgments. MLE is a dominant framework for explaining multisensory integration in a wide variety of contexts, and states that components of a mixture are weighted according to their relative reliability, resulting in more reliable multisensory judgments. In our experiment, rats expressed preferences for taste, odor and taste+odor solutions in a series of two-bottle preference tests featuring an unpalatable odor component (amyl acetate), and either a palatable taste component (sucrose) or an unpalatable taste component (citric acid). Taste reliability was experimentally varied by presenting taste components at two different concentrations. Reliability of animals' preference judgements was quantified as the variance in preference across repetitions of the same conditions in the same animals. Our results confirm that preferences for mixtures featuring a palatable taste can be described as a weighted average of the component preferences where the weights depend on the relative reliability of the components-a finding that is in line with the MLE framework. However-contrary to MLE-component weighting does not increase the reliability of multisensory preference judgments themselves. In addition, preferences for taste+smell mixtures featuring an unpalatable taste follow a qualitatively different pattern: taste and smell components are combined to enhance flavor rejection judgements. These results demonstrate that the multisensory integrative principles underlying flavor preference differ from other multisensory domains and depend on the valence of the flavor components.

papers.title: Histopathological and virus-associated features of Boid Inclusion Body Disease in Boa constrictor
papers.abstract: Boid inclusion body disease (BIBD) is a reptarenavirus-induced fatal disease of boid snakes that, while diagnosed with ease due to the pathognomonic intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies (IB), is not yet fully characterized pathomorphologically and with regards to its pathogenesis. The present study retrospectively investigated a random cohort of 50 captive male and female boa constrictors of variable age (neonate to 25 years) for histopathological changes and in situ viral protein (nucleoprotein, NP, and glycoprotein 2, GP2) expression patterns. IB formation and NP expression were scored semiquantitatively. The vast majority of snakes (42/50; 84%) exhibited histopathological changes; these mainly (39/42; 93%) represented inflammatory processes that most frequently affected the gastrointestinal tract. Overall, IB and NP scores were significantly higher in the more recent cases (2020-2025) compared to the older cases (2000-2003). NP scores did not differ between age groups or sex, but were lower in animals with clinical signs and higher in those with histopathological changes. No statistically significant association was found between NP scores and inflammatory processes, neither in general nor in individual organs. GP2 expression, as an indicator of virion assembly, was less consistent than NP expression and generally restricted to individual cells with and without IBs. There was no histological evidence of overt damage in infected cells. Jointly, the results indicate different phases of restrictive and systemic viral replication that are not directly associated with pathological processes and/or clinical signs.

papers.title: Genetic disruption of cutaneous de novo glucocorticoid synthesis: a CRISPR-Cas9 CYP11B1-knockout human epidermal model
papers.abstract: Human skin functions as both a physical barrier and a neuroendocrine and steroidogenic organ. Glucocorticoids (GC) synthesized in the skin help to maintain skin immune homeostasis and to mediate responses to environmental stressors. Cutaneous GC synthesis has so far been disrupted only pharmacologically, with inhibitors that do not discriminate CYP11B1 from its close paralogue CYP11B2, or genetically in mouse keratinocytes, so the consequences of blocking this pathway in human keratinocytes remain untested. Here, we disrupted de novo GC synthesis by knocking out the CYP11B1 gene using CRISPR-Cas9, thereby interrupting the terminal enzymatic process of converting 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol in mitochondria. Two independent knockout clones were established, one carrying a 28 bp deletion spanning the start codon and one carrying a multi-exon deletion. Both clones reconstituted stratified 3D epidermal models as in wild-type models, indicating that loss of CYP11B1 does not by itself impair epidermal differentiation. Wild-type models responded with increased CYP11B1 transcript abundance and immunofluorescence signal, whereas both knockout clones retained a UVB-inducible transcript signal but showed no detectable CYP11B1 protein, confirming loss of the protein product at the tissue level. This work provides, to our knowledge, the first human keratinocyte model carrying a genomically defined block in de novo GC synthesis, and a tissue-level platform for resolving the role of keratinocyte-derived GC in epidermal homeostasis and environmental stress responses.

papers.title: Optimization of a Subcutaneous Epithelioid Hemangioendothelioma Xenograft Model for Evaluation of Preclinical Therapeutics
papers.abstract: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma (EHE) is an ultra-rare vascular sarcoma characterized by an unpredictable clinical trajectory and lack of established standard-of-care treatment regimens. Despite the pressing need for effective therapeutic strategies, the scarcity of clinically relevant preclinical models remains a major barrier to drug development. To address this challenge, we used a patient-derived human EHE cell line to optimize and validate a subcutaneous xenograft model in mice. Optimization of cell-inoculation density revealed that injection of high cell densities was associated with adverse systemic responses and primary tumour growth kinetics unsuitable for longitudinal drug screening. In contrast, inoculation of low, sub-million cell densities generated reproducible xenografts that followed classical sigmoidal growth kinetics, providing a suitable therapeutic window for comparative treatment studies. Subsequent histopathological analysis confirmed that the tumours were highly proliferative and retained key features of EHE pathology, including expression of the EHE-associated markers ERG and CAMTA1. Treatment response validation further demonstrated sensitivity to mTOR inhibition, a characteristic preserved from the original patient-derived sample.
