Green chromides retained stable conspecific preferences despite contrasting light environments. Opsins exhibited plasticity, with long wavelength-sensitive opsin (LWS) increasing under blue light, whereas short wavelength-sensitive opsins remained unchanged. Additionally, Cyp27c1 expression declined under blue light, suggesting a potential shift towards increased A1 chromophore utilization. Together, these findings suggest that green chromides undergo multiple molecular modifications under contrasting light environments, whereas maintaining stable social behaviours, demonstrating the cross-talk between the two is not straightforward. Overall, these results highlight that unraveling the underlying proximate mechanisms of behavior is highly intricate, involving multiple pathways, starting from perception (at the retinal level) to post-processing of the stimulus.

papers.title: In vivo effects of inducible transgene expression of the age-associated glycogenes St6gal1 and Man1a on epidermal homeostasis
papers.abstract: Glycosylation of cell-surface proteins plays several essential roles in cell-matrix interactions and receptor signaling, thereby contributing to tissue homeostasis and aging. In aged mouse skin, epidermal stem cells exhibit increased levels of a2,6-sialylated complex-type N-glycans alongside upregulation of glycogenes such as St6gal1 and Man1a; however, the functional importance of these glycosylation changes in vivo remains largely unknown. Here, we generated doxycycline-inducible transgenic mice expressing the age-related glycogenes St6gal1 and Man1a, either individually or in combination, using ubiquitous and epidermis-specific drivers. Lectin-based analyses with SNA and rHeltuba demonstrated corresponding alterations in glycosylation patterns in these mice. Transgenic Man1a induction reduced epidermal proliferation and epidermal thickness. In contrast, St6gal1 induction caused splenomegaly and elevated expression of inflammatory signature genes in the skin but did not measurably alter epidermal proliferation or morphology. Double transgenic mice exhibited a hybrid phenotype combining inflammatory and proliferative impairments, although comparison of ubiquitous and epidermis-specific induction indicated that the observed skin phenotypes depended on the epidermal expression of the transgenes. An SNA lectin-based pull-down assay followed by mass spectrometry identified candidate a2,6-sialylated proteins, including integrin family members, junctional proteins, and surface receptors, following induction of St6gal1 and Man1a. Together, these findings suggest that increased expression of the age-associated glycogenes St6gal1 and Man1a perturbs distinct aspects of epidermal homeostasis in vivo and identify candidate glycoproteins that may mediate these effects.

papers.title: Linking dynamic photosynthetic traits to biomass: a functional data framework that pinpoints when photosynthesis limits growth
papers.abstract: Photosynthesis responds rapidly to environmental changes, such as light fluctuations, and these responses affect how much carbon plants gain over time. Modelling genetic variation in photosynthesis over time opens a route for selection on photosynthetic performance. High-throughput chlorophyll fluorescence has enabled measurements of photosynthetic processes at high time resolution, yet methods to model the temporal and genetic variation in these time-series data remain scarce. Here, we combined splines and functional principal component analysis (FPCA) to model genotype-specific trajectories of fluorescence traits and capture their main variation in a few components. We applied this approach to 412 Arabidopsis thaliana MAGIC lines under daily sinusoidal and fluctuating light. The first component captured differences in overall trait level, whereas subsequent components captured differences in how trait values changed across days, mainly in the early growing period. These component scores predicted final dry weight reasonably well (average r = 0.7224 under sinusoidal and 0.82 under fluctuating light). Information on changes across days added most predictive value when measurements were limited to a few days. Time-varying coefficients revealed that the associations between fluorescence traits and dry weight changed over time. For most traits, these associations were strongest early in the growing period. Our framework thus shows not only which photosynthetic processes are associated with biomass, but also when. This insight will point to the period in which photosynthesis limits growth and to the traits beneficial to select for.

papers.title: Isolation of functional endogenous clathrin-coated vesicles and in vitro reconstitution of pure clathrin cages
papers.abstract: Clathrin-coated vesicles (CCVs) mediate key endocytic trafficking events, and dysfunction of CCVs is linked to multiple human diseases. Conventional centrifugation-based purification protocols can enrich endogenous CCVs but fail to eliminate intraluminal smooth vesicles (SVs) and co-isolated exosomes; these lipid contaminants reduce sample homogeneity and hinder high-resolution structural and proteomic analysis. Here, we present an integrated workflow to isolate biologically active endogenous CCVs from porcine brain and reconstitute homogeneous, SV-free clathrin cages. Crude CCVs are first enriched by differential and sucrose density gradient centrifugation to deplete the majority of exosomes. Clathrin cages are then depolymerized under alkaline conditions, allowing separation of soluble clathrin and adaptor proteins from SVs and residual lipid contaminants via ultracentrifugation. Purified coat proteins are reassembled in vitro into uniform clathrin cages. Functional assays confirm that purified CCVs retain Auxilin-Hsc70-dependent uncoating activity, and the enclosed SVs carry active vATPase proton pumps. This approach produces well-defined samples suitable for cryo-electron microscopy and mass spectrometry-based investigation of clathrin assembly and disassembly.

papers.title: Intestinal molecular siphoning by engineered bacterial spores for non-systemic treatment of nicotine addiction
papers.abstract: Eradicating toxic small molecules from the body typically requires the administrations of therapeutic agents for systemic circulation and tissue distribution, resulting in inevitable adverse events from off-target effects. Here, we propose a intestinal molecular siphoning approach for treating diseases caused by toxic substances, in which enzymatic degradation of a toxic substance in the intestinal lumen serves as a driving force for the diffusion of the toxic substance from blood to gut, and continuous elimination of the toxic substance in the gut could effectively ease substance dependence. Using nicotine as a model substance, a live bacterial system was constructed by displaying a trypsin-resistant nicotine oxidase on the surface of Bacillus subtilis spores, and encapsulating in enteric-coated microspheres for gastric protection and targeted intestinal release. After oral treatments with the live bacterial system in mice, peak concentrations of nicotine in blood and brain were remarkably reduced compared to controls. Moreover, the live bacterial system could effectively attenuate nicotine addiction by suppressing dopamine reward surges to reverse withdrawal hyperalgesia, preventing the upregulation of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, and alleviating anxiety-like behaviors. These findings show the potential of intestinal molecular siphoning as a target-independent therapeutic strategy for lowering circulating toxic substances through non-systemic enzyme reprogramming.

papers.title: Naturalistic recall preserves temporal specificity despite cortical feature reorganization
papers.abstract: Although sensory input arrives in a largely continuous stream, recall is temporally compressed, discontinuous, and often structured as events. However, the temporal specificity of recall-related neural activity within events, and the separation and cortical organization of recalled features relative to perception, remain poorly characterized. We analyzed functional MRI data recorded during viewing and free recall of an episode of Sherlock. A data-driven alignment between viewing and recall data identified neural recapitulation of corresponding narrative events and revealed information that distinguished moments within events, particularly in the association cortex. Features ranging from low-level visual to semantic information predicted recall reinstatement. However, differences in predictive performance among feature levels became smaller during recall, and their organization along the cortical sensory-to-association gradient reversed relative to viewing. Thus, temporal specificity within events can be preserved despite substantial reorganization of feature representations across the cortex during recall.

papers.title: High-fat diet promotes exhaustion-associated T-cell remodeling across vascular and lymphoid tissues in atherosclerosis-prone mice
papers.abstract: Background: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease driven by lipid accumulation and immune dysregulation. How chronic dietary lipid exposure reshapes T-cell states across vascular and lymphoid tissues, and whether these changes resolve after dietary normalization, remains incompletely defined. This study examined diet-associated T-cell remodeling and the contribution of macrophage-mediated stimulation. Methods: ApoE-deficient mice received a vegetarian diet (VD) or high-fat diet (HFD) for 12 or 24 weeks; a dietary reversal group received HFD for 12 weeks followed by VD for 12 weeks. CD45-positive cells from aorta, blood, spleen, lymph nodes, and bone marrow underwent single-cell RNA sequencing with matched T-cell receptor sequencing. T cell states were annotated using canonical markers, and exhaustion- and naive-associated programs were quantified using UCell scores. Analysis assessed T-cell composition, clonal expansion, and predicted macrophage-T cell communication, with splenic flow-cytometric validation. Results: HFD was associated with enrichment of exhaustion-associated states, with the highest exhaustion scores in the aorta. At 24 weeks, the pooled exhausted-cell proportion was 15.7% under HFD versus 10.6% under VD. Dietary reversal restored this proportion to 10.6%, while residual transcriptional changes persisted in a tissue-dependent manner. Flow cytometry corroborated increased inhibitory receptor expression and co-expression. Aortic macrophages exhibited inflammatory and antigen-presentation programs alongside increased predicted communication with T cells. Aortic T-cell activation and clonal expansion accompanied these changes, and clonotype size correlated with exhaustion score (Spearman correlation coefficient = 0.57, p = 0.029). Conclusion: Chronic HFD is associated with multicompartment T-cell remodeling, with prominent vascular exhaustion-associated programs and tissue-dependent recovery after dietary normalization. These findings suggest that dietary lipid exposure may leave a durable adaptive immune imprint across organs during atherosclerosis.

papers.title: Live Droplet Single-Cell RNA Sequencing
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has emerged as one of the most influential methods of the past decade, enabling the dissection of cellular heterogeneity and the discovery of rare cell types. However, most workflows require cell lysis and provide only terminal snapshots, limiting their ability to capture dynamic cellular trajectories and temporal variations within the same cell. Herein, we present Live Droplet single-cell RNA sequencing (Live D-seq), a technology that enables scalable transcriptome-wide profiling of individual living cells over time. Live D-seq combines longitudinal intracellular sampling of live, barcoded cells with particle-templated emulsification and barcoded hydrogel beads, enabling repeated samples from the same cell lineage to be linked across time points. We showcase Live D-seq's capabilities by (i) demonstrating minimal cross-contamination in cross-species experiments, (ii) precisely mapping cellular barcodes to hydrogel bead barcodes, and (iii) tracking epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition dynamics in A549 cells over time. Altogether, Live D-seq enables repeated, non-destructive measurements of gene expression in the same single cells, offering a framework to study longitudinal single-cell biology in health and disease.

papers.title: The behaviour bends, the code holds: working-memory category information in the multiple-demand network across graded interruption
papers.abstract: Protecting working memory (WM) from interference is essential for goal-directed behaviour, yet its neural mechanisms remain unclear. The multiple-demand (MD) network - a set of frontoparietal regions recruited by diverse cognitive demands - is a candidate system for maintaining WM content under interference. We examined how the MD network represents a memorandum when an unrelated task interrupts maintenance. Participants memorised an image of a tool or animal and, during the delay, performed a digit task whose difficulty was parametrically varied (passive, easy, hard), allowing us to test how task engagement and associated cognitive demands affected concurrently maintained information. Using fMRI and multivariate pattern analysis, we decoded the maintained category (tool vs. animal) from 13 MD regions and early visual cortex. Behaviourally, interruption reduced recall accuracy, while the most demanding interrupter slowed responses. Neurally, category information was present during the delay, most strongly in visual cortex and bilateral intraparietal sulcus. This information was unaffected by task engagement (active vs. passive), consistently across decoding accuracy and cross-validated Mahalanobis (crossnobis) distance, with Bayesian evidence supporting the null effect. Increasing the demand of the active interrupter, however, produced a modest, network-wide reduction in crossnobis distance that was not detectable in decoding accuracy. Together, these findings reveal a dissociation between the behavioural costs of interruption and the neural representation of maintained category information. Although interruption impaired recall, engaging in an interrupter did not measurably alter category-level information in the MD network or visual cortex. Increasing the demand of the interrupter produced only a modest, network-wide reduction in representational distance, without affecting decoding accuracy, suggesting that the behavioural costs of interruption may not be fully explained by changes in the categorical representation of the memorandum.

papers.title: HiFiTaxa: a reproducible analysis pipeline for full length 16S rRNA gene and ITS amplicon sequencing from PacBio reads
papers.abstract: Long-read amplicon sequencing profiles communities at high resolution, but taxonomic accuracy depends on the reference, classifier and the parameters used. Here, we present HiFiTaxa, a reproducible, single command Nextflow pipeline for PacBio HiFi 16S rRNA gene and fungal ITS amplicons. It builds versioned references from current GTDB and UNITE releases and supports Bayesian lowest common ancestor (BLCA) and naive Bayes (NB) classifiers and the read level profilers Emu (16S rRNA gene) and EMITS (ITS). We benchmarked them on mock communities and on holdouts with 10% of GTDB or UNITE databases sequences withheld. On the 16S rRNA gene mock of 20 species, BLCA detected all 20 species and reported two false positives, NB detected 17 and reported none, and Emu detected all 20 and reported eight. In the GTDB holdout, for taxa represented in the reference, BLCA reached 80.0% species level accuracy against 48.1% for the exact matching species step of NB. However, NB produced fewer incorrect assignments for taxa absent from the reference. On fungal ITS, BLCA had slightly higher holdout accuracy at species level(54.7%) against 52.2% for NB. NB was more conservative for novel taxa, and EMITS detected the most mock species. HiFiTaxa therefore offers a single reproducible workflow that uses current GTDB and UNITE releases and enables users to choose between different classifier algorithms depending on their needs.

papers.title: Large-scale AI-guided discovery of antifreeze peptides reveals functional tandem-repeat architectures
papers.abstract: Despite growing demand for biocompatible materials that regulate ice crystallization in cryopreservation, antifreeze peptide discovery remains constrained by limited candidate sequence diversity and reliance on known protein scaffolds. Here, we establish an AI-guided discovery framework integrating multimodal antifreeze protein prediction, generative sequence expansion and local sequence-pattern analysis. AFPFusionLM combines protein sequence and structure-aware representations, achieving an AUROC of 0.937 and an AUPRC of 0.957 on an independent reference set. Antifreeze-domain-adapted protein sequence generation and multimodel consensus screening of UniProt, glacier metagenomes and generated sequences yielded 87,305 candidate protein records. Large-scale sequence analysis revealed recurring periodic sequence architectures across multiple candidate protein clusters, enabling the identification of short-peptide families with shared repeat features and their natural variants. Experimental evaluation revealed ice recrystallization inhibition activity in multiple peptides from repeat-associated families, with inhibitory effects comparable to or greater than those of reference peptides reported in the literature. Cell-based experiments using a representative peptide-containing formulation also supported its cryoprotective potential under reduced-DMSO conditions. These findings show that large-scale sequence exploration can reveal function-associated peptide sequence architectures, providing a research framework for the systematic discovery and subsequent optimization of antifreeze peptides.

papers.title: A DNM1L GTPase Effector Domain Deletion Causes Intermediate Defects in Peroxisomal and Mitochondrial Dynamics and Reveals a Targetable Metabolic Vulnerability
papers.abstract: DNM1L encodes dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1), a key GTPase regulating mitochondrial and peroxisomal dynamics. Pathogenic DNM1L variants are associated with a broad spectrum of neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders, with phenotypic severity varying by affected protein domain. While variants in the GTPase domain are typically associated with milder phenotypes and middle-domain variants with severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, the functional impact of GTPase effector domain (GED) variants remains less defined. Here, we describe four individuals harboring a recurrent heterozygous GED deletion (L700del) presenting with movement disorders and lacking severe infantile encephalopathy, consistent with an intermediate clinical phenotype. Patient-derived fibroblasts exhibited tubular peroxisomes and enlarged mitochondria, while Drosophila models demonstrated that DNM1LL700del has intermediate functional effects that were more pronounced than those of a GTPase-domain variant A192E but less severe than those of the middle-domain variant G350R. Comparison with another GED variant, Y691C, further demonstrated variant-specific differences in severity within the GED. Metabolic stress assays showed that L700del fibroblasts exhibited impaired growth under galactose conditions, consistent with increased vulnerability under conditions dependent on mitochondrial oxidative metabolism. Bezafibrate, a PPAR agonist that promotes mitochondrial biogenesis, partially rescued this growth defect. Together, these findings support a functional allelic spectrum in DNM1L-associated disease in which protein domain contributes to, but does not completely determine, functional severity. L700del represents an intermediate-strength allele associated with a movement-disorder phenotype and a pharmacologically modifiable metabolic vulnerability.

papers.title: Matching Corticospinal and Cortical Excitability along the motor cortex: TMS-EMG-EEG study
papers.abstract: There is still no consensus on how to choose intensities for transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS). The resting motor threshold (RMT), the intensity needed to evoke muscle contractions in the contralateral limb muscles, is a robust muscle-specific index of corticospinal excitability. RMT from one of the hand muscles is commonly used as a reference for TMS neuromodulation interventions and TMS-electroencephalography (EEG) studies. However, it only provides an indirect measure of cortical excitability, and even for the primary motor cortex (M1), we do not understand how cortical and corticospinal excitability correspond to each other. Indeed, it remains unclear whether cortical responses to TMS follow similar location-dependent patterns along the M1, and whether subthreshold stimulation can reliably engage cortical circuits relevant to motor output. Combining TMS with electromyography (EMG) and EEG, TMS-EMG-EEG, enables simultaneous assessment of corticospinal and cortical excitability to answer these questions. We investigated how cortical excitability thresholds (CETs, measured with EEG), relate to corticospinal excitability thresholds (RMTs, measured with EMG) at the hand, arm, and leg hotspots along the M1 in 24 subjects. RMTs and CETs were strongly correlated, and both increased from hand to arm to leg. CETs were generally lower than RMTs, indicating that subthreshold stimulation was enough to evoke robust early TMS evoked potentials (TEPs). Within subjects, CETs differed from the corresponding RMTs at all three M1 hotspots, and this difference increased from hand to leg representations. The findings of the present study argue against using a default hand-muscle RMT to set cortical excitability dosage along the M1 and beyond. Online TMS-EEG can enable real-time dosing and could improve stimulation precision, efficiency, and generalizability, but the site-specific variability calls for adaptive control.

papers.title: Competence repression by the SPβ prophage in Bacillus subtilis revealed by transcriptomics across culture conditions
papers.abstract: Prophages are near-ubiquitous in bacterial genomes, yet their effects on host physiology are typically assayed under a narrow range of laboratory conditions, mostly involving DNA-damaging agents or physical and chemical stress. This leaves open the question of which ecological and physiological conditions trigger prophage-host interaction, and whether the outcome benefits the host or the prophage. Here, we used publicly available transcriptomic data to investigate conditions promoting prophage-host interaction in Bacillus subtilis. This analysis identified that competence strongly induces prophage gene expression. To further investigate the role of competence, we used two sets of B. subtilis strains: a natural SP{beta} lysogen strain and its cured counterpart, and a natural non-lysogenic strain and the same strain lysogenised with SP{beta}. Under competence-inducing conditions, both lysogen strains showed lower expression of the competence genes compared with their non-lysogenic counterparts. This result was corroborated by transformation assays that showed consistently lower transformation efficiency in the lysogen strains, and by fluorescence microscopy using a transcriptional reporter for the late competence gene. Because competence is a principal route for horizontal gene transfer in B. subtilis, prophage repression of the competence programme constrains host DNA uptake and evolvability. More broadly, these results show that mining public transcriptomes for condition effects can guide experimental effort towards prophage-host phenotypes that conventional laboratory conditions would miss.

papers.title: Unilateral naris occlusion with custom-made plugs for reversible olfactory deprivation in juvenile and adult mice
papers.abstract: Deprivation paradigms that reduce environmental input have been successfully applied across multiple species and sensory modalities, including vision, audition, somatosensation, and olfaction in order to understand how neurons and circuits respond to loss of sensory input. One notable advantage of studying sensory deprivation in the rodent olfactory system is the ease and control with which smell loss can be induced. Various methods of olfactory deprivation have long been available and rely on blocking a nostril, either through invasive and often non-reversible approaches such as chemical ablation or surgical procedures, or through reversible approaches such as unilateral naris occlusion using custom-made nose plugs. Here, we provide a systematic description of this well-established method, including its construction from commercially available materials, procedures, validation, and reliability in post-weaning mice, thereby providing a detailed and reproducible framework for controlled, reversible olfactory deprivation.

papers.title: The Pregnane X Receptor (PXR) contributes to phenotypic plasticity and modulates the sensitivity to targeted therapies in melanoma
papers.abstract: The challenge in treating advanced metastatic melanoma lies in the development of therapeutic resistance and the risk of recurrence. Understanding the mechanisms underlying tumor adaptation to treatment is therefore crucial, as they can directly influence therapeutic efficacy. Tolerance to targeted therapies may be influenced by drug transport and metabolism within tumors, processes regulated by numerous genes under the transcriptional control of the nuclear receptor PXR (Pregnane X Receptor, NR1I2). We revealed, for the first time, significant and heterogeneous expression of PXR in human melanoma samples. We previously showed that PXR can be activated by BRAF inhibitors (BRAFi), but not by MEK inhibitors (MEKi), which are currently used in combination for the treatment of BRAF-V600E-mutated melanoma. Here, we investigated whether PXR expression influences melanoma cell sensitivity to MAPK pathway inhibitors. Using BRAF-mutated human melanoma cell lines, we showed that stable PXR expression sensitizes cells to combined BRAFi/MEKi treatment. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed that PXR expression is associated with the upregulation of several phenotypic markers, with MITF identified as a major regulator in untreated PXR-overexpressing cells. These findings suggest that PXR promotes a shift toward a melanocytic phenotype, which is associated with increased sensitivity to BRAFi/MEKi treatment. Characterization of the PXR-associated transcriptional signature in melanoma may therefore have translational value for identifying patients more likely to benefit from targeted therapies and support the development of PXR as a predictive biomarker of therapeutic response.

papers.title: Microtubules coordinate with actin assembly and disassembly to elongate cortical actin cables
papers.abstract: The coordination of actin filament elongation, bundling and turnover within bundled actin structures is poorly understood. Nurse cells extend bundles of actin filaments (cables) from the cortex during Drosophila oogenesis. We previously showed that cable assembly requires a developmentally-regulated microtubule (MT) network. Here we demonstrate that MTs coordinate with actin filament assembly and disassembly to promote the persistent elongation of actin cables. Disrupting the MT network caused actin cables to detach from the cortex and become free in the cytoplasm. The subsequent fate of those free cables, shrinking over time or maintaining a stable length, depended on the MT manipulation. Furthermore, maintaining cortical continuity and persistent cable elongation requires a regulated imbalance between filament assembly and disassembly. Favoring disassembly caused cable detachment and shrinkage while reducing disassembly allowed free cables to continue elongating in the cytoplasm. Our results also suggest that both filament assembly and disassembly occur at the cortical filament barbed-ends protected from excessive disassembly by Capping Protein.

papers.title: SeverYX: An ensemble framework for robust variant severity classification
papers.abstract: Accurate interpretation of genetic variants in clinical genomics depends on reconciling multiple computational predictors that often disagree or provide incomplete evidence. We present SeverYX, a transparent, rule-based ensemble framework that consolidates conservation, splicing, and functional-impact predictors into a three-tier severity classification ('High', 'Medium', 'Low') through an effect-aware decision architecture. We benchmarked SeverYX against a curated ClinVar dataset of 270,208 MANE-transcript variants (86,161 pathogenic/likely pathogenic, 184,047 benign/likely benign), stratified by molecular consequence, review status, and haploinsufficiency. The baseline configuration achieved 97.6% concordance with ClinVar; at a fixed High cut, 90.0% of pathogenic and 2.0% of benign variants were assigned High. Concordance was highest for loss-of-function variants and lowest for non-coding and unclassified pathogenic variants, reflecting known gaps in current predictive tools. Systematic threshold optimization, combined with the addition of AlphaMissense and REVEL as missense predictors, raised overall concordance to 98.7%, reduced the benign High rate to 0.4% (at a cost of pathogenic High sensitivity falling to 88.3%), and improved the Matthews correlation coefficient from 0.895 to 0.908. These results show that SeverYX offers a transparent, reproducible and extensible approach for consolidating heterogeneous variant-effect evidence into clinically interpretable severity calls, and a scalable path for incorporating future predictive models into genomic interpretation workflows.

papers.title: The YjfJ protein is the effector of a second PspA/VIPP1 system that is widespread in the Gammaproteobacteria
papers.abstract: Maintaining the integrity of the cytoplasmic membrane is essential for bacterial cell survival. Unsurprisingly, prokaryotes have evolved conserved mechanisms by which they sense, maintain, and repair membrane integrity in response to stress. The phage shock protein (Psp) is one such system, understood primarily through work undertaken in the Gammaproteobacterial species Escherichia coli and Yersinia enterocolitica. The system utilises an effector, PspA, alongside accessory proteins that sense stress and recruit PspA to damaged membranes. Homologues of PspA - part of the PspA/VIPP1 family - are found in a variety of bacterial phyla. Although most work in the Gammaproteobacteria has concerned the canonical Psp response, there have been descriptions of non-canonical PspA/VIPP1-containing systems that warrant further genomic analysis. By analysing the PspA/VIPP1 content of a diverse selection of Gammaproteobacterial genomes, we reveal the existence of two phylogenetically distinct subtypes of PspA/VIPP1 proteins, PspA- and YjfJ-like, which are found at similar frequencies. The YjfJ-like proteins are not only a novel subtype of PspA/VIPP1, having their own unique set of accessory proteins, but in some species, such as the ESKAPE pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa, comprise the only PspA/VIPP1-containing system. Our study positions the YjfJ-like containing systems on equal footing with the PspA system in terms of their conservation and distribution in the Gammaproteobacteria. This suggests that studies into the biological functions of YjfJ-like proteins would be well-justified from their unique presence in some important human pathogens.

papers.title: Connectome structure constrains neural activity across scales
papers.abstract: Connectomes can be represented at many resolutions, but coarse-graining risks discarding structure relevant to neural dynamics. Here we ask at what resolution a connectome preserves what it predicts about neural activity. In C. elegans, direct synaptic connectivity poorly predicts whether stimulating one neuron evokes a response in another. A parameter-free predictor based on paths through the connectome performs substantially better, with most predictive information carried by two-step paths and by the arrangement rather than the number of connections. Coarse-graining neurons into biological cell classes preserves these predictions despite discarding path structure, whereas random partitions degrade them. Connectivity alone identifies alternative coarse-grainings that preserve prediction down to about nine groups corresponding to nervous-system subsystems. Partitions inferred from newly hatched animals preserve adult predictions, and lineage-based partitions in Drosophila preserve path structure better than random coarse-graining. Functional prediction can therefore survive at resolutions far coarser than those required to preserve structure.

papers.title: An orphan LuxR regulator controls plant developmental reprogramming during interaction with Novosphingobium resinovorum HR1a
papers.abstract: Rhizoremediation depends on productive plant/pollutant-degrading microorganism interactions, yet the bacterial regulatory mechanisms that shape host responses remain poorly understood. We investigated the role of the previously uncharacterized orphan LuxR874 from the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) degrading bacterium Novosphingobium resinovorum HR1a, in the modulation of plant physiology. Bacterial transcriptomics revealed that LuxR874 controls the expression of genes associated with aromatic and sugar metabolism, and acylCoA related functions. Inactivation of luxR874 altered bacterial responses without affecting root colonization, suggesting that this regulator contributes to the physiological state required to elicit host responses. In gnotobiotic systems, HR1a induced a root phenotype characterized by reduced primary root elongation, increased root thickness, and enhanced root hair formation. These alterations were attenuated in the luxR874 mutant and restored by complementation despite similar colonization levels among strains. Plant RNA-seq analyses revealed extensive host transcriptional reprogramming, including activation of developmental regulators, hormone associated pathways, cell wall remodeling genes, and oxidative stress responses. In contrast, plants inoculated with the luxR874 mutant displayed a weaker transcriptional response resembling the non-inoculated state. Functional analyses supported LuxR874-dependent activation of reactive oxygen species and ethylene related pathways. Our results reveal an unexpected role for an orphan LuxR regulator in coordinating multi-level responses during a rhizoremediation-relevant plant microbe interaction.

papers.title: Perturbation-induced gene programs map the hidden regulatory architecture of complex diseases
papers.abstract: Steady-state molecular profiles incompletely capture the regulatory programs through which genetic variation influences complex disease, particularly programs that emerge only when cells are perturbed. Here, we introduce Perturbscape, a computational framework that learns multiscale gene programs for individual perturbations in a CRISPR Perturb-seq screen using linear and nonlinear contrastive approaches alongside complementary program-learning methods, and integrates them with human genetics to prioritize disease-relevant genes, perturbations and downstream regulatory pathways. Across 15,859 perturbation-by-context profiles from 7 Perturb-seq systems and 53 complex diseases and traits (mean GWAS N=291K), perturbation-induced programs showed up to 4.3-fold higher heritability informativeness than analogous steady-state multi-tissue gene prioritization, and retained significant conditional heritability informativeness across all 34 matched cell system-trait comparisons after accounting for steady-state prioritization. Preserving perturbation-specific programs further yielded 2.5-5.3-fold higher trait relevance scores than programs derived from control cells, pooled perturbations or differential-expression summaries. In K562, Perturbscape-prioritized genes showed stronger enrichment for rare-variant burden genes than steady-state prioritization and were supported by orthogonal enhancer CRISPRi screens. In HepG2, LDL cholesterol-associated perturbation-induced programs specifically revealed statin-responsive pathways not significantly enriched by steady-state PoPS prioritization, supported by pharmacological transcriptional responses and population plasma proteomics. Perturbscape also recovered blood-related trait-conditioned trans-regulatory relationships that were specifically supported by population trans-eQTLs in IFN-gamma-stimulated monocytes (OR = 1.30, P=1.6e-05). Perturbscape further revealed developmental-stage-specific convergence between monogenic diabetes regulators and polygenic T2D risk during pancreatic islet differentiation, and neuronal-subclass-specific autism-associated regulatory programs in vivo. Together, these findings establish perturbation-induced gene programs as a complementary layer of disease-relevant regulatory information, revealing genetically informative pathways and context-specific regulatory relationships incompletely represented by steady-state molecular atlases.

papers.title: Lineage tracing in rhabdoid tumor organoids and orthotopic xenografts reveals convergent transcriptional states
papers.abstract: Malignant rhabdoid tumors (MRTs) are aggressive pediatric malignancies driven by loss of a single SWI/SNF subunit in an otherwise near-silent genome, yet they display extensive transcriptional heterogeneity. Whether this heterogeneity reflects the outgrowth of transcriptionally distinct clones, or states adopted independently of lineage, is unknown. Here we combined lentiviral lineage barcoding with single-cell RNA sequencing in two patient-derived renal MRT organoid models, followed through long-term in vitro culture and in a novel orthotopic xenograft setting. In both modalities, tumors and cultures became progressively restricted to a small number of lineages, and the clones that expanded were transcriptionally distinct from one another. Decomposing into gene expression programs showed that some transcriptional states were used broadly across lineages while others were confined to a few, and that lineages expanding independently, in separate cultures and separate animals, converged on the same restricted states. Individual lineages generally maintained their transcriptional identity across passaging and across anatomical sites, including in metastases, which arose from clones already expanded in the matched primary tumor. Which lineages came to dominate, however, differed between animals given the same starting population. Clonal outcome is therefore variable while the transcriptional states available to a tumor are drawn from a constrained and recurring repertoire.

papers.title: Intrinsic timekeeping in Escherichia coli
papers.abstract: Circadian clocks allow organisms to anticipate predictable environmental changes across the day-night cycle. Here we show that the bacterium Escherichia coli exhibits intrinsic timekeeping that anticipates daily temperature cycles. E. coli biofilms entrained to daily temperature shifts, producing 24-hour rhythms in curli plaque formation that persisted under constant temperature. Mechanistically, genetic analyses localized the autonomous timing machinery to the Rcs phosphorelay, which exhibits structural and conceptual parallels with other circadian systems. The BluFR sensory pathway, which acts upstream of the Rcs phosphorelay, linked temperature and blue-light cycles to rhythmic curli production. Flagellar promoter activity and curli production peaked at opposite times of day, suggesting daily coordination of adhesion and motility programs. These findings identify an intrinsic timing system in E. coli that expands our understanding of biological timekeeping.

papers.title: Finely tuned DDA-PASEF-based immunopeptidomics workflow enhances HLA class I coverage
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based immunopeptidomics is essential for the direct identification of HLA-presented peptides, but its application to low-input and clinical samples remains challenging. In this study, we present an optimized DDA-PASEF-based workflow to improve HLA class I peptide coverage. First, we optimized a magnetic bead-based sample preparation protocol to support analysis from reduced starting material and increase compatibility with automation. We then evaluated LC gradient length and column dimensions to define complementary configurations for high-throughput and high-coverage analysis. For MS acquisition, we fine-tuned key parameters, including ion accumulation time, number of PASEF scans, ion mobility range, and polygon filtering, to improve sensitivity while maintaining a suitable cycle time and limiting pre-CID truncations. The customized polygon filter improved the detection of singly charged HLA class I peptides, thereby broadening the identified immunopeptide repertoire. Finally, TIMS2Rescore was integrated to improve confidence in peptide identification. Overall, this optimized workflow improves HLA class I immunopeptide coverage across different sample types, even from low injected sample amounts, supporting its future applicability to clinically relevant samples.

papers.title: Podoplanin shapes epidermal morphogenesis and coordinates stem cell and epidermal-dermal responses during inflammatory remodelling
papers.abstract: Skin development and adaptation to inflammatory stress require keratinocytes to coordinate changes in cell behaviour with tissue organisation. Cell adhesion and the cortical cytoskeleton support the structural plasticity underlying these responses. Here, using complementary mouse models of global podoplanin deletion and conditional deletion in basal keratinocytes driven by keratin 5-Cre (K5Cre), we identify a role for the small transmembrane glycoprotein podoplanin in maintaining basal layer organisation and coordinating differentiation with barrier acquisition during development, as well as in inflammatory skin remodelling. Podoplanin expression was dynamically regulated during epidermal morphogenesis, becoming enriched in basal epithelial compartments before declining postnatally in the interfollicular epidermis. Both deletion models exhibited basal layer disorganisation, altered division orientation and increased epidermal thickness. Premature or expanded expression of differentiation markers was accompanied by delayed barrier acquisition, indicating that podoplanin loss uncouples differentiation marker expression from functional maturation. Barrier function subsequently recovered despite persistent histological abnormalities. In primary keratinocytes, podoplanin deficiency disrupted junctional actin organisation, reduced ERM phosphorylation and impaired junctional enrichment of pERM and doubly phosphorylated myosin light chain 2 (ppMLC2), despite largely preserved recruitment of adhesion proteins. In adult skin, K5Cre-mediated deletion altered differentiation marker dynamics following topical application of the proinflammatory agent 12-O-tetradecanoylphorbol-13-acetate (TPA), while the epidermal thickening response remained largely comparable to controls. These epidermal changes were accompanied by altered dermal thickness dynamics and an absence of TPA-induced podoplanin expression in dermal fibroblasts. Furthermore, TPA reduced the number of BrdU-retaining cells in the interfollicular epidermis of controls but not K5Cre-mediated conditional podoplanin knockout mice. This difference is consistent with impaired activation or mobilisation of slow-cycling cells, suggesting altered responsiveness within the epidermal stem and progenitor compartment. Together, these findings establish keratinocyte-expressed podoplanin as a regulator of epidermal organisation and functional maturation, with effects extending beyond the epithelium to shape the dermal response to inflammatory challenge.

papers.title: The chloroplast-localised transporter RETICULATA controls palisade mesophyll cell division and expansion
papers.abstract: Plant leaves contain extensive intercellular air spaces, which contribute to photosynthetic capacity and water use efficiency in different environments. Despite this importance, the developmental mechanisms that control leaf air space patterning are poorly understood. For over 20 years it has been known that plants with disrupted chloroplast biogenesis and metabolism have increased intercellular air spaces, but the underlying molecular mechanism is unknown. Here, we characterise leaf air space morphogenesis in mutants of the chloroplast amino acid transporter RETICULATA (RE), which has enlarged air spaces. We show that the reticulata-6 (re-6) loss of function mutant exhibits increased air space expansion specifically in the palisade, and not the spongy, mesophyll. We also show that RE does not regulate air space patterning via programmed cell death, via a change in stomatal density or a change in cell identity of the mesophyll tissue. Instead, we quantify mesophyll cell morphology and division rates to show that RE acts by promoting early palisade cell division and suppressing later cell expansion. Overall, we show that RE specifically regulated palisade mesophyll morphogenesis and air space patterning and hypothesise that chloroplasts may act to regulate air space patterning in the palisade mesophyll in response to light.

papers.title: Differential modulation of the neurocomputational signature of early and late mismatch responses to spoken words by awareness and task relevance
papers.abstract: Mismatch responses (MMRs), including the mismatch negativity (MMN) and the P3, are a hallmark of the brains capacity to detect unexpected events. They are discussed to be generated by two main processes: adaptation and prediction error (PE). However, MMR research on underlying mechanisms has mostly relied on simple, non-linguistic stimuli such as tones, and it remains unknown how awareness and attentional conditions affect MMRs to auditory verbal stimuli, that, unlike tones, carry lexical-semantic meaning. Here, we conducted a preregistered EEG study that disentangled influences of awareness, general task-relevance of word stimuli, and specific target-relevance of word oddballs on the MMN and P3. In addition, single-trial neurocomputational models were applied to uncover the underlying generative models of the MMRs. Results show that word-related MMN and P3 were only elicited when words were task-relevant, and the P3 increased with target-relevance. Crucially, no word-related MMN emerged under inattention, in contrast to the pre-attentive MMN typically reported for tonal deviants. Neurocomputational modeling revealed that the early part of the task-relevant MMN reflects adaptation processes. PE processes generated later parts of the MMN under task-relevance, and the entire MMN under target-relevance, as well as the P3 independent of relevance conditions. This suggests that the same temporal generation pattern of adaptation and PE underlie mismatch responses to both words and tones, but that, unlike tonal MMRs, eliciting MMRs to words requires the allocation of attention. This attentional dependency may reflect the additional lexical-semantic and multi-level representational demands that spoken words impose on the auditory system.

papers.title: Discovering Prognostic Risk Strata and Heterogeneous Progression Routes from Cross-Sectional Survival Data
papers.abstract: Inferring how individual patients progress towards higher disease risk typically requires longitudinal observations, which are often unavailable. Population-level analyses of cross-sectional data can identify differences between risk groups but may obscure heterogeneous progression patterns across individual patients. In this work, we introduce GOTSurv, a framework for patient-specific progression modelling. Using cross-sectional survival data, it first learns to rank patients by survival risk and automatically stratify them into prognostic risk groups without requiring predefined risk cut-offs. It then uses unbalanced optimal transport to infer patient-specific changes in the magnitude and direction of features associated with transitions towards higher-risk strata. We evaluated GOTSurv across ten TCGA cancer cohorts using two modalities: gene expression (n=4,767) and whole-slide image representations (n=4,655), with external validation in two independent cohorts. Compared with established survival models, GOTSurv generally achieved stronger prognostic stratification without requiring predefined risk cut-offs, while retaining competitive survival-ranking accuracy. More importantly, GOTSurv enabled the discovery of individualised progression trajectories associated with increasing risk, revealing distinct progression patterns even among patients within the same risk stratum. Overall, GOTSurv provides a novel framework for inferring heterogeneous, patient-specific progression patterns from cross-sectional survival data, enabling the identification of distinct pathways associated with increasing disease risk and informing the development of personalised therapeutic strategies. The code for GOTSurv is available at https://github.com/EtharZaid/GOTSurv/.

papers.title: An Eyewear-Based EEG Interface for Temporal-Region Monitoring and Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Conventional electroencephalography (EEG) devices are often impractical for ambulatory settings due to their reliance on specialized hardware and expert operation. To address this, we developed a user-friendly eyewear-based EEG system featuring dry titanium electrodes positioned approximately 5 mm inferoposterior to the T7/T8 sites (near the ears), with metal nose pads serving as references. We evaluated the system across 103 recordings spanning five paradigms: alpha reactivity, blink-related transients, fatigue, attention, and video-elicited emotion. Following quality control, 93.2-100.0% of epochs were retained. The system demonstrated high sensitivity to ocular transients, showing significant amplitude increases during the blinking task. The emotion task yielded the most robust state-related features, with statistically significant differences in differential entropy across negative, neutral, and positive video categories, achieving balanced accuracies of 0.882 for two-class and 0.667 for three-class prediction. Despite challenges at the multiple testing correction stage, the alpha reactivity and fatigue contrast tasks were still noteworthy to some extent. The attention paradigm revealed a consistent increase in differential entropy during focused states, and the eyewear system outperformed the Muse headband in group-held-out classification. These findings provide strong evidence for the feasibility of temporal-region eyewear EEG acquisition, highlighting its potential applications in the real-world, particularly for emotion recognition.

papers.title: Chromosome folding encodes mechanisms of cohesion maintenance
papers.abstract: After DNA replication, sister chromatids are physically linked by the cohesin complex. These cohesin linkages must be maintained for many hours for faithful chromosome segregation and DNA repair. Cohesin interacts with multiple rapidly exchanging cofactors, including SORORIN, which is often described as a molecular lock for cohesin on chromatin. How such transient SORORIN binding can protect cohesin over much longer timescales remains mechanistically unclear. Furthermore, how loop-extruding cohesins interact with and influence the positioning of sister-linking cohesins remains largely unknown. Here we show that changes in sister chromatid folding over time and after perturbations encode distinct signatures of the underlying mechanisms of cohesion maintenance. By integrating biochemical kinetics with polymer modeling, we infer cohesin turnover, motion, and encounter rules from these folding signatures. Repeated transient sequestration by SORORIN enables long-lasting protection yet acts as a quantitative modulator, rather than a binary switch for cohesion maintenance. Prolonging cohesin residence time by WAPL depletion exposes additional mechanisms shaping sister chromatid conformation, including pushing of sister-linking cohesins and diffusion of loop-extruding cohesins. Together, these results reveal how transient cofactor interactions regulate long-lived cohesin maintenance and establish sister chromosome organization as a quantitative readout of otherwise hidden molecular mechanisms.

papers.title: The Molecular Interplay of Tau and Motor Proteins on Microtubules
papers.abstract: Tau is a microtubule (MT)-associated protein essential for neuronal cytoskeletal organization and intracellular transport, yet how tau physically regulates motor proteins remains elusive. Here, we integrate single-molecule imaging, cryo-electron microscopy, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying tau-mediated inhibition of kinesin-1 and cytoplasmic dynein motility. We show that tau suppresses MT landing and triggers frequent pausing and premature detachment when motors encounter tau-enriched patches. Unexpectedly, tau impairs each motor using different mechanisms. Tau and kinesin-1 compete for the same surface on tubulin, precluding simultaneous binding to the same MT site. On the other hand, while dynein and tau can co-occupy the same tubulin, tau inhibits the transition of dynein into its high-affinity MT-binding state. Thus, tau can act as a physical or a conformational roadblock in a concentration-dependent manner, exerting distinct structural constraints on kinesin and dynein transport. These findings establish a structural framework for tau-mediated regulation of axonal transport.

papers.title: Generalizable virtual staining from histopathology to spatial proteomics across biological scales
papers.abstract: Large histology archives capture morphological correlates of molecular tissue states but lack direct spatial protein measurements. In this study, we show that routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histology can provide a queryable, morphology-based representation of spatial protein expression that remains informative from pixels to patients. To achieve this, we developed QUEST, a model framework that represents protein markers as semantic queries for flexible multiplex immunofluorescence (MIF) prediction. Trained on a heterogeneous atlas of paired H&E and MIF images comprising over 10,000 tissue regions, QUEST captured morphological patterns associated with protein markers and reconstructed their expression intensities across diverse tissue types and cohorts. Its utility extended beyond image reconstruction and preserved biologically meaningful information across multiple scales: virtual staining preserved protein marker expression at the cellular and tissue scales, supported cell phenotyping, cellular neighborhood analysis, and characterization of spatial tissue organization, retained clinically relevant signals for patient stratification, and enabled H&E-based queries to retrieve MIF references with similar molecular profiles. These findings position virtual staining not simply as image generation but as a flexible interface between routine histology and spatial proteomics, expanding the analytical value of existing H&E archives.

papers.title: Algal turf sediment dynamics across the Florida Reef Tract
papers.abstract: Algal turfs and their associated sediments are dominant components of many degraded reefs, where they mediate key ecosystem processes. However, the quantification of algal turfs and their sediments across reef shelves is limited outside Indo-Pacific reef systems. We quantified algal turf length, sediment loads, and sediment grain size distribution across four reef positions (nearshore, inner, middle, and outer) at three locations along the northern Florida Reef Tract (FRT). Sediment loads were positively associated with algal turf length and generally declined moving offshore. Nearshore reefs supported algal turfs that were both 1.6-fold longer and contained 1.6-fold higher sediment loads than on outer reefs, while sediment composition shifted toward finer grain sizes offshore. Nevertheless, regardless of reef position, all algal turfs had high sediment loads ranging from 1,445 to 16,639 g m-2. Our findings suggest that cross-shelf patterns in algal turf sediment dynamics are present on Western Atlantic reefs and reveal that long sediment-laden algal turfs dominate on the FRT. These results highlight the pervasive nature of sediment-laden algal turfs on degraded reefs and emphasize the need to monitor and manage their expansion on reefs subject to chronic coastal development and climate-driven disturbance.

papers.title: Mitochondria-Coupled Hitchhiking Drives Vimentin Intermediate Filament Transport
papers.abstract: Vimentin intermediate filaments (VIFs) undergo active microtubule-dependent transport throughout the cell, with trajectories resembling those of motor-driven organelles, yet our recent work showed that only a small subset of VIFs lies close to microtubules. How VIFs engage the microtubule-based transport machinery, and whether additional transport routes contribute, remain unresolved. We hypothesized that VIFs move indirectly, by hitchhiking on motile organelles, and tested this using mitochondria. Live imaging showed mitochondria and adjacent VIFs moving together, and volume electron microscopy revealed VIFs closely following mitochondrial surfaces at sites distinct from microtubule contacts. Depleting the mitochondrial motor adaptor TRAK1 to inhibit anterograde mitochondrial transport shifted both mitochondria and VIFs toward the nucleus. Driving mitochondria toward the cell periphery with a tailless kinesin-1 in cells lacking endogenous kinesin-1, or toward the cell center with a minus-end-directed motor, redistributed a subset of VIFs in the same direction. Thus, VIF transport to a large extend is accomplished by hitchhiking on motile mitochondria.

papers.title: Aging activates latent enhancers that can be reversed withexercise
papers.abstract: Aging profoundly alters the genome's regulatory landscape, but the properties of age-acquired enhancers, including how they are selected and sustained in aged animals are unclear. We used single-cell multiomics in the mouse heart to identify age-responsive cis-regulatory elements and endurance exercise to understand which of these elements can be attenuated. Aging increased AP-1 engagement at more than 100,000 regulatory loci across cardiac cell types. Exercise opposed most of these gains. Despite low endogenous accessibility, age-gained enhancer sequences drove reporter activity comparable to stable elements, revealing substantial latent transcriptional potential. Local sequence features distinguished responsiveness to aging and exercise. Reporter perturbations implicated sequence outside the AP-1 core, and mutagenesis localized informative positions to dispersed segments of dynamic enhancers. These enhancers were IL-1-sensitive and were preferentially responsive to neutralization of the cytokine in vivo. AP-1 inhibition further opposed age-associated transcription. Together, these findings support a model in which aging engages latent cell-type specific enhancers that are sustained in an active state by ongoing trans signaling. Aging therefore changes the deployment of existing regulatory information, while the acquired activity remains responsive to changes in signaling even in old age.

papers.title: Four genome assemblies of new wild Gossypium hirsutum accessions from the Yucatan Peninsula, the center of domestication
papers.abstract: Gossypium hirsutum is a leading source of natural cotton fiber, accounting for most of the market share. While domestication and improvement have led to significant gains in fiber quantity and quality, the narrow germplasm base of modern cultivars creates vulnerabilities, including to emerging pests. Wild populations provide a reservoir for genetic diversity that may be valuable in identifying and transferring resistance or stress-adaptation alleles to modern breeding lines. Here we report four new genome assemblies of G. hirsutum representing distinct populations from its center of diversity in Yucatan, Mexico. These chromosome-level assemblies are highly contiguous and structurally similar to existing G. hirsutum genomes; however, comparative analyses highlight their distinctiveness, suggesting they form a valuable reservoir of untapped diversity. Preliminary analyses of nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) immune receptor genes underscore this variation, suggesting presence-absence variation may exist among populations. These findings demonstrate the potential of these new genomic resources for discovery of novel disease resistance alleles and, generally, for expanding the narrow germplasm base of the modern cotton cultivars.

papers.title: Disentangling Context-Specific Alzheimer's Disease Progression Signatures through an Explainable AI Framework
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression involves stage-dependent transcriptional changes that are often masked by dominant cellular and biological variation. Here, we present ADVISE (Alzheimer's Disease Variational Isolation of Signal Embeddings), an interpretable deep generative framework designed to disentangle Braak stage-associated transcriptional signals from background biological variation through separate latent representations. Using explainable AI, ADVISE prioritizes genes and pathways contributing to the disease-specific representation. Applying ADVISE to large-scale single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from the human prefrontal cortex, we identify shared and context-specific signatures of AD progression across global, sex-specific, and cell-type-specific analyses, revealing convergent molecular programs involving synaptic transmission, HSF1-associated proteostatic stress responses, and SLIT/ROBO axon guidance. Notably, ADVISE prioritizes ROBO2 as a progression-associated candidate in excitatory neurons. Experimental validation using CRISPR activation in hiPSC-derived excitatory neurons demonstrates that ROBO2 activation reduces the phosphorylated Tau-to-total Tau ratio. ADVISE thus reveals context-dependent molecular signatures of AD progression and bridges human single-cell discoveries with experimental validation of candidate regulators of AD pathology.

papers.title: Locomotor activity enhances environmental representation by boosting visuo-frontal communication
papers.abstract: During environment exploration we rapidly acquire visual information to identify targets of interest. Here, we discovered that locomotion limits how long natural scenes are viewed dur- ing free exploration. Whether the brain has developed compensatory mechanisms to ensure that sensory information is accurately transmitted to downstream areas during and after locomotion is unknown. We examined this issue by recording the spiking activity of popula- tions of neurons in visual and prefrontal cortex in conjunction with wireless recordings of oculomotor events while macaques moved freely to explore their environment or performed treadmill bipedal locomotion. The communication between visuo-frontal cortical areas was enhanced during and after locomotion to increase visual-evoked responses and population coding accuracy in prefrontal, but not visual cortical neurons. This in turn improved behav- ioral performance in a freely moving visual detection task after locomotion. Electrical stim- ulation further revealed elevated inter-areal synaptic efficacy during locomotor activity. The mechanism whereby locomotion enhances stimulus coding accuracy in prefrontal cortex and behavioral performance by increasing visuo-frontal communication is functionally beneficial during environmental exploration when incoming stimuli are rapidly changing and the win- dow for perceptual decisions is temporally restricted.

papers.title: Discontinuation of GLP-1RA Treatment Reinstates Binge-Like Eating and Drives Body Weight Past Pre-Treatment Levels in Mice
papers.abstract: We examined the impact of semaglutide treatment and discontinuation in a pre-clinical model for binge eating. Treatment reduced body weight and palatable food intake in mice with binge-like eating. Discontinuation reinstated binge-like eating and caused body weight to significantly exceed pre-treatment baseline, revealing specific binge-related risk when discontinuing GLP-1RAs.

papers.title: Life on leaves left a lasting mark on the Methylobacterium core genome
papers.abstract: The extent to which core genomes reflect strictly vertical inheritance remains debated, particularly in ecologically diverse bacterial lineages. Here, we investigate the evolution of the core genome of Methylobacterium, a major leaf-associated bacterial genus, to assess how evolutionary signals vary across genes and whether they relate to functions involved in adaptation to life at the surface of plant leaves (the phyllosphere). Identifying 1,099 protein-coding core genes across 293 genomes, we combined gene tree comparisons, phylogenetic network reconstruction, nucleotide polymorphism patterns, and functional enrichment analyses. We found that most core genes show some deviation from the consensus phylogenetic tree. However, this discordance is not randomly distributed. Across all analytical approaches, genes showing the strongest deviations are consistently associated with functions linked to life in the phyllosphere, including anoxygenic photosynthesis, protection against UV and osmotic stress. These genes are often grouped into conserved clusters in the genome. In particular, a large cluster involved in anoxygenic photosynthesis, including bacteriochlorophyll and carotenoid biosynthesis, shows strong variation in its evolutionary history and organization across lineages, despite maintaining a conserved core structure. Similar patterns of phylogenetic incongruence and gene organization are observed across related Hyphomicrobiales inhabiting the phyllosphere, suggesting that these functions extend beyond Methylobacterium. Together, these results indicate that evolutionary heterogeneity within the core genome is concentrated in genes involved in key ecological functions. While alternative explanations cannot be excluded, these patterns are consistent with horizontal gene transfer contributing to the diversification of traits important for survival and adaptation in phyllosphere bacterial communities.

papers.title: Transferrin receptor binding valency determines the circulating half-life and weight-loss efficacy of Fc-FGF21 in TfR-humanized mice
papers.abstract: Fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) is a promising metabolic hormone with potent anti-obesity effects. It acts in both the central nervous system and peripheral tissues to exert its metabolic benefits. Because its receptors are expressed at low levels in the brain, we hypothesized that enhanced transport across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) would improve its efficacy. To achieve this, FGF21 was fused to Fc(TV35), an engineered Fc fragment that binds the human transferrin receptor (hTfR), to generate Fc(TV35)-FGF21. Fc(TV35)-FGF21 does not bind to mouse TfR, so it produced weight-loss effects in wild-type diet-induced obese mice comparable to those of Fc-FGF21. However, it failed to induce weight loss in homozygous hTfR-humanized mice because of a markedly shortened circulating half-life. Converting Fc(TV35)-FGF21 from a homodimer to a bispecific Fc format with a single hTfR-binding arm partially restored the circulating half-life and weight-loss efficacy. Reducing mouse hTfR zygosity from homozygous to heterozygous did not substantially improve the engineered protein's half-life or weight-loss effect. Taken together, our findings suggest that sustained systemic exposure is a major determinant of FGF21's weight-loss efficacy and that hTfR engagement can shorten its systemic half-life and compromise its therapeutic activity. These results highlight an important design limitation of TfR-based brain vehicles, especially for delivering metabolic hormones with low-abundance CNS receptor targets. As a result, further optimization of shuttle formats to minimize systemic clearance while crossing the BBB is needed for metabolic hormones.

papers.title: Explainable Multimodal Prognostic Modeling Uncovers New Clinically Relevant Pathological Features in a Multi-Institutional Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor Cohort
papers.abstract: Although many patients with a well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (PanNET) are cured after surgical resection, it is hard to predict outcome in these patients. Current prognostic assessment relies largely on Ki-67 proliferation index, tumor stage, and established adverse pathologic features, such as vascular and perineural invasion. However, individually, these variables incompletely explain why patients with similar clinicopathologic profiles sometimes experience markedly different outcomes. To address this challenge, we assembled three independent cohorts with a surgically resected PanNET. In total, we included 1,438 patients with approximately 30,000 histology images, and approximately 12,000 person-years of follow-up. We separately modeled structured clinicopathologic information with Cox regression and tumor-centered pathology images with deep learning on an internal cohort treated at Johns Hopkins Hospital and performed multimodal continuous-time survival modeling to reveal which clinical and pathologic features are most important in predicting patient outcome. Across Cox models of censored time to recurrence-free survival, a text-based clinicopathological model that incorporated known prognosticators achieved a C-index of approximately 0.87, the image-based histology model approximately 0.80, and decision-level late multimodal fusion approximately 0.88 on the internal test set. The clinical model demonstrated strong prognostic discrimination using established risk factors, mainly relying on the TNM stage and Ki-67 index. Primary tumor histology retained substantial prognostic signal, with analysis restricted to tumor-centered regions to reduce reliance on unrelated tissues that might indirectly indicate disease extent. Interpretation of high-attention image tiles revealed regions of importance in the primary tumor, including recognized adverse morphologic features such as the leading edge of the tumor and foci of vascular or perineural invasion. Unexpectedly, intratumoral and peritumoral stroma accounted for nearly 50% of the model's high-attention regions, suggesting that the stroma may yield equal prognostic information to neoplastic cells in recurrence-prediction models. To test generalizability, we further evaluated the trained models in independent cohorts from two institutions with different demographics, where discrimination varied by site (mean late-fusion C-indices of 0.864 and 0.723). Together with the improved discrimination achieved through late fusion, our findings suggest that current clinicopathologic variables can be modeled to form reliable prognosticators, and that routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained slides of the primary tumor contain additional prognostically important information not fully captured by conventional clinicopathologic assessment, such that together, the two sources provide complementary information.

papers.title: MULTI-COHORT TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS REVEALS SHARED INFLAMMATORY SIGNALING AND UROTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION ACROSS IC/BPS PHENOTYPES
papers.abstract: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) is a heterogeneous disorder characterized by bladder pain, inflammation, and urothelial dysfunction, yet the molecular features shared across clinically defined disease phenotypes remain incompletely understood. Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and acyloxyacyl hydrolase (AOAH), a regulator of TLR4 ligand activity, have been implicated in IC/BPS in clinical and preclinical mechanistic studies. Here, we performed a multi-cohort reanalysis of four independent human IC/BPS transcriptomic datasets spanning bladder tissue and urine sediment from non-ulcer/non-Hunner, ulcerative/Hunner, normal-capacity, low-capacity, non-lesion, and lesion phenotypes. We evaluated immune cell-associated expression, urothelial differentiation and barrier integrity, TLR4 and pro-inflammatory signaling, and AOAH expression. IC/BPS exhibited phenotype-specific immune remodeling, yet shared features were also identified. Bladder-tissue IC/BPS was consistently associated with reduced expression of urothelial differentiation and barrier markers, together with increased TLR4 recognition and pro-inflammatory signaling. AOAH expression was elevated across all three bladder-tissue cohorts and was associated with monocyte/macrophage and pro-inflammatory transcriptional states. TLR4 signaling similarly paralleled myeloid and inflammatory features, whereas inflammatory programs generally showed inverse relationships with urothelial barrier markers. Notably, independently defined severe phenotypes of ulcerative IC and low-capacity IC showed concordant molecular remodeling characterized by increased leukocyte and monocyte/macrophage signatures, enhanced TLR4 signaling, elevated AOAH expression, and reduced urothelial barrier-associated expression. Together, these findings identify reproducible molecular signatures that extend across IC/BPS phenotypes and support a model in which urothelial dysfunction and TLR4-AOAH-associated myeloid inflammatory states coexist across disease phenotypes. These results provide a molecular framework for stratifying IC/BPS beyond clinical labels and identify shared and subtype-specific molecular signatures that may inform therapeutic response evaluation and clinical management.

papers.title: Biological Signaling Pathways Associated with Late Tendon Development in Chicken Embryos and Their Dependence on Mechanical Stimulation
papers.abstract: During embryonic and neonatal development, tendons exhibit rapid changes in mechanics and structure, including increases in collagen content, crosslinking, and fibril length. These functional and structural changes are partly dependent on mechanical stimulation. However, the specific mechanobiological mechanisms driving these changes remain poorly understood. The objective of this study was to identify the potential biological mechanisms and pathways driving tendon maturation into load-bearing materials using an embryonic chick model. Using bulk RNA sequencing, gene set enrichment analysis, and transcription factor analysis, we produced a transcriptomic profile of chick hindlimb tendons during late embryonic development (E16, E18, and E20) and tendons from rigid and flaccid paralysis-treated embryos. Additionally, we assessed the results from two differential expression analysis models to improve the replicability of our findings. Our results suggest that the largest transcriptomic response occurs between embryonic day 16 and 20, and that among paralysis conditions, rigid paralysis produces the greatest effect relative to controls. Across development, we found positive enrichment in processes related to mechanotransduction, extracellular matrix remodeling, cell adhesion, and contractility, and identified candidate pathways upregulated with development, including TGF-{beta}, PI3K-AKT-mTOR, Hippo, circadian rhythm, and focal adhesion signaling. In paralysis-treated embryos, our data suggest impairment in extracellular matrix remodeling and mechanotransduction events. Specifically, we found that both modes of paralysis are associated with a cellular stress response and downregulation of WNT signaling. Together, our findings identify candidate mechanotransduction pathways that are associated with late tendon maturation and altered by paralysis, which may inform tendon tissue engineering and regenerative approaches.

papers.title: NBDC Data Tools: Building Analysis-ready Datasets From ABCD and HBCD Releases in R and Python
papers.abstract: act The NIH Brain Development Cohorts (NBDC) Data Hub provides access to large-scale longitudinal datasets, including the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study(R) and the HEALthy Brain and Child Development (HBCD) Study. The studies release their tabulated data as hundreds of tables with tens of thousands of variables. Turning these files into a dataset for a particular analysis poses substantial informatics challenges, especially when data preparation and analysis workflows must be reproducible and reusable for new releases. We therefore developed NBDC Data Tools, a suite of open-source packages for preparing NBDC data in local or other approved computing environments. NBDCtools is the core R package for dataset construction and processing. The Python package nbdctools either calls the R workflow or assembles datasets natively in Python, and the R package NBDCtoolsData provides the release metadata support for both NBDCtools and nbdctools. Users define a dataset in code by naming the study, the release, and the variables or tables they need. The software then uses the standardized metadata released by the studies to locate the relevant files, join tables on the participant and session identifiers, convert data types, attach labels, and optionally recode non-response codes as missing values. Because the dataset definition is a short script that runs on the original release files, it can be rerun, shared with collaborators, and reported in publications. NBDC Data Tools complements the web-based data platforms of the NBDC Data Hub by providing a reproducible, scriptable path from approved data access to analysis-ready data for statistical analysis.

papers.title: Auditing Biomedical Literature with Blinded AI Peer Review: Where Peer Review Works, Where It Fails, and How to Strengthen It
papers.abstract: Biomedical publishing has grown more than elevenfold since 1991, outstripping human peer review. Unblinded language models cannot audit this literature objectively because they recognize famous authors and journals from training memory. We built BARS (Blinded AI Review System), an automated referee that strips titles, author names, institutions, journal headers, and dates before grading full-text manuscripts on a 10-point scale covering methods, evidence, biology, and reproducibility. We used BARS to generate 1,874 blind reviews across 1,714 unique papers. BARS passed 100% of verified sound controls, caught 77% to 91% of internally flawed papers, eliminated a +0.35-point prestige boost, and more than doubled human referee consistency. Across 320 recent open-access articles (2020-2025) from eight fields, 54% failed on core scientific rigor (<5.0/10; 41% excluding megajournals). Revision at selective journals improved preprints more than twice as much as revision at commercial megajournals (+0.62 vs. +0.30 points; baseline-adjusted p = 0.033), and BARS recalled 98% of unresolved human referee critiques across 100 open-review papers. Across 915 date-blinded papers from 1991 to 2025, average scores fell from 7.6/10 to 5.8/10 as megajournals and template database studies expanded. Blinded self-audits of 238 papers by two senior authors -- and of this manuscript itself -- caught real statistical, control, and table errors in our own work.
