We examined whether hypothalamic subunit volumes are associated with age and socioeconomic status (SES) in cognitively healthy adults. Methods: From the OASIS-1 cross-sectional dataset (n = 416, 18-96 years), 133 participants with a Clinical Dementia Rating of 0 and complete segmentation output were analysed (33-94 years). A FreeSurfer-based convolutional neural network, run on a cloud virtual machine, segmented five subunits per hemisphere. Volumes were normalised to estimated total intracranial volume (eTIV) and related to age and SES (Hollingshead index) using Pearson correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction; partial correlations adjusted for sex (age) and for age and sex (SES) served as sensitivity analyses. Results: Older age was associated with lower normalised volume of the right posterior subunit (r = -.456, q < .001) and the left posterior subunit (r = -.274, q = .007); both associations persisted after adjustment for sex. Lower SES showed a trend towards larger left anterior-inferior volume (r = .242, uncorrected p = .005) that did not survive FDR correction (q = .053). Conclusions: Age-related volumetric differences in the healthy hypothalamus appear to be concentrated in its posterior portion, a region housing arousal-promoting circuitry. Automated subunit segmentation offers a scalable tool for studying the hypothalamus in ageing and in relation to environmental exposures; the cross-sectional associations reported here should not be interpreted as causal or as within-person change.

papers.title: SPaRTA: Spatial Reasoning in Text-to-SQL for Omics Analysis
papers.abstract: Spatial-omics technologies provide clinicians, pathologists, and biomedical researchers with high-resolution maps of transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic activity within tissues. However, querying these complex datasets often requires specialized computational expertise, limiting their accessibility to domain experts without programming experience. In the current manuscript, we develop SPaRTA (Spatial Reasoning in Text-to-SQL for Omics Analysis), a natural-language interface that translates free-text questions into executable spatial SQL queries over such data. We release SPaRTA-Bench, comprising dataset-specific database schemas, explicit query conventions, and 7,500 question-SQL pairs validated through LLM-assisted verification and targeted human review, spanning breast cancer, pancreatic cancer, and melanoma tissue sections, and identify 15 failure modes in which a query runs but returns a wrong answer. Open-weight large language models (LLMs) of the Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma and Phi families reach 10-40% execution accuracy zero-shot, and at most 61% with reasoning and execution feedback. Fine-tuning raises them to 63-77%, and they lose at most 6 percentage points on a tissue unseen in training. Execution feedback repairs queries that fail to run, but rarely queries that run and return a wrong answer.

papers.title: GPBench: A benchmark framework for genomic prediction
papers.abstract: Genomic prediction (GP) has emerged as a powerful data mining strategy for disease risk assessment and molecular breeding. GP leverages genome-wide genetic variations and phenotypic information through a computational model to estimate genetic potential or disease risk. However, the field of GP still faces several major challenges: (i) dataset bias and insufficient representativeness; (ii) the lack of standardized evaluation protocols and a systematic benchmarking framework; (iii) heavy reliance on empirical expertise for experimental result interpretation, which hinders large-scale and systematic analysis. These issues make it difficult to conduct systematic cross-species evaluation and comparison of GP methods, and their authentic applications. To address these challenges, we established a standardized and extensible GP benchmark framework-GPBench. We first collected and harmonized public datasets from 16 species, covering animals, plants, and microorganisms, comprising 57 traits, 40,821 samples, and 493,821 single-nucleotide polymorphisms. Then, using the standardized datasets, the framework evaluates 21 GP models and provides a unified assessment across four dimensions: effectiveness, sensitivity, robustness, and scalability. Furthermore, we developed a large language model-based intelligent analysis system to facilitate the interpretation of GP experiments and model recommendations. GPBench provides the community with a fair, unified, and scalable platform (https://www.sdu-idea.cn/GPBench/) and an open-source library for comparing and optimizing GP methods, ultimately accelerating the application of GP in life sciences and biomedical research.

papers.title: Computational Analysis of Antioxidant Effects on Stress Response Mechanisms in Candida albicans
papers.abstract: Candida albicans was used as a eukaryotic model to study aging and oxidative stress response pathways focused on NAD dependent deacetylases, Sir2 and SIRT3. A significant gene expression regulation of both Sir2 and SIRT3 was observed under sublethal hydrogen peroxide treatment towards their association with stress adaptation. Natural ligands known for antioxidant properties were docked against Sir2 and SIRT3 structures. Binding free energy of most components fall in the range of -5.0 to -11 kcal/mol. The best candidates pterostilbene, quercetin and naringenin formed stable hydrophobic interactions and hydrogen bonds within catalytic and NAD binding pockets confirmed by visualization. Detailed ADME profiling shows most of the ligands passed the Lipinski rule of five and revealed a very good gastrointestinal absorption. PASS (Prediction of Activity Spectra for Substances) and SOM (Sites of Metabolism) predicts antioxidants, anti-aging properties, toxicity profiles, with key metabolic hotspots. This integrated in-silico approach highlights naringenin and quercetin as promising modulators of Sir2/SIRT3 mediated metabolic pathways in Candida albicans, warranting further validation with the help of in-vitro and in-vivo methods.

papers.title: A trustworthy semantic knowledge network linking data-driven cell phenotypes to diseases and drugs
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association and other genetic studies have identified genes involved in disease pathogenesis, and their encoded proteins have provided therapeutic targets. However, little is known about which cells are the functional home of these disease-associated genes and proteins. Single-cell technologies are enabling high-resolution profiling of cell phenotypes and revealing cellular contexts of disease, yet much of the resulting knowledge remains embedded in individual datasets and scientific literature. To address these gaps, the National Library of Medicine has developed Cell Knowledge Network (NLM-CKN, https://nlm-ckn.org). Reproducible computational workflows have generated cell phenotype knowledge for 2,585 cell sets and 5,139 selectively expressed genes from 88 datasets covering 10 human organs. Mapping of these cell sets to cell types grounds Cell Ontology terms in experimental evidence. This experimental knowledge is integrated with external knowledge of anatomical and cell-type hierarchies, gene-disease associations, and therapeutic interventions. A semantic schema defines node types and relations, enabling knowledge to be transformed into triple assertions and loaded into an ArangoDB database with provenance and quantitative evidence. The NLM-CKN interface supports graphical exploration of the cellular constituents of healthy human tissues. Finally, topological analyses generate insights into cellular contributions to disease pathogenesis, cellular contexts for therapeutic intervention, and drug-repurposing hypotheses.

papers.title: Disrupted mannosidase enzymes in C9orf72 ALS/FTD
papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is an age-related neurodegenerative disorder resulting from the loss of motor neurons in the brain and spinal cord. Neuroinflammation, induced by glial cells including microglia (MG) and astrocytes, is an acknowledged aspect of this neurodegeneration. Generating induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) neuroinflammatory models of ALS may help elucidate non-neuronal mechanisms of disease. Here, we analyze human postmortem tissue and an iPSC derived glia-crosstalk model identifying a reduction in Golgi enzymes MAN1A1 and MAN1A2 in addition to other glycan enzymes from ALS-associated microglia and astrocytes. Impaired Golgi and glycan metabolism is linked to inflammation and other related ALS disease mechanisms including impaired lysosomal proteostasis, altered extracellular matrix, disrupted secretion, and altered cell-cell signaling.

papers.title: Characterising cortical perturbation-recovery dynamics using TMS-EEG: The Brain Dynamic Toolbox
papers.abstract: Objective: To adapt dynamical measures used in computational and experimental perturbation models to human transcranial magnetic stimulation and electroencephalography (TMS-EEG) and determine whether analysis of the extended post-stimulation trajectory reveals additional features of the cortical response to long-interval intracortical inhibition (LICI). Methods: Single pulse and paired pulse LICI TMS-EEG responses from the bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortex were re-analysed in 16 healthy adults. At the stimulation site, 75 single-pulse and 75 paired-pulse trials were delivered; paired pulses comprised conditioning and test stimuli separated by 100 ms. Responses from 20 frontocentral EEG channels were analysed from 50-950 ms following TMS using the open source Brain Dynamic Metric Toolbox. Perturbative Integration Latency Index (PILI) indexed cortical resilience via response energy and recovery, Autocorrelation Function Width (ACFW) captured temporal memory, and Lyapunov Exponent (LE) indicated the dynamical stability. Linear mixed-effects models examined temporal, spectral, and time-frequency effects from the measured metrics. Results: LICI altered the temporal evolution of the dynamical measures. PILI distinguished conditions in the earliest post-stimulation window before converging, whereas ACFW differences persisted across a broader early interval. LE showed weaker and less consistent discrimination. Spectral effects were most evident for ACFW, while time-frequency analyses revealed later, frequency-specific LICI effects for PILI and ACFW but not LE. Conclusions: The extended post-stimulation trajectory revealed LICI-related differences in cortical resilience and temporal memory with distinct temporal and spectral profiles, while effects on dynamical stability were less consistent. Significance: The Brain Dynamic Metric Toolbox provides a reproducible framework for quantifying perturbation-recovery dynamics in TMS-EEG and demonstrates that the extended perturbational response contains information about LICI not captured by discrete early response measures.

papers.title: Megakaryocytic proteomic signatures define myeloproliferative neoplasms
papers.abstract: The classical Philadelphia-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are clonal stem cell disorders of the bone marrow with significant niche dysregulation driven in part by abnormal megakaryocytes. The three classical MPNs: polycythemia vera (PV), essential thrombocythemia (ET) and primary myelofibrosis (PMF), display established megakaryocytic morphological differences which aid in their diagnostic classification. The paucity of megakaryocytes in the bone marrow aspirate has previously limited a proteomic analysis of megakaryocytes in clinical samples. We aimed to undertake an unbiased proteomic analysis of in situ megakaryocytes from the bone marrow of patients with PV, ET, and PMF. Using a novel, deep visual proteomics strategy, we dissected and analyzed megakaryocytes from 60 MPN patients and 20 controls (patients with limited stage non-Hodgkin lymphoma who had uninvolved bone marrow). We reveal that megakaryocyte proteomics from MPN patients are distinct to those from control patients, and further, that the megakaryocytes from the three MPNs have unique, disease-specific signatures. The disease-specific megakaryocyte proteome highlights novel pathways of disease.

papers.title: IL-23 licenses the transition from preclinical autoimmunity to inflammatory arthritis through IL-17A-dependent mechanisms
papers.abstract: Objectives: The mechanisms driving transition from systemic autoimmunity to clinical rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remain poorly understood. We investigated the role of interleukin-23 (IL-23) in disease transition using a murine model of experimental arthritis, complemented by human transcriptomic analyses in individuals at risk of RA and RA synovial tissue. Methods: Collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) was induced in less susceptible C57BL/6 mice and combined with sustained systemic IL-23 overexpression. Disease severity, histopathology, immune responses, and tissue gene expression were evaluated. The contribution of IL-17A was assessed using a neutralizing anti-IL-17A antibody. Expression of IL-23 pathway-related genes was assessed in whole-blood transcriptomic data from a large cohort of first-degree relatives of patients with RA (n=1080) and in an independent synovial RNA-sequencing dataset (n=218). Results: In mice, sustained IL-23 overexpression converted a mild CIA phenotype into a highly penetrant arthritis characterized by increased expression of innate inflammatory mediators, and enhanced antigen-specific production of IL-17A and IFN-{gamma}, despite unchanged collagen-specific antibody responses. Neutralization of IL-17A prevented arthritis development. In human whole blood longitudinal analyses, lower RORC and KLRB1 expression was associated with a higher risk of RA onset. KLRB1 expression was persistently lower in progressors, whereas RORC expression showed a steeper decline before diagnosis, although this difference did not remain significant after correction for multiple testing. In RA synovium, IL23R, IL23A, and CCR2 expression was increased compared with controls, while IL23R expression was higher in early than established RA. Conclusions: IL-23 acts as a critical regulator of the transition from systemic autoimmunity to inflammatory arthritis by promoting IL-17A-dependent cellular and myeloid inflammatory pathways. The change in IL-23 pathway signatures in at-risk individuals and early RA supports the translational relevance of this pathway during disease initiation.

papers.title: Context-dependent effects of ketamine on emotional evidence integration
papers.abstract: Understanding others' emotions requires continuously integrating noisy affective information as emotional states change over time. Research on emotion processing, however, has thus far focused on static environments or discrete events. Here, we developed a continuous emotional evidence integration task in which participants had to track the average emotional state in a rapidly changing sequence of faces under different levels of environmental volatility. This allowed us to examine emotion integration in changing environments. In online (n=92) and in-person (n=29) cohorts, participants integrated emotional information over longer timescales in stable environments while relying more strongly on recent evidence under volatility, consistent with principles established in perceptual decision-making. We further examined whether this process was modulated by ketamine, an NMDA receptor antagonist associated with evidence integration in the perceptual domain. We conducted a double-blind, placebo-controlled, within-subject study and probed emotion integration during the post-acute period, approximately 1.5 hours after the infusion. Ketamine modulated the temporal weighting of emotional evidence, shifting the balance between recent and past information depending on environmental volatility. Together, these findings show that emotional evidence integration dynamically adapts to the statistical structure of the environment and that ketamine can further modulate this process, which may have relevance for affective disorders.

papers.title: Predicting single-molecule chromatin distribution from DNA sequence
papers.abstract: Genome regulation unfolds through dynamic and stochastic single-molecule events. Deep learning models that read gene regulatory activities from DNA sequences have markedly advanced our ability to predict cell-population-level averages. However, they cannot capture the full spectrum of heterogeneity and dynamics at the single-molecule level, which directly reflect the underlying mechanisms of genome regulation. Here, we introduce a sequence-to-distribution (S2d) framework that directly models the entire probabilistic distribution of single-molecule chromatin states from DNA sequence alone. We used this framework to train Mola, a model of single-molecule chromatin accessibility. We harness Mola to investigate sequence-based regulatory code and mechanisms for multiple aspects of chromatin regulation at the single-molecule level. By quantifying sequence-driven nucleosome regulation, we reveal distinct modes of transcription factor engagement with nucleosomes, including a novel nucleosome-trapping factor, ZNF146. We characterized the sequence determinants governing the +1 nucleosome after transcription start sites and identified YY1 as the strongest +1 nucleosome-positioning factor. Leveraging long-context single-molecule modeling, we further discovered a shared sequence basis for the co-accessibility of regulatory elements and the co-footprinting of transcription factors. Joint prediction of DNA methylation and accessibility reveals a sequence-driven bimodal state mediated by methylation-sensitive transcription factors. Beyond static single-molecule snapshots, the S2d framework can generate pseudo-dynamic trajectories of chromatin states and propose a roadmap toward genome-wide chromatin dynamics. Moreover, we showed that Mola can predict and interpret the effects of genetic variants at the single-molecule level, revealing how sequence changes reshape distal regulatory coordination. Together, this sequence-to-distribution framework lays the foundation for understanding how genomic sequence encodes stochastic and dynamic genome regulation, and how genetic variation changes it, one molecule at a time.

papers.title: Differential Gene Expression and Functional Enrichment Analysis of Breast Tumor and Normal Tissue RNA-seq Data: A Reanalysis of GEO Dataset GSE210787
papers.abstract: Background: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) allows a global assessment of expression differences between biological states. The present study reanalyzed publicly available RNA-seq data from human breast tumors and normal tissues to identify DEGs and to investigate functional enrichment. Methods: Twelve paired-end RNA-seq samples from the GEO series GSE210787 were analyzed, including six tumor and six normal samples. Reads were obtained using the SRA Toolkit, checked with FastQC and MultiQC, trimmed with fastp, aligned to the GRCh38.p14 reference with STAR, and quantified at the gene level with featureCounts. Differential expression analysis was performed using DESeq2 in the Galaxy environment. The project report details criteria of adjusted p-value < 0.05 and absolute log2 fold change [≥] 1. Gene Ontology enrichment was performed using g:Profiler and KEGG overrepresentation analysis was performed separately for the up- and down-regulated gene sets. Results: The project report contains a list of 120 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including 69 upregulated and 51 downregulated genes in tumor tissue compared with normal tissue. One upregulated-gene GO Cellular Component term, cell periphery (GO:0071944), was observed with a P-value of approximately 0.017585 and 29 overlapping genes. The original report does not specify if this P-value is nominal or adjusted. No significant GO terms were found for the down-regulated gene set. After multiple testing corrections, no KEGG pathway was significant; the lowest adjusted p-value for the upregulated group was about 0.71393. Conclusion: The project identified differences in expression between tumor and normal samples, but no KEGG pathway reached the set FDR significance threshold. The final interpretation needs to check sample metadata, DESeq2 contrast, GO significance statistic, KEGG background universe and analytical parameters against the original results. Keywords: RNA-seq; breast tumor; differential expression; DESeq2; Gene Ontology; KEGG pathway; transcriptomics; cell periphery.

papers.title: An Improved Manufacturing Method for Infusible Extracellular Matrix Materials to Enable Efficient Scale-Up, Improved Efficacy, and Clinical Translation
papers.abstract: Decellularized extracellular matrix (ECM) materials are a popular choice for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine applications due to their multifaceted bioactive capabilities arising from their heterogenous composition. For minimally invasive delivery, infusible ECM (iECM) was developed through fractionation of digested decellularized ECM, allowing the material to be safely delivered intravascularly. iECM localizes to permeable vasculature in inflamed tissues and exerts immunomodulatory and pro-reparative effects with proof-of-concept already demonstrated in multiple preclinical models including myocardial infarction (MI) and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS). However, one major limitation of iECM is the steps required for manufacturing, involving centrifugation, dialysis/lyophilization, and filtration (C-D-F). These steps limit manufacturing output and iECM concentration, and require significant human handling, limiting compliance with current good manufacturing practices (cGMP). To overcome these challenges, we developed a method for manufacturing iECM that utilizes depth filtration and tangential flow filtration (DF-TFF), which reduces manufacturing time, allows for increased iECM concentration, and reduces human manipulation of material, improving translatability and scalability of iECM materials. Based on multiple material characterization methods, we determined that iECM made with DF-TFF was comparable to iECM made with C-D-F. By increasing iECM concentration through this manufacturing method, we demonstrate a dose dependent response in an acute MI porcine model and a mouse MODS model. Finally, DF-TFF enabled timely production of iECM from alternative tissue sources. Altogether, DF-TFF allows for improvements in production time, scale-up, cGMP compliance, and increased dose through higher concentration, paving the way for future clinical translation as well new preclinical studies.

papers.title: Self-Other Neural Representational Distinction is Associated with Distorted Social Predictions in Social Anxiety
papers.abstract: Background: Social anxiety (SA) is characterized by distorted negative expectations about the future. Because optimism bias is inherently comparative, the extent to which these predictions reflect a fundamental disruption in self- versus other-referential processing remains poorly understood. Methods: Across two experiments, we investigated the mechanisms underlying social predictions in SA. In Experiment 1, individuals with high (n = 52, LSAS > 65) and low SA (n = 51, LSAS < 35) rated the future likelihood of positive and negative social outcomes for themselves or for a protagonist. In Experiment 2, 35 adults spanning a continuous spectrum of SA completed the task during fMRI. Behavior was analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Neurally, multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) quantified self-other representational distinctions, while a parametric general linear model (GLM) tracked neural sensitivity to likelihood predictions. Results: Behaviorally, higher SA was characterized by an attenuated optimism bias: individuals predicted a lower likelihood of positive outcomes, but a higher likelihood of negative outcomes, for themselves compared to others. Neurally, higher trait SA correlated with greater self-other representational distinction within the left pregenual anterior cingulate cortex (pgACC). Concurrently, the precuneus exhibited stronger parametric tracking of self-negative predictions versus others. Crucially, pgACC representational distinction during positive outcome processing significantly mediated the association between SA severity and heightened prediction-tracking in the precuneus. Conclusions: These findings offer a novel mechanistic framework, suggesting that an exaggerated neural segregation of the self from others drives hyper-vigilant, risk-sensitive social predictions in SA. This candidate circuit-level dynamic warrants further replication in clinical cohorts.

papers.title: A closed genome of Streptococcus agalactiae ST347/II reveals a composite integrative element coupling nisin P biosynthesis to erm(B) and tet(O) in Dominican group B Streptococcus
papers.abstract: Clindamycin is the alternative for intrapartum prophylaxis against group B Streptococcus in penicillin-allergic women, and whether it works depends on which lineages carry the resistance and on the mobile element that moves it. No Dominican group B Streptococcus genome has been closed. A Streptococcus agalactiae isolate from residual diagnostic material was sequenced twice on Oxford Nanopore, annotated, and screened against 83 genomes from a published Dominican maternal colonisation survey. The assembly is one circular chromosome of 2,066,859 bp with all seven rRNA operons resolved: ST347/CC19, serotype II, carrying erm(B), tet(O), mef(J) and msr(I). Two integrative conjugative elements were delimited: one of ~34 kb related to Tn5252 carrying erm(B) and tet(O), another of ~35 kb at a tRNA-Lys gene carrying mef(J) and msr(I). An eleven-gene class I lanthipeptide cluster lies 96 bp from the first element, on the same strand and with no annotated feature between them; its precursor encodes a 31-residue core identical to nisin P. The complete operon was found in 12 of the 83 genomes, 13 of 84 (15.5%) with the isolate. tet(O) was present in all 12 carriers and none of the 71 others (Fisher p = 1.03 x 10^-14), erm(B) in 12 of 12 against 3 of 71 (p = 4.70 x 10^-12). All eleven ST1 genomes lack both the operon and the nisin resistance protein; all 15 ST1010/IV genomes carry aac(6')-Ie/aph(2'')-Ia. Clindamycin resistance is therefore tightly associated with a lantibiotic-encoding element and contiguous with it in the one closed genome; in the drafts the relationship is statistical, and co-occurrence is not linkage. The ST1 absence predicts lineage-wide susceptibility, testable by deferred antagonism.

papers.title: Degree bias predicts, outperforms and improves machine learning phage-host interaction predictions
papers.abstract: Phages are promising therapeutics for difficult-to-treat bacterial infections. However, phages are highly specific in which bacterial strains they infect, necessitating extensive experimental screening for each patient isolate. Machine learning (ML) models predicting phage-host interactions from genomes are increasingly developed to prioritize phages for experimental screening. The Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic (AUROC) metric is standard for model evaluation, with reported high scores (0.7-0.95) suggesting strong predictive power. However, because phage-bacterium networks are highly structured, these scores can be inflated by "degree bias", the baseline likelihood of infection driven purely by average phage infectivity and bacterial susceptibility. Here, we show that an interaction-naive model based solely on network degrees accurately predicts and outperforms the global AUROC scores of five published ML models across ten datasets, indicating that global AUROC primarily reflects network structure rather than predicted interactions. Using randomized degree-conserved networks and degree-stratified evaluation, we isolate true interaction predictions and demonstrate that current ML model performance is far more modest than global AUROC suggests. Finally, we demonstrate that regressing out degree bias from training data improves interaction predictability and boosts global and stratified performance. Our work provides a critical framework for model evaluation and a straightforward route to improve ML-guided phage selection.

papers.title: mTORC1-dependent control of Hedgehog signaling mediates nutrient-responsive licensing of intestinal stem cell differentiation
papers.abstract: How progenitor cells couple their metabolic state to the regulation of fate and differentiation remains a fundamental question in tissue development and regeneration. Here, we identify a nutrient-responsive circuit that links progenitor anabolism to differentiation in the Drosophila midgut. We show that the mTORC1 downstream effector PWP1 is necessary and sufficient for differentiation of intestinal stem cell progeny toward the absorptive lineage in fed animals. In progenitors with high mTORC1 activity, PWP1 controls gene expression to promote Hedgehog (Hh) signaling, which cell autonomously drives progenitor differentiation into enterocytes. This circuit is constrained by feedback regulation, as elevated Hh activity inhibits mTORC1 and consequently excludes PWP1 from the nucleus. Disruption of the mTORC1-PWP1-Hh axis causes a progressive failure of enterocyte turnover during aging and reduced lifespan. While the aged midguts retain their barrier function, defective renewal leads to aging-associated deregulation of intestinal metabolism. Collectively, these observations support the concept of growth-dependent licensing of differentiation, whereby the nutrient-responsive anabolic state of a progenitor cell controls its lineage progression, consequently enabling organ renewal.

papers.title: NeuroWeave-3D: Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Completion for Brain Tumor Segmentation with Missing MRI Modalities
papers.abstract: Multi-parametric MRI segmentation models are accurate when all prescribed sequences are available but can be brittle under missing or corrupted modalities. We propose NeuroWeave-3D, a 3D glioma segmentation framework that treats missing modalities as uncertain evidence rather than deterministic channels to reconstruct. The model combines spatial modality routing, probabilistic latent feature completion, complete-to-missing consistency, and voxel-level uncertainty estimation. A curriculum over all non-empty MRI modality subsets trains one network for arbitrary sequence availability. We define a BraTS-centered evaluation that reports complete-input accuracy, macro and worst-case missing-modality performance, corruption robustness, calibration, and failure detection.

papers.title: High-throughput sequencing of unmethylated DNA (UMR-seq) reveals extensive epigenetic variation in the hypomethylome of diverse plant species
papers.abstract: The unmethylated regions (UMRs) in a genome can reveal the location of genes and gene regulatory loci. However, discovering UMR variation across and between entire genomes and disentangling the contribution of genetics and epigenetics to traits are challenging because they require separate and costly whole-DNA methylome and whole-genome genetic analyses. In many species this is prohibitively expensive for even a small number of samples, curtailing analysis on a population or breeding scale. Here we introduce UMR-seq, a method for the specific capture of UMRs from a genome and simultaneous sequencing of genetic variants in a single economical and scalable assay. UMR-seq charts the hypomethylome, revealing that it is highly enriched with functionally important regulatory loci. While UMRs are highly stable between vegetative tissues in plants, we find they are dynamic in the endosperm and vary substantially between accessions. Adaptable to diverse species, using this method we uncover a positive correlation between gene number in a species and UMR content, reflecting gene regulatory space in a genome. At 1/50th of the conventional cost of methylome sequencing in wheat, UMR-seq enables simultaneous population scale analysis of genetic and epigenetic variation in the functional genomic space. We reveal that in a panel of 187 elite wheat cultivars, profiling UMR variation improved genomic prediction across population groups, and UMR-based association mapping identified trait associations that were largely distinct from those detected with SNPs, providing new opportunities to understand trait biology and to enhance predictive breeding.

papers.title: Transmural Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics Nominates Candidate Disease Programs in Human Necrotizing Enterocolitis
papers.abstract: Background & Aims: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a life-threatening disease of premature infants marked by inflammation, ischemia, mucosal injury, and, in advanced cases, necrosis extending into deeper layers of the intestinal wall. Because NEC affects specialized, interacting cells in a developing intestine, we used single-nucleus transcriptomics to build a transmural, cell-type-resolved map and nominate hypothesis-generating disease programs distinct from maturation. Methods: Full-thickness intestinal specimens from fetal/prenatal controls, acute NEC cases, and infant controls were analyzed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq). Fetal and infant samples served as developmental references. Analyses included cell annotation, NEC-versus-infant differential expression, gene ontology (GO), cross-lineage recurrence, cell death signatures, and developmental maturity. Results: We profiled 53,735 nuclei by snRNA-seq and resolved 34 epithelial, stromal, vascular, immune, neuronal, glial, and smooth muscle populations. We used a morphology-based nuclei scoring system for sample selection that predicted high-quality transcript recovery. NEC nuclei were represented across this cellular landscape, with recurrent gene-expression changes suggesting shared inflammatory recruitment, antimicrobial/redox defense, stress adaptation, complement/vascular activation, reduced homeostatic signaling, and cell death-associated regulation. Developmental maturity analysis identified fetal-like expression levels in subsets of NEC-regulated genes. Proliferative crypt populations retained DNA repair/cell-cycle programs with inflammatory, hypoxic, and ER-stress features, while absorptive enterocytes showed reduced digestive, transport, detoxification, and terminal villus-function programs. Secretory-lineage changes implicated goblet mucus-barrier responses with reduced glycosylation, trafficking, and hydration; enteroendocrine changes in epithelial defense, metabolic stress, and neural signaling; and Paneth cell retention of antimicrobial effector transcripts despite altered ER quality control, autophagy, and granule delivery in NEC. Non-epithelial programs implicated stromal Wnt/BMP niche loss, impaired lymphatic drainage/scavenging, macrophage cytokine activation with reduced clearance machinery, neuroglial circuit defects, and altered smooth muscle contraction-relaxation balance. Conclusions: This single nuclear intestinal cell atlas nominates multicellular programs that may govern NEC initiation, progression toward tissue destruction, and resolution toward functional recovery.

papers.title: Latent Transforming Growth Factor Binding Protein-2 promotes microfibrillar TGF-β bioavailability to drive pathologic fibrosis in remote regions of infarcted hearts
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) initiates ventricular remodeling that extends beyond the infarct into remote, viable myocardium, where diffuse extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and stiffening contribute to progressive dysfunction and heart failure. Latent transforming growth factor binding protein 2 (LTBP2) is an injury-induced, microfibril-associated ECM glycoprotein that, among the LTBP family, does not covalently bind latent TGF-{beta}. We asked whether LTBP2 regulates remote remodeling after MI, and how a protein lacking latent TGF-{beta}-binding capacity could influence TGF-{beta}-dependent fibrosis. Wild-type and Ltbp2-null mice underwent permanent coronary ligation or sham surgery and were followed for 28 days by echocardiography and speckle-tracking strain analysis. Remote myocardium was assessed by histology, atomic force microscopy, and quantitative proteomics. Mechanism was interrogated in primary cardiac fibroblasts using a TGF-{beta} reporter assay. Sufficiency was tested with a fibrillin-1?binding module of LTBP2 delivered as purified protein or by lentiviral expression. LTBP2 was induced in injury-activated cardiac fibroblasts and localized to infarct and remote myocardium by 7 days post-MI. Ltbp2 deletion improved 28-day survival (P=0.0272) where Ltbp2-null hearts showed preserved ejection fraction and faster diastolic strain rates, with protection concentrated in segments remote from the infarct. Remote myocardium contained less interstitial collagen and was significantly less stiff. Proteomic profiling showed enrichment of ECM organization and TGF-{beta}-responsive programs in wild-type hearts that was attenuated in knockouts. In fibroblasts, loss of LTBP2 increased LTBP1 matrix incorporation and shifted TGF-{beta} from the soluble to the matrix-bound compartment; conversely, the minimal LTBP2 module bound fibrillin-1 directly and mobilized latent TGF-{beta} from established matrix within 20 minutes. LTBP2 drives maladaptive remodeling of remote myocardium after MI by limiting matrix sequestration of latent TGF-{beta} and expanding the activatable pool, resolving how an LTBP that does not bind latent TGF-{beta} amplifies TGF-{beta}- dependent fibrosis. LTBP2 and its fibrillin-1 interaction surface may be tractable targets.

papers.title: Few-shot regulatory sequence design with a genomic language model
papers.abstract: A central challenge in generative biology is translating knowledge learned from natural sequences and experiments into designs with desired functions. In-context learning (ICL) is an emergent capability of large language models that allows them to adapt to new tasks from a few examples without additional training, enabling these models to become general-purpose learners. Here, we show that the genome language model, Evo 2, exhibits generative ICL in biological sequence design. Prompting with just tens of examples conditions Evo 2 to generate novel and diverse regulatory DNA sequences without any additional training. Mechanistic analysis suggests that genomic ICL may originate from induction, similar to phenomena observed in natural language. Reinforcement learning leveraging sequence-to-function models as experiment-derived rewards further strengthens ICL. We first validate this approach by generating enhancers that drive cell-type-specific gene expression in three human cell lines. Extending this approach in vivo, enhancers designed using human regulatory element data selectively label layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the mouse cortex with high specificity and stronger activity than existing enhancers. Our study provides evidence of emergent properties in genomic sequence models and introduces a promising approach for improving functional conditioning in generative biology.

papers.title: Sensory representation by non-equilibrium flows of neural activity at the mesoscale of cortex
papers.abstract: We present a non-equilibrium theory of sensory perception and the mesoscale of sensory cortex. We propose that local neuron assemblies (cortical columns) toggle spontaneously between activity states (on and off) and that small populations of columns are coupled within and between areas of sensory cortex. The resulting network generates sudden, large-scale fluctuations and represents sensory inputs and perceptions by characteristic patterns of activity flows. The non-equilibrium dynamic is governed by the variational principle of maximal path entropy, or Maximum Caliber. Many current theories, by contrast, posit equilibrium dynamics and representation with activity states Our minimal model of sensory cortex describes populations of columns from two cortical areas and is fully constrained by empirical observations of `reversals' in perceived appearance, which occur spontaneously for visual, auditory, and tactile stimulation. We formalize representation by activity flows with dynamic Hamiltonian functions. Surprisingly, effective representation requires small-number fluctuations of toggling columns, as larger numbers would be dominated by hysteresis. Finally, we detail predictions for the microscale of spiking neurons that follow from on-off toggling and non-equilibrium dynamics. We conclude that the neural levels underlying perception are functionally organized in terms of activity flows. The inherent instability of non-equilibrium ensures active updating and renders all perceptions open to immediate revision. We conjecture that current theories of brain function (such as the Free Energy Principle) could be reformulated in terms of the variational principle of non-equilibrium, Maximum Caliber.

papers.title: Presynaptic PMCA interacts with Dlg, regulating in vivo synaptic calcium in Drosophila larval NMJ
papers.abstract: Precise regulation of presynaptic Ca2+is essential for neurotransmitter release and synaptic function. At the Drosophila larval neuromuscular junction (NMJ), the plasma membrane Ca2+-ATPase (PMCA) mediates presynaptic Ca2+; extrusion and is enriched in peri-active-zone membrane domains. Here, we investigated how PMCA distribution is regulated and contributes to synaptic function. Co-immunoprecipitation and super-resolution STED microscopy revealed that PMCA interacts and co-localizes with the MAGUK scaffold protein Discs large (Dlg) in discrete presynaptic membrane clusters. Neuronal depletion of the DlgS97 isoform disrupted PMCA clustering without substantially altering its abundance, redistributing the pump into smaller membrane puncta. Reporter assays further showed that PDZ-binding motifs in the PMCA C-terminus mediate its interaction with Dlg and are required for normal cluster formation. Electrophysiological analyses revealed that reducing either PMCA or Dlg increased spontaneous neurotransmitter release and enhanced asynchronous release following high-frequency stimulation. PMCA depletion also prolonged postsynaptic current decay during repetitive stimulation, implicating PMCA in the rapid regulation of presynaptic Ca2+; signals. Together, these findings identify Dlg as a key organizer of presynaptic PMCA and establish a link between synaptic scaffold organization and Ca2+; homeostasis in vivo. Our results demonstrate that PMCA contributes to maintaining resting presynaptic Ca2+; levels, restoring Ca2+; homeostasis after repetitive stimulation, and regulating Ca2+; dynamics following a single stimulus. These findings highlight the importance of the nanoscale organization of Ca2+; extrusion machinery in controlling neurotransmitter release at the Drosophila NMJ.

papers.title: Prediction of early Toxoplasma gondii infection during pregnancy combining host biomarkers and machine learning
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii is a major cause of reproductive failure and severe gestational complications in both humans and small ruminants and early diagnosis is essential to prevent adverse outcomes. In sheep, congenital toxoplasmosis can trigger early fetal death (EFD) during the acute phase of the infection (days 7-14 post-infection) when conventional diagnosis methods are ineffective. Therefore, this study aimed to identify early infection biomarkers using a machine learning approach to support EFD diagnosis and providing a translational foundation for early diagnostic strategies in human toxoplasmosis. For that, 27 serum biomarkers (cytokines, acute-phase proteins, oxidative stress and hemostatic parameters) were evaluated during the early stage of infection in 22 pregnant sheep experimentally challenged with T. gondii and 6 uninfected controls. To assess diagnostic specificity, models were tested using sera from animals experimentally infected with other abortifacient agents (Neospora caninum and Chlamydia abortus) and validated with samples from 19 natural abortion outbreaks. A four-biomarkers panel, encompassing CXCL9, CXCL10, IFN-{gamma}, and serum amyloid A, achieved over 74% accuracy in the specific detection of early T. gondii infection and 100% of sensitivity when studying natural infection cases. This approach might support the development of rapid diagnostic strategies, improving early intervention and disease management in livestock production systems. Its translation to human medicine could also aid in addressing current diagnostic gaps and facilitate timely interventions to prevent congenital toxoplasmosis and pregnancy loss in women.

papers.title: Cellular composition and the interpretation of candidate RNA readouts of trogocytosis in colorectal cancer
papers.abstract: Background: RNA measurements of genes associated with trogocytosis may reflect cellular composition rather than contact-dependent membrane acquisition. We evaluated an eight-gene candidate module in colorectal cancer (CRC) using expression- and lineage-matched random modules, independent compartment analysis and patient-level inference. A separate rare-transcript definition and cancer-model fitness screens provided complementary analyses. Results: In 62 GSE178341 patients, the module correlated with T-cell fraction ({rho}=0.767), but this association was typical of 10,000 matched modules (null median 0.766; one-sided empirical P=0.493; equal-tail two-sided P=0.985). A post hoc closest-10% matching sensitivity gave P=0.571. In 23 independent GSE132465 patients, the tumour-wide correlation was 0.735 (permutation P=0.00060) and the epithelial correlation was 0.376 (P=0.0892). The difference in absolute correlations was 0.359, with a 95% confidence interval of -0.041 to 0.759, leaving attenuation uncertain. Among 43,817 leukocytes, 16 CEACAM5-positive candidates arose from four patients; 15 had expression [≤]2 transcripts per million. Candidate counts were threshold-sensitive. No survival association was detected for the module in two cohorts. SCD fitness dependency reproduced across CRC organoids and cell lines, whereas adjusted SCD-VPS72 and exploratory ATF3-SMYD2 co-dependencies did not. Exploratory CH25H, ATF3 and FADS2 analyses yielded no Hallmark enrichment meeting the multiple-testing threshold. Conclusions: Matched-module calibration placed the strong association with T-cell abundance within the range expected for comparable immune-lineage genes. Independent compartment analysis was consistent with a contribution from cellular composition, although attenuation remained uncertain. These results identify the comparison conditions needed to interpret the tested RNA readouts. Linking them to membrane transfer requires event-resolved protein measurements.

papers.title: Serial dependence carries the action that produced the previous report
papers.abstract: Serial dependence pulls current judgments toward the recent past, but what is carried forward is debated: the previous stimulus, the previous decision, or something about the report itself. Three magnitude-reproduction experiments separated these sources. Participants viewed dot arrays that varied independently in duration and numerosity, then reproduced the cued dimension by holding a key while a display accumulated, so that both magnitudes were produced through the same action. A response-history model partitioned the attraction into previous-stimulus and previous-response paths. The previous response predicted cross-dimensional attraction after controlling for the previous and current stimuli: a numerosity report biased the next duration judgment and vice versa (Experiment 1), also when each task used its own response key (Experiment 2). A task switch weakened this carryover without abolishing it. Experiment 3 randomized, trial by trial, whether a reported number required a long or a short key hold. The influence of a previous number on the next duration judgment changed with this mapping, showing that reported value alone did not account for carryover. Conventional stimulus-based measures showed none of this cross-task history. Serial dependence can therefore carry the trace of the action through which a previous judgment was expressed, bounded but not gated by task context.

papers.title: The Braarudosphaera bigelowii genome reveals cellular remodeling around a nitrogen-fixing organelle
papers.abstract: Braarudosphaera bigelowii hosts the nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterial organelle UCYN-A, or the nitroplast, but the absence of a reference genome has limited investigation of the genomic features accompanying this association. Here, we present nuclear and organellar genome resources for the cultured B. bigelowii strain FR-21. The assembly comprises a 472.1-Mb nuclear genome together with representative nitroplast, chloroplast, and mitochondrial genomes of 1.49 Mb, 107 kb, and 44 kb, respectively. The four genomic compartments have strongly differentiated GC compositions, consistent with their distinct evolutionary origins. The large nuclear genome does not appear to reflect a corresponding expansion of protein-coding capacity. Repeat annotation indicates that approximately 77% of the nuclear assembly is repetitive, leaving approximately 108 Mb of nonrepetitive sequence containing roughly 16,000 predicted protein-coding genes. Phylogenomic analysis places B. bigelowii within the expected diversity of haptophytes, indicating that its unusual diazotrophic lifestyle is not associated with an anomalous phylogenetic position. Comparative analysis of nitrogen metabolism genes reveals extensive remodeling of host nitrogen acquisition and assimilation. B. bigelowii lacks major components required for nitrate and nitrite assimilation and has reduced capacity to use urea, cyanate, and several internally recycled nitrogen sources. In contrast, ammonium transport and the glutamine synthetase-glutamate synthase pathway are retained. This combination suggests reduced flexibility in nitrogen use and a host metabolism increasingly centered on ammonium supplied by the nitroplast. B. bigelowii also encodes an expanded set of flavodoxin and cryptochrome genes. Eleven of 14 flavodoxin candidates and 21 of 39 cryptochrome candidates contained motifs linked to nitroplast targeting. Together with previous evidence that some of these proteins are abundantly imported into the nitroplast, these expansions point to host-encoded roles in nitroplast redox metabolism and diel regulation. These genome resources establish a foundation for investigating nitroplast protein import, host-organelle metabolic integration, and the genomic consequences of acquiring an intracellular nitrogen-fixing compartment. They further show that the evolution of the B. bigelowii-UCYN-A relationship involved substantial remodeling of genome architecture and nitrogen metabolism in both partners.

papers.title: Spatially resolved single-cell atlas reveals cortical glial reactivity associated with regions of neuronal growth programs in both hemispheres after stroke
papers.abstract: Recovery after focal motor cortex stroke relies on structural remodeling of neuronal circuits in the perilesional cortex (PLC) and contralesional cortex (CLC). Although transcriptomic studies have identified distinct reactive glial states after stroke, how their spatial organization relates to processes of tissue degeneration and neuronal circuit remodeling remains poorly understood. We used a custom 347-gene Xenium spatial transcriptomics panel to profile approximately 650,000 cells across both hemispheres of male and female mice 7 days after photothrombotic stroke. We identified injury-associated myeloid populations concentrated within the infarct and reactive astrocytes enriched in the glial scar. Distinct reactive populations also extended into spared cortex, including an interferon-associated myeloid population and a reactive astrocyte population that was present in both PLC and CLC. Spatial mapping further revealed elevated neuronal growth-associated gene expression in both regions, particularly among layer 5 extratelencephalic projection neurons, which include corticospinal neurons. Intriguingly, reactive glial populations were enriched in regions exhibiting elevated neuronal growth-associated gene expression, including areas of the CLC containing axons and presynaptic terminals originating from the PLC. Together, these findings reveal a striking spatial association between reactive glial populations and neurons exhibiting elevated growth-associated gene expression and support glial-neuronal interactions as potential targets for promoting circuit remodeling and functional recovery after stroke.

papers.title: Correlation-resolved sum-frequency generation microscopy of biological tissue with bright twin beams
papers.abstract: Sum-frequency generation (SFG) driven by bright twin beams from high-gain parametric down-conversion yields a coherent component from correlated mode pairs and an incoherent component from uncorrelated mode combinations. Modal correlations can enhance coherent SFG in anisotropic nonlinear media, for example by extending the effective interaction length. Whether these correlations can also benefit image formation in biological tissue, where molecular organization and refractive index vary spatially, remains unknown. Here we address this question by performing SFG imaging of biological tissue using bright twin beams as the excitation source. Spectral decomposition yields co-registered coherent and incoherent images from a single acquisition. In mouse skeletal muscle, the coherent-component image revealed sarcomere periodicity with a Bragg-spot-to-background ratio approximately 40 times that of the incoherent-component image. In fresh human dermis, the coherent-component image showed greater Fourier power in the 0.30-0.50 m-1 band and greater fractional autocovariance decay at short spatial lags than the incoherent-component image. These results demonstrate that twin-beam correlations can enhance contrast and detectability at selected spatial frequencies in heterogeneous tissue. Correlation-resolved SFG microscopy thus offers a route to label-free characterization of tissue microstructure with bright quantum light, with potential applications in biomedical research.

papers.title: The AP-1 clathrin adaptor has a conserved role in recycling resident proteins of the trans-Golgi network
papers.abstract: Although the AP-1 clathrin adaptor has been studied for decades, its role in membrane trafficking has been ambiguous. Here, we systematically investigated the localization and function of mammalian AP-1. This adaptor associates with the trans-Golgi network (TGN) and with TGN-related recycling endosomes. Disruption of the 1A subunit of AP-1 has only a mild effect on the Golgi export of secretory cargoes, but it causes depletion from the Golgi of multiple transmembrane TGN proteins. Live-cell imaging and a cell surface labeling assay indicate that when TGN proteins are unable to bind AP-1, they exit the Golgi to the plasma membrane. Our interpretation is that the vesicles generated with AP-1 recycle transmembrane TGN proteins, thereby keeping those proteins in the Golgi during cisternal maturation. The clathrin adaptor epsinR seems to function as a partner for AP-1 in recycling a subset of TGN proteins. These results closely align with studies of AP-1 function in yeast, suggesting that the conserved core role of AP-1 is the intra-Golgi recycling of TGN proteins.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Structural Prioritization of Sulforaphane Targets in Neurodegeneration: A Multi-Dataset In Silico Study
papers.abstract: Sulforaphane (SFN), a natural isothiocyanate from cruciferous vegetables, exerts neuroprotective effects through mechanisms extending beyond canonical Nrf2/ARE activation. Here, we developed a multi-dataset computational framework integrating transcriptomic analysis, multi-criteria target prioritization, and structural docking evaluation. R- and S-SFN were docked against 693 prioritized targets using AutoDock Vina, followed by cross-validation, brain expression profiling, and molecular dynamics simulations. Four genes (IGSF9, KCNQ5, KCTD12, and NFIX) were dysregulated across all four datasets. Among 693 targets, 88 showed favorable predicted docking scores (deltaG less than or equal to -4.0 kcal/mol), with 65 (73.9%) exhibiting expression in at least one GTEx brain region. Independent cross-validation showed significant enrichment of prioritized targets in an SFN-responsive Alzheimer disease transcriptomic dataset (OR = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.08-1.89, p = 0.0104). Complementary disease gene set enrichment confirmed that 33% of strong hits (29/88) overlap established neurodegeneration gene sets across AD, PD, and ALS - including ACHE, target of FDA-approved anti-AD drugs - with highly significant enrichment across all three disease categories (OR range: 67-127, all p less than 0.001). R-SFN showed a modest but statistically detectable preference over S-SFN across the 88 strong hits (Wilcoxon p = 0.0081; paired t-test p = 0.0047). TMEM45A, GRIK2, and FABP3 emerged as putative neurodegeneration-relevant targets. Molecular dynamics simulations supported the structural stability of R-SFN poses for TMEM45A, GRIK2, and FABP3, while MM-GBSA estimated favorable binding energies for GRIK2 (deltaG_bind = -19.78 kcal/mol) and FABP3 (deltaG_bind = -14.49 kcal/mol). These findings generate testable hypotheses regarding previously underexplored molecular targets that may contribute to the neuroprotective actions of SFN.

papers.title: The Muskox Way: Humans, plants and animals in northeast Greenland through the Holocene
papers.abstract: The Muskox Way hypothesis suggests that the first humans entering northeast Greenland from Arctic Canada followed and hunted muskox. Yet whether muskox arrived before people remains debated, as only two bones predate the Independence culture (4500-3900 cal BP). More broadly, the arrival of plants and animals, and how the three periods of human settlement related to ecosystem changes, remain poorly understood. We analysed sedimentary ancient DNA from lakes in Wandel Dal (Late Sommersoe and Midsommersoe) and Zackenberg, identifying 121 native plants and nine animal taxa. In Wandel Dal, the plant assemblage indicates a warmer climate than today about 8200-3900 years ago, followed by an abrupt change in flora and sedimentation rate at 3900 cal BP, especially at Midsommersoe. Muskox DNA is present continuously at Midsommersoe from 7400 cal BP, about three millennia before humans arrived. The Zackenberg record dates to 12,200 cal BP, with arctic forbs, grasses, ferns and crowberry in the earliest layers, willow from 8200 cal BP and birch from 7200 cal BP, but muskox only in the last 2500 years, the latter period coinciding with Greenlandic Dorset culture. The arrival of the Thule culture in 1400 CE coincides with a slight increase in plant richness at Wandel Dal and an increase in mammal detections. Reindeer occurred only in samples older than 6000 years, consistent with their absence from archaeological bone records. Overall, humans arrived long after the first megafauna and appear to have had limited impact on their populations, although cultural periods coincided with environmental changes.

papers.title: MCT4-Associated Lactate Export Defines Myeloid Metabolic Reprogramming during Head and Neck Cancer Progression
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) development is accompanied by metabolic remodeling of the tumor microenvironment, yet how metabolic programs evolve across specific cell populations during tumor progression remains poorly understood. We integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing data from five HNSCC cohorts comprising 645,351 cells from 114 patients and inferred metabolic flux using single-cell Flux Estimation Analysis (scFEA). Myeloid cells showed the highest and most consistent metabolic allocation to lactate export among major cell types. In ten patients with paired normal mucosa and carcinoma, myeloid lactate-export allocation increased from 1.72% to 3.31% of total inferred metabolic flux, with an increase in every patient. SPP1+ macrophages showed the highest lactate-export allocation in carcinoma. Lactate export was predominantly associated with MCT4/SLC16A3. In carcinoma, myeloid SLC16A3 expression exceeded SLC16A1 by 17-fold, and CPTAC-HNSCC confirmed tumor enrichment of MCT4 protein. Together, these findings identify increased MCT4-associated lactate export as a prominent feature of myeloid metabolic reprogramming during HNSCC progression.

papers.title: The phage-host interaction landscape of Mycobacterium smegmatis
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages are highly specific predators of bacterial hosts, but the molecular mechanisms governing their entry across the complex mycobacterial cell envelope remain poorly defined. Utilizing a genome-wide CRISPR interference library in the model organism Mycobacterium smegmatis against a phylogenetically representative collection of 70 mycobacteriophages, and subsequent efficiency of plating assays, we mapped the host susceptibility determinants for phage infection. This screen established a spatial continuum of infection requirements spanning from the surface accessible outer membrane components down to cytoplasmic proteins. The four major outer membrane Mycobacterium smegmatis porins (Msp) emerged as the dominant candidate receptor family for 46 diverse phages, representing the first protein receptors proposed within this group. Interrogating the asymmetric outer bilayer also implicated cell envelope glycolipids as candidate receptors for 14 phages, resolving into glycopeptidolipid sub-lineages. Beneath the M. smegmatis mycomembrane, arabinogalactan functions as a determinant for 5 phages, while the inner membrane lipid transporter MmpL11 and the global nucleoid-associated protein Lsr2 represent determinant factors for 14 and 31 phages respectively. Although physical deletions of major porins genes trigger spontaneous regulatory pathways that upregulate silent backup paralogues, transcriptional knockdowns circumvent suppressor accumulation, revealing single-gene dependencies. Cluster analysis demonstrated that host determinant usage decouples from whole-genome viral phylogeny, indicating that standard phylogenetic groupings fail to predict surface recognition profiles. Ultimately, mapping these host dependencies reveals an evolutionary strategy where phages target highly redundant or abundant host proteins to exploit physiological liabilities, presenting a robust molecular blueprint for the rational engineering of escape-resistant therapeutic phage cocktails.

papers.title: Integrin α3β1 is required for alveolar-capillary barrier formation through regulation of epithelial differentiation
papers.abstract: Laminin-binding integrins regulate critical morphogenic processes, but their specific roles in lung development are unknown. In this study, we combined an in vivo model of epithelial 3 subunit deletion in the murine lung with a multiomics approach to investigate the role of the epithelial 3{beta}1 integrin during murine lung development. We demonstrate that 3{beta}1 integrin is dispensable for airway branching morphogenesis due to delayed epithelial expression. Instead, in vivo deletion of 3{beta}1 integrin impaired alveolar epithelial cell differentiation and disrupted alveolar-capillary barrier formation, functionally limiting gas exchange. A discontinuous alveolar BM contained abnormal collagen IV and laminin networks and widened the gap between epithelial and endothelial cells in the alveolar-capillary barrier niche. Mechanistically, mice deficient in epithelial 3{beta}1 integrin possessed an intracellular trafficking and secretion defect for BM components. Thus, integrin 3{beta}1 orchestrates the temporal maturation of alveolar epithelial cells required for organization of the alveolar-capillary barrier.

papers.title: Linear NeuroPaint: An Efficient Baseline for Cross-Session Neural Alignment and Inpainting
papers.abstract: Large-scale Neuropixels recordings sample many brain areas, but no single experimental session records every area of interest. NeuroPaint, a transformer-based autoencoder, integrates such recordings by aligning area-specific latent dynamics across sessions and "inpainting" activity in unrecorded areas. Could a linear model, which would be computationally efficient and potentially more interpretable, suffice to achieve this? To address this question, we introduce Linear NeuroPaint, a linear variant of NeuroPaint, and evaluate it on two multi-area Neuropixels datasets. Linear NeuroPaint achieves strong predictive performance on recorded areas, however, it is less accurate than nonlinear models at cross-area inpainting, despite extensive hyperparameter optimization. Moreover, its parameters are not readily interpretable: incomplete cross-session alignment leads parameter-defined neuron clusters to exhibit heterogeneous response profiles. Together, these results show the limits of what a linear model can extract from multi-session recordings. Nevertheless, Linear NeuroPaint provides a computationally efficient baseline for benchmarking multi-session neural models.

papers.title: Islet size, cellular composition, and spatial location are interconnected in the human pancreas
papers.abstract: Stem cell-derived (SC) islets hold promise as a transformative therapy for type 1 diabetes (T1D). To enhance graft uniformity, SC-islet organoids are often dissociated and reaggregated into standardized sizes. However, how endocrine cell composition varies with islet size in native human islets remains largely unknown. Defining this relationship is essential for establishing physiological benchmarks for islet engineering for transplantation. In this study, we examined the relationships among islet size, endocrine cell composition, and spatial distribution throughout whole pancreata from 10 age-matched, non-diabetic male subjects. Insulin-, glucagon-, and somatostatin-positive endocrine cells were identified as single-, double-, and triple-hormone populations ranging from non-islet single endocrine cells and small clusters (niSSCs) to large islets. Approximately 80% of the total endocrine area was contained in islets positive for all three hormones. Islet size strongly correlated with endocrine composition. Specifically, larger islets had increased alpha-cell fractions and reduced beta-cell fractions, while delta-cell fractions were consistent across sizes. Spatial analysis revealed that niSSCs, mono-, and tri-hormone islets frequently exhibit a clustered distribution. Additionally, tri-hormone islets were positioned near the core of the pancreas, whereas mono-somatostatin islets were often localized in the periphery. These findings were consistent across all three pancreatic regions (head, body and tail).

papers.title: PaleoRigor: a bounded research agent with a reproducible evidence trail for paleomicrobiome data processing
papers.abstract: Background: Ancient microbial evidence informs research on past health, diet, and environments, but its scarcity and susceptibility to contamination demand care in selecting and processing data. Language models can now turn a research request into an analysis plan, but an unconstrained planner may reference files that do not exist, apply operations a format forbids, or answer a question the data cannot settle. A planner used on such evidence therefore needs to be bounded, and its decisions recoverable afterwards. Results: We developed PaleoRigor around three commitments. Agent: a language model plans the analysis. Constraint: a validator checks every file reference, format and step dependency before anything runs, execution is restricted to predefined local modules, and a planning contract directs the model to refuse out-of-scope requests with a named reason code rather than answer them. Reproducibility: each run is exported with its plan, intermediate files, checksums and decisions. In a preregistered, frozen held-out evaluation, PaleoRigor passed 23 of 24 runs (95.8%; Wilson 95% confidence interval, 79.8-99.3%): 11 of 12 supported runs and all 12 prespecified boundary decisions. An ablation that removed this planning contract from the same model passed 19 of 24 (79.2%). Repeating the frozen design with a second model configuration yielded 24 of 24 successes for PaleoRigor and 19 of 24 for the ablated arm. Pooled post hoc across both configurations, PaleoRigor passed 47 of 48 runs (97.9%), compared with 38 of 48 (79.2%) for the ablated arms. All 96 run labels were recomputed from retained records and matched. Dataset-level tests matched read counts and compressed-file sizes for six public sequencing records and documented the removal of 114 duplicate sequence entries. A retraction-associated audit illustrated how expert review limited conclusions to file-level evidence. Conclusions: For paleomicrobiome data, pairing a language-model agent with explicit constraints and a reproducible record makes the agent's proposed analysis reviewable before its outputs support a biological claim. PaleoRigor delivers checked inputs, a recorded transformation history and a named reason for each request it refuses, and runs as a local desktop application. It prepares data for specialist analysis; ancient-DNA authentication and biological interpretation remain with the paleobiologist.

papers.title: The transcription factor THAP11 is a general regulator of early embryonic polarization
papers.abstract: During mouse embryogenesis, three sequential waves of cell polarization occur in the 8-cell-morula trophectoderm (TE), E3.5-E4.5 primitive endoderm (PrE), and E4.5-E5.5 epiblast (Epi), driving cell fate determination and morphogenic events that lay the foundation for embryonic development. However, it is not clear whether a general regulator that functions in all three waves of polarization exists. Here, we demonstrate that transcription factor THAP11 is such a general regulator. Using a novel mouse model combining genetic knockout and an inducible degron system, we demonstrate that stage-specific acute THAP11 depletion causes the failure of the three waves of cell polarization, resulting in defective blastocyst formation, PrE maturation, and Epi lumenogenesis, respectively. Mechanistically, THAP11 does not directly regulate pluripotency genes but drives polarization through both stage-specific and conserved chromatin-binding that commonly activate polarity programs, including Golgi vesicle transport. THAP11 activates polarity genes by promoting chromatin accessibility at their promoters. THAP11, together with stage-specific regulators, sequentially paces the timing of cell polarization. Collectively, our study establishes THAP11 as a general regulator of embryonic morphogenesis.

papers.title: Somatic genetic variation shapes clonal selection of memory NK cells
papers.abstract: In adaptive immunity, antigen receptor specificity and affinity drive clonal selection, but what enables individual innate lymphocytes to gain a selective advantage without rearranged antigen receptors remains unknown. We traced somatic mutations in human natural killer (NK) cells, revealing extensive clonal dominance in cytomegalovirus-associated memory, with individual genetically diversified clones comprising up to 95% of the population, originating early in life and expanding over years. Their genetic evolution demonstrated positive selection of acquired coding mutations, linking somatic variation to NK cell clonal fitness. Among candidate drivers, we identified mutations in the chromatin regulator KMT2D, whose induced deletion in mature NK cells conferred a competitive advantage following infection in vivo. These findings establish somatic evolution as a fundamental mechanism shaping innate immune memory.

papers.title: Varied forms of mutant tRNA mistranslation produce distinct phenotypes across multiple model organisms
papers.abstract: Mutant tRNA mistranslation is a phenomenon in which specific tRNA gene mutations cause translational errors wherein amino acids incorporated during translation differ from those coded by mRNA sequences. The biological consequences of mutant tRNA mistranslation are highly complex and contextual, but are often deleterious. Importantly, many variables exist that are likely to affect the outcomes of any one mutant mistranslating tRNA; biochemical characteristics of the exchanged amino acids, frequency of use, identity of mistranslated products, and so on. Here, we generate a carefully curated array of tRNA mutants to assess which characteristics of mistranslating tRNA variants are most predictive of deleterious phenotypes. We find that toxicity often arises from mutant tRNAs that induce dramatic changes in biochemical properties between exchanged amino acids, as well as mistranslation that occurs more frequently. Importantly, exceptions are also observed to each of these general rules, implying instead that some deliriousness may arise from more granular, product-specific mechanisms. Additionally, quantification of mistranslation via mass spectrometry demonstrates a weak relationship between quantity of mistranslated products and severity of toxic phenotypes. Lastly, despite previous establishment of mutant mistranslating tRNA models in Drosophila melanogaster, incorporation of higher frequency mistranslating tRNA variants was largely unsuccessful, and incorporation of lower frequency mistranslating tRNA variants produces no detectable developmental phenotypes. These experiments support the notion that although general rules may be capable of reasonably predicting their consequences, each mistranslating tRNA variant warrants individual consideration and investigation for thorough understanding of its biological outcomes and precise mechanisms of toxicity.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN: Evaluating phage-antibiotic synergy in differentiated primary airway epithelial cultures against Pseudomonas aeruginosa
papers.abstract: The authors have withdrawn this manuscript because subsequent and more comprehensive analyses conducted after posting this preprint has resulted in revised interpretations of findings. The updated analyses has changed our interpretation of the interactions between bacteriophages and antibiotics, which are central to the study's conclusions. Therefore, the authors do not wish this work to be cited as reference for the project. If you have any questions, please contact the corresponding author.

papers.title: Agrochemical-responsive gene expression control systems for modulating plant development and metabolism
papers.abstract: Precise temporal control of gene expression is critical for studying plant biology and engineering complex crop traits. Current systems enable chemically inducible regulation but rely on costly or agriculturally impractical inducers and lack the flexibility needed to regulate combinations of native loci and transgenes. In this work, we elucidate the design rules for control systems, based on Cas9 and Cre recombinase fused to the ecdysone receptor (EcR), which respond to a widely used agrochemical methoxyfenozide (MF). First, we validated the function of both circuits in transient assays and explored how transduction properties can be modulated by engineering nuclear trafficking dynamics. We next characterized both the Cas9-based and recombinase-based systems by using them to regulate fluorescent reporters in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana plants. Here, we demonstrate systemic activation following root application of MF, validating the use of an agriculturally compatible inducer for whole-plant gene regulation. Finally, we validated the utility of the inducible Cas-based SynTF system to regulate multigene pathways and control both metabolic and developmental pathways. Together, these results elucidate design considerations for agrochemical-inducible control systems and demonstrate their utility for temporally regulating plant phenotypes. These synthetic circuits provide a versatile framework for engineering complex traits using an agriculturally compatible inducer.

papers.title: Tunable kinetic destabilization governs RNA polymerase passage through a DNA-bound transcription factor
papers.abstract: Eukaryotic transcription factors recognize short motifs, creating abundant binding sites within gene bodies and potential collisions with elongating RNA polymerases, yet how such encounters are resolved remains unclear. Here, we use optical tweezers to monitor RNA polymerase transcription through DNA-bound Egr-1, a zinc-finger transcription factor. Using DNA-fluctuation suppression as a readout of polymerase arrival, we show that Egr-1 delays elongation in an orientation- and rNTP-dependent manner, whereas force measurements indicate that RNAP does not bypass the TF by mechanical eviction. Instead, RNAP destabilizes the Egr-1-DNA complex over a short, structured interaction zone, increasing TF dissociation non-monotonically with distance. Monte Carlo simulations incorporating these kinetic changes recapitulate passage-time distributions. CpG methylation shortens Egr-1 residence time and largely eliminates the TF-dependent delay, suggesting a role for gene-body methylation in reducing kinetic barriers to elongation. These results reveal DNA-bound TFs as tunable barriers that locally shape transcription elongation.

papers.title: Genetic effects of plant plant interactions depend on neighbor identity and environmental context
papers.abstract: Plant-plant interactions shape community productivity and resilience, yet how genetic variation influences these interactions remains poorly understood. We conducted multi-environment field phenotyping of 200 common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) lines grown in association with three maize (Zea mays ssp. mays) landraces to characterize the determinants of interspecific interactions. Our results reveal that maize landraces constitute distinct biotic environments, and interactions were strongly asymmetric, with maize acting as the dominant competitor. Bean responses to the identity of the maize partner involved phenology, vegetative development, productivity, and root architecture, and varied across field environments, with no evidence of bean local adaptation. We used genome-wide association to link variation across the bean genome to variation in bean and maize traits, thereby capturing both direct and indirect genetic effects, and tested for maize bean interactions. We identified six genomic regions with indirect effects: three with stable effects across maize partners and three whose effects varied with maize partner identity, including candidate genes involved in neighbor perception and facilitative interactions. Our findings demonstrate that the phenotypic effects of genetic variation extend beyond individual plants, with competitive tolerance modulated by the genetic identity of neighboring plants and the environment.

papers.title: Salt stress shifts wild tomato root systems toward transport efficiency along a gravitropism-constrained Pareto front
papers.abstract: - Root system architecture balances the carbon cost of building roots (wiring cost) against transport speed to the shoot (conduction delay). Wild tomato (S.
