The results demonstrate that the level of cap misalignment typically observed in newborn imaging can affect the spatial accuracy of reconstructed functional images, particularly in cases with larger probe displacements. These findings provide a quantitative basis for adopting more conservative interpretations of group-level functional brain activity and functional connectivity results, and strongly support the routine use of registration methods in infant HD-DOT studies.

papers.title: An interferon-like off-switch in invertebrates: Vago4 downregulates Domeless to restrain JAK/STAT signaling
papers.abstract: Whether invertebrates possess a functional interferon (IFN)-like system remains controversial, as canonical IFN ligands and their receptors are absent from invertebrate genomes. Although Vago proteins in Drosophila and shrimp are compelling functional analogs of IFN, direct evidence for a canonical cytokine-receptor axis and, importantly, for how such signaling is restrained to prevent excessive immune activation, has been lacking. Here, we identify Vago4 as a bona fide ligand of Domeless, the canonical type I cytokine receptor upstream of JAK/STAT signaling. Vago4 binds the extracellular CBM1 and CBM2 domains of Domeless, triggering receptor endocytosis followed by lysosomal trafficking and K27-linked ubiquitination-dependent proteasomal degradation. This ligand-induced receptor downregulation serves as a negative feedback mechanism that restrains excessive JAK/STAT activation. During acute Vibrio infection, Vago4 silencing accelerated shrimp mortality, whereas recombinant Vago4 alleviated inflammatory lesions and oxidative stress, enhanced phagocytosis, and improved survival, phenocopying JAK or STAT knockdown. Thus, by downregulating Domeless, Vago4 limits immunopathology and defines an IRF-Vago4-Domeless-JAK/STAT IFN-like axis in invertebrates, offering new insight into the evolution of IFN-mediated immune regulation.

papers.title: Negative sampling shapes benchmark discrimination and experimental retrieval in synthetic-lethality prediction
papers.abstract: Benchmarks for synthetic-lethality prediction compare known interactions with sampled negatives. Does performance under degree matching predict which gene pairs a model can prioritize? Across five gene-disjoint folds, matching test negatives by degree in the full labelled graph brought four methods near chance. SLMGAE states selected by benchmark test F1 had a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.501 on matched negatives. The same states retrieved 21 experimental hits among 198 SPIDR selections, versus 8.00 expected by chance. Comparable enrichment was not established in three other screens. Changing training negatives increased HAP1 retrieval from 3.6 to 15.8 hits for logistic regression; swapping 28 endpoint coefficients transferred most of this difference. Rewiring positive pairs while keeping the original matched negatives reduced HAP1 retrieval for logistic regression and gradient boosting. This preserved individual gene degrees but also changed their joint distribution, limiting attribution to partner identity. A density-ratio estimate closed 55-65% of the logistic-regression shortlist gap across four previously evaluated pools, with limited transfer to nonlinear models. Frozen predictions met the shortlist criterion for one of two new graph relations. Benchmark discrimination and experimental retrieval therefore warrant separate evaluation at the intended screening budget.

papers.title: scRM: A single-cell foundation model trained on scRNA-seq reads
papers.abstract: To our knowledge, scRM is the first single-cell foundation model trained on sequencing reads, demonstrating that raw data pretraining is not only feasible but competitive at a fraction of the computational cost. We anticipate that scaling this framework and exploring alternative architectures will unlock biological information inaccessible to count models and extend the dataset-specific pretraining it already makes possible. The source code is available at https://github.com/altoslabs/scRM.

papers.title: A vagal-to-sympathetic reflex controls lung vascular leak
papers.abstract: Dynamic regulation of the vascular barrier is required for innate immunity, yet excessive leak endangers vulnerable organs like the lungs, where edema stiffens tissue and threatens breathing. Using a chemogenetic screen, we discover a vagal-to-sympathetic reflex that controls pulmonary vascular leak. The reflex originates in a previously-uncharacterized population of polymodal, alveolus-innervating vagal sensory neurons marked by Cysltr2. Stimulating CYSLTR2 neurons increases lung fluid within minutes, whereas sustained activation elicits perivascular edema and respiratory dysfunction. Silencing them during allergen challenge reduces leak and improves lung mechanics. Rather than acting locally, CYSLTR2 neurons relay centrally to sympathetic efferents to broadcast effects throughout lung vasculature. This pathway thus forms an axis of organ defense that can go awry in disease, suggesting new ways to control lung fluid balance.

papers.title: Practical Identifiability of a Minimal Adaptive Learning-Gain Model for Binary Feedback: A Simulation Study
papers.abstract: Social learning is shaped by distinct computational components--baseline beliefs (prior mean), feedback sensitivity (learning gain), and temporal uncertainty (drift)--that empirical designs rarely disentangle. We evaluate practical identifiability and predictive performance of a parsimonious four-parameter adaptive learning-gain model for binary feedback, where a latent belief about positive-outcome probability updates deterministically between observations and an internal confidence-precision state decays each trial. {sigma}, {omega}, and {lambda} are internal, model-defined variables--not validated psychological constructs. Using fixed-seed simulations, we report four findings. Joint maximum-likelihood recovery is poor: on a 24-condition grid (T=80), {sigma} and {omega} show near-zero tolerance-based recovery ([≤]0.002) across tolerances 0.3-1.0, {lambda} recovers at 0.078-0.263, and longer sequences do not improve recovery. Profile-likelihood and trade-off diagnostics show flat regions for {sigma} and {omega} and an asymmetric {lambda} profile, indicating weak practical (not structural) identifiability. A fitting-parity audit fixed a return-order bug in the fixed-gain candidate. After correction, block-level model discrimination is 0.48 (72/150) under common bounds--above chance (p<0.001)--but is driven almost entirely by Rescorla-Wagner (0.88-0.90); the adaptive filter and its nested fixed-gain restriction remain indistinguishable. Across 50 held-out datasets, the model shows no predictive advantage over an empirical-frequency baseline (paired 95% CIs span zero). Ablations show the added update components provide no consistent benefit. These results caution against interpreting individual parameter estimates from this model class in short binary-feedback designs, and specify that mechanistic claims about clinical group differences in {sigma}, {omega}, or {lambda} require graded responses, manipulated volatility, multi-context sequences, and longitudinal replication.

papers.title: A robust mutation spectrum analysis framework for high-depth error-corrected sequencing data
papers.abstract: Comparing mutational spectra across experimental groups requires inference at the level of the biological replicate. Error-corrected sequencing (ECS) generates hundreds to thousands of mutations per replicate, yet classical pooled G2 tests treat individual mutations as independent observations and ignore replicate-level variability, inflating statistical significance (pseudo-replication). We present a replicate-aware Ridge-Penalized Dirichlet-Multinomial (RP-DMM) framework that models biological replicates directly and accounts for overdispersion. An L2 (ridge) penalty, with strength chosen by leave-one-out cross-validation, stabilizes spectrum estimates by shrinking weakly supported mutation categories toward a common baseline, and inference uses a parametric bootstrap. We also provide a complementary non-parametric rank-permutation test for sparse datasets. In simulations, the pooled G2 test became increasingly anti-conservative as mutation depth increased, with false-positive rates approaching 100% under the null hypothesis. RP-DMM maintained Type I error near the nominal 5% level and had substantially greater power than the rank-permutation test. Regularization was most consequential for high-dimensional spectra. False positive rates approached the nominal 5% level once the lower-mutation group contained approximately 300-500 mutations, depending on the number of biological replicates. A practical target of approximately 400 mutations in the lower-mutation group provided robust Type I error control across all scenarios examined; below this, the rank-permutation test performed robustly and is preferred. In Duplex Sequencing data from benzo[a]pyrene-exposed mice, RP-DMM distinguished exposure-associated mutational signatures from comparisons with higher mutation counts but null effect size, whereas the pooled G2 test declared all comparisons significant. The cross-validated penalty decreased as mutation depth increased, indicating that regularization strength should be tuned to the data. The framework is implemented in the MutSeqR R package.

papers.title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq
papers.abstract: Summary: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. VIGAT jointly examines accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes, integrating genomic annotations and biological context to select gene-specific regions enriched for cluster-discriminative signals. Selected regions are used to generate a gene-by-cell activity matrix. Across 196 paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets, VIGAT outperformed five existing methods in recovering marker-associated accessibility enriched in the corresponding cell populations, demonstrating the utility of VLM-guided visual reasoning for scalable gene activity quantification. Availability and implementation: VIGAT is implemented as an open-source R package and is freely available at https://github.com/beijie02/VIGAT.

papers.title: Multi-level mosaicism shapes the evolution of small eukaryotic DNA viruses
papers.abstract: Eukaryote-infecting small dsDNA viruses, including those referred to as virophages, polintons, and their relatives, are major constituents of ecosystems across the globe as both agents of mortality and as integrated elements that shape host genome evolution. As the ubiquity of these viruses has become apparent, there have been efforts to organize their diversity into major lineages in order to better understand their biogeography, ecological impact, and evolution. Virophages, polintons, and polinton-like viruses were recently placed in the sub-phylum Polisuviricotina, though efforts to resolve relationships within this sub-phylum have been complicated by the vast diversity of these viruses and the existence of horizontal gene transfer between their genomes. To address these complications, we have used a gene profile occurrence based method of phylogenetic tree construction to aid in comparative genomic analysis of Polisuviricotina. We find that mosaicism is common within Polisuviricotina, in particular, reassociation of replication modules and morphogenic modules occurs throughout major Polisuviricotina groups. In addition to mosaic exchanges of full replication modules, we also observe extensive domain swapping within some replicases, indicating that mosaic recombination occurs on both the genome and subgenic level in these viruses. Analysis of individual replication modules suggests that they may be capable of some level of autonomous mobility, partially decoupling their evolution from the morphogenic module. This model helps explain the high levels of mosaicism in these viruses and has implications for the mechanisms through which small dsDNA viruses evolve.

papers.title: Archival data storage using DNA proximity graphs
papers.abstract: DNA offers a promising medium for long-term archival data storage, but writing information into DNA remains costly. Here we introduce SPAN (Synthesis-free Proximity-graph Archiving in Nucleic acids), a synthesis-independent storage architecture in which information is written as a physical pattern and encoded in the spatial relationships of randomly barcoded DNA molecules. Barcodes are deposited onto an optically patterned surface, and an enzymatic reaction records neighboring barcode pairs. Sequencing these pairs produces a proximity graph from which the information is decoded. We demonstrate this principle by writing a 136-bit pattern using photolithography and recovering 98.5% of the bits. Our cost analysis estimates 10X lower writing costs than any existing DNA storage method. Using established commercial optical writing technologies, we project a further five-order-of-magnitude reduction to below flash memory costs. Although readout is more expensive, this trade-off is attractive for deep archival storage, where information is written once and rarely, if ever, retrieved.

papers.title: Gain-of-function mutations in the RodZ juxtamembrane domain promote Rod system activity in Escherichia coli
papers.abstract: The peptidoglycan (PG) cell wall protects bacteria from osmotic lysis and determines their shape. In rod-shaped bacteria, the lateral wall is elongated by the Rod system (elongasome). This synthetic machine is built around the RodA-PBP2 PG synthase complex, the actin-like protein MreB, and the accessory proteins MreC, MreD, and RodZ. Notably, RodZ shares a similar domain organization with FtsN, an essential division protein that triggers PG synthesis by the division apparatus (divisome). Both are single pass transmembrane proteins that bind actin-like proteins in the cytoplasm and have largely unstructured periplasmic regions capped by small, folded C-terminal domains. We therefore investigated whether RodZ might function like FtsN in activating the Rod system. To this end, gain-of-function variants of Escherichia coli RodZ were isolated that restored growth and shape to cells producing a hypomorphic mreC mutant. Production of these RodZ variants in wild-type cells increased resistance to the MreB antagonist A22 and enhanced sensitivity to the beta-lactam mecillinam. These phenotypes have all previously been associated with Rod system hyperactivation, and we found that they were caused by substitutions in the cytoplasmic juxtamembrane (JM) domain of RodZ. This domain is analogous to the N-terminus of FtsN known to promote divisome activation via its interaction with filaments of the actin-like FtsA protein. Structural modeling indicates that the JM domain of RodZ is similarly likely to associate with MreB filaments. Our results therefore support a model in which RodZ activates PG synthesis by the Rod system via a mechanism analogous to divisome activation by FtsN.

papers.title: Binding of a Macrocyclic Nonapeptide Inhibitor to Histone Deacetylase 6
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) plays an essential role in the regulation of post-translational lysine acetylation. Myriad biological processes depend on the precise regulation of lysine acetylation-deacetylation cycles, and their dysregulation is linked to human pathologies such as cancer and neurodegeneration. Broad-specificity HDAC inhibitors are efficacious in treating disease, but the inhibitors currently approved for clinical use often cause deleterious side effects due to inhibition of multiple HDAC isozymes as well as other zinc enzymes. Cyclic peptides comprise novel platforms that, in principle, can be tailored for affinity and selectivity. A key advantage of cyclic peptide design is the ability to incorporate both canonical and noncanonical amino acids. As part of our program focusing on cyclic peptide HDAC inhibitors, we now report the 1.9-[A] resolution crystal structure of HDAC6 CD2 complexed with macrocyclic nonapeptide 1. The structure reveals zinc coordination by a noncanonical thiolate-containing amino acid, plus direct and water-mediated enzyme-inhibitor hydrogen bonds that contribute to nanomolar inhibitory potency. Structural comparisons with previously reported HDAC6 CD2 complexes with tetrapeptide and octapeptide macrocycles reveal similar networks of direct and water-mediated interactions. Given the surge of interest in cyclic peptide inhibitors, fueled in part by advances in computational design approaches, the crystal structure of the HDAC6 CD2-1 complex sets an important foundation for further development of macrocyclic peptide inhibitors.

papers.title: A Plasmid-Derived Machinery Drives Chromosomal Replication Initiation in the Colorectal Cancer-Associated Bacterium Fusobacterium nucleatum and Its Close Relatives
papers.abstract: Chromosome replication initiation in bacterial genomes typically occurs at a single origin, called oriC, through the binding of the DnaA initiator protein to specific chromosomal repeats known as DnaA-boxes. Here, relying on comparative genomics, we show that the family Fusobacteriaceae, which belongs to the order Fusobacteriales alongside the family Leptotrichiaceae, deviates from this paradigm. Our analysis revealed a stark contrast between the two lineages: while dnaA flanks oriC in Leptotrichiaceae, it is notably missing from Fusobacteriaceae genomes. Adjacent to oriC in Fusobacteriaceae, we identified a gene encoding replication initiator protein A (RPA). We characterized RPA as a Rep-type initiator involved in plasmid replication that likely originated from an iteron-containing plasmid, iterons being the plasmid analogues of DnaA-boxes. Phylogenetic reconstruction indicates that the gene encoding RPA was acquired together with its associated iterons and subsequently domesticated by the Fusobacteriaceae ancestor, successfully displacing the ancestral chromosomal dnaA gene at the origin of replication. This shift to a plasmid-derived replication system may represent an adaptive trait of the Fusobacteriaceae, potentially offering new insights into the biology of Fusobacterium nucleatum, a member of this family known to be a major driver of colorectal cancer progression within the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Hierarchical TPR:ZC3HC1 interactions drive stepwise assembly of serially arrayed nuclear basket appendages extending into vertebrate cell nuclei
papers.abstract: The nuclear basket (NB) is a fibrillar scaffold anchored to the nuclear pore complex (NPC), with protein TPR constituting its structural backbone. Recently, ZC3HC1 was identified as an additional structural NB component interconnecting TPR subpopulations. However, it had remained unclear how ZC3HC1 and TPR engage each other and how the resulting ensembles are arranged relative to the NB. Here, we uncover a hierarchy of sequential interactions between distinct ZC3HC1 and TPR domains, resulting in serially arrayed TPR:ZC3HC1 ensembles appended to the NB. Projecting into the nucleus, these ensembles extend beyond the NB dimensions traditionally considered prototypic. We also find that the copy numbers of NPC/NB-associated TPR are far higher than commonly anticipated and sufficient to support this modular organizational principle. Together with sufficient ZC3HC1 copy numbers, our data define a model in which alternating recruitment of ZC3HC1 and TPR extends the NB's spatial and functional reach into the nuclear interior.

papers.title: Summed contrasts can conceal reversed regional preferences: directional and dose criteria for screening transcranial direct current stimulation montage pairs
papers.abstract: Background: The regional-matching design evaluated here requires two transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) montages, each stronger in its own target region, with adequate exposure. Summed contrasts can be positive when only one preference holds. Objective: To test whether a summed double-dissociation index (DDI), overlap and cohort-median dose rules identify such pairs, for a focused-attention versus open-monitoring experiment. Methods: Twenty-four montage pairs were simulated in 20 anatomical head models (SimNIBS 4.6, 2 mA). A four-rule screen (DDI, overlap, cohort-median dose) was recorded before cohort results; a post hoc conjunction required both regional contrasts positive in >=80% of heads. Two leading pairs were compared on per-head dose, a second solver and 60 conductivity stress-test draws. Results: Eighteen pairs passed the screen, but 13 failed the conjunction; one with positive median DDI (0.782) reversed the salience-region preference in all 20 heads. The nominated pair (F3-centered 4x1 ring; F8-Fp2 sponges; median DDI 1.561; both preferences in 20/20 heads) brought both anatomical targets to the 0.20 V/m operational floor in 11/20 heads; a conventional sponge pair (DDI 0.627) did so in 20/20, though both passed the cohort-median dose rule. The nominated pair's separation held across a second solver and all 60 stress-test draws, but both network targets reached the floor in 19/60. Conclusions: Summed indices and cohort-median dose rules can pass pairs that fail reciprocal-exposure criteria. Such screens should pre-specify the directional conjunction and report per-head joint dose coverage. These are modeled exposures, not physiological or behavioral effects.

papers.title: DAPHNE: A global database of pest herbivores and their natural enemies
papers.abstract: Anticipating and managing the impact of herbivorous pests requires evidence-based knowledge about the interactions between pests and their natural enemies. Knowledge of species' ecologies and biological interactions are typically disseminated in unstructured text across hundreds of thousands of scientific articles spanning a rapidly growing scientific literature, but manually screening this literature is time-consuming and impractical at scale. Taxonomic and geographic coverage thus remains sparse, and structured data on interactions between individual species are lacking, particularly for invertebrates. Large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as a novel and powerful text-mining tool for knowledge extraction and evidence synthesis in a wide range of scientific disciplines, including ecology and conservation. In this study, we use an open-weight, pre-trained LLM to analyse abstracts of a corpus of published material on biological pest control to obtain a global Database of Pest Herbivores and their Natural Enemies (DAPHNE). This method resulted in the extraction of 175,404 species interactions from 112,830 published pest control studies, containing16,755 unique animal taxa resolved at the species level. Interactions include herbivory (granivory, frugivory and gall-formation), predation, parasitism and hyperparasitism, and comprise a range of additional information, such as species' taxonomy, pest status, pest importance, natural enemy importance, provision of biocontrol, associated plants and industries, invasiveness and the vectoring of pathogens and diseases. Validation of the results shows that most data columns were extracted with high recall and precision (>90%) and comparison of DAPHNE with other sources shows a high degree of agreement, but also highlights that the dataset contains information that may have been missed by other sources. In addition to the identification of important crop pests and their natural enemies, DAPHNE may be used for a variety of use-cases, including the identification of invasive species and pathogen vectors, trophic network analysis and literature search and discovery.

papers.title: Intensive pine plantation management shapes infectious agent communities in the generalist rodent Apodemus sylvaticus, with consequences for zoonotic hazard
papers.abstract: Land use change is widely recognized as a major driver of emerging zoonotic diseases. Yet, while forest plantations are expanding worldwide, their consequences on the circulation of infectious agents in wildlife remain poorly understood. We investigated how native pine plantations and broadleaved habitats shape rodent-associated infectious hazard in the generalist wood mouse (Apodemus sylvaticus), in southwestern France. Using a multi-season survey, we screened 424 wood mice for a broad range of infectious taxa and compared infection probability and infected-host abundance among pine plantation edges, broadleaved hedgerows embedded within pine plantations and broadleaved forests. Using a combination of linear mixed model and joint species distribution modelling, we tested whether infectious hazard differed between pine plantations and broadleaved forests, whether broadleaved hedgerows shifted these patterns towards those observed in broadleaved forests, and how these habitat-related patterns varied across seasons. We detected 22 potentially infectious taxa, including nine recognized zoonotic bacteria. Season strongly influenced infectious patterns, while habitat effects were taxa and season dependent. In spring, pine plantation edges increased infection probability for Bartonella grahamii and Neoerhlichia mikurensis compared to broadleaved forest, but their strong negative effect on wood mouse abundance resulted in consistently lower infected-host abundance for most infectious taxa. Broadleaved hedgerows showed distinct and season-dependent patterns with infectious profiles resembling those of pine edges in spring, but with higher infectious hazard than both other habitats for several taxa in autumn. Our results highlight that habitat effects on infectious hazard cannot be inferred from infection probability alone. Pine plantations may reduce rodent-associated zoonotic hazard through their strong negative effect on host abundance, despite increasing infection probability for some agents. Forest diversification and restoration initiatives, such as broadleaved hedgerows here, may have unforeseen epidemiological consequences, underscoring the need to integrate disease ecology into forest management and restoration to anticipate variation in zoonotic risks, while maximizing ecological benefits.

papers.title: Suspension culture drives metabolic rewiring in human pluripotent stem cells
papers.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) are increasingly expanded in 3D suspension culture to support scalable cell culturing, yet how the transition from 2D to 3D cultures affects hPSCs remains poorly understood. Here, we compare hPSCs in 2D and 3D cultures using transcriptomics, proteomics, spent-medium analysis, and stable-isotope tracing. hPSCs maintained pluripotency in both formats, although suspension culture showed altered growth dynamics and increased initial cell loss. Multi-omics analysis identified culture format as the dominant driver of molecular variation and revealed changes in adhesion, cytoskeletal organization, glycolysis, and oxidative phosphorylation. Spent-medium analysis showed increased lactate/glucose ratio in 3D suspension. Stable-isotope tracing revealed increased glucose-derived labelling of pyruvate and altered partitioning of glucose-derived carbon within the TCA cycle in 3D suspension cultures. Together with increased abundance of glycolytic enzymes, these findings support increased glycolysis in 3D suspension. Glutamine contribution to the TCA cycle was reduced, whereas relative reductive carboxylation was increased in 3D suspension cultures. Together, these findings show that transition from 2D to 3D suspension culture induces metabolic rewiring in hPSCs.

papers.title: Genome-wide characterization of host factors involved in single-stranded RNA and DNA phage infection pathways
papers.abstract: Single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) and single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) bacteriophages form a key component of the global virome, yet the host genetic networks supporting their infection cycles remain poorly understood. Here we present a genome-wide map of the host factors involved in infection by F pilus-dependent ssRNA and ssDNA phages in Escherichia coli. Screens across ssRNA phages spanning all four genogroups of the Leviviricetes reveal a conserved network of host dependencies, with the notable exception of the F plasmid gene traD. Primary structural receptor components and DsbA-mediated disulfide bond formation are universally required to ensure F pilus integrity, whereas traD shows a strict genogroup-specific requirement during entry despite all lineages sharing the same receptor. Gene dosage screens identify elevated copy number of the genomic fragments encoding the HslU protease or the RNA chaperone StpA as barriers that restrict infection. Parallel assays with filamentous ssDNA phages confirm reliance on the host TolQRA complex for entry downstream of pilus engagement and track negative fitness signatures across envelope homeostasis clusters, reflecting the physiological burden of non-lytic virion extrusion. Comparative genomics and high-throughput genetics trace the selectivity of the isolation host, E. coli HSF, to a horizontally acquired Klebsiella capsule that excludes a large panel of double-stranded DNA phages isolated on other E. coli strains while allowing ssRNA and ssDNA virions to engage the extended F pilus and bypass the barrier through native pilus retraction. The work delivers a systematic, class-wide map of single-stranded phage-host interactions, a host platform for accessing uncultured viral diversity, and a functional blueprint for diagnostics, protein antibiotics and biocontrol tools that halt horizontal gene transfer.

papers.title: Region-dependent regulation of Tau phosphorylation by Glycerophosphodiester Phosphodiesterase 2 in a mouse model of tauopathy
papers.abstract: Hyperphosphorylation of Tau promotes its aggregation and neurofibrillary tangle (NFT) formation, contributing to neuronal dysfunction and neurodegeneration in diseases such as Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRDs). However, the mechanisms underlying dysregulated Tau phosphorylation under pathological contexts remain unclear. Glycerophosphodiester phosphodiesterase 2 (GDE2) is a six-transmembrane enzyme that acts at the cell surface to cleave the glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchor that tethers a subclass of proteins to the membrane. Here, we show that in the PS19 tauopathy mouse model, GDE2 disruption modulates Tau phosphorylation by transiently decreasing Tau's propensity for aggregation through region-specific regulation of local kinase environments. In the cortex, GDE2 ablation in 6-month-old PS19 male mice (PS19;Gde2KO) reduces Tau phosphorylation at Serine (S)202/Threonine (T)205, T212, and S396 but increases S262 phosphorylation in the hippocampus of 6-month-old PS19;Gde2KO male and female mice. Consistent with these changes, in males, Glycogen Synthase Kinase-3 / {beta} (GSK3 / {beta}) activity is decreased in the cortex, while AKT activity is increased in both males and females in the hippocampus, with no changes in protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) and protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) activity. Primary cortical neurons from PS19;Gde2KO animals showed reduced Tau phosphorylation at S202/T205, implying cell-autonomous roles for neuronal GDE2 in this process. GDE2 overexpression in heterologous SH-SY5Y cells increased Tau phosphorylation at S202/T205, while a catalytically inactive form of GDE2 did not, suggesting that GDE2 regulation of target GPI-anchored protein surface activity is required to modulate Tau phosphorylation. Taken together, our study identifies GDE2 as a component of the complex regulatory network that controls Tau phosphorylation in the context of tauopathy and provides insight into putative pathways relevant to Tau pathologies observed in disease.

papers.title: Mechanical coupling narrows an epithelial colony before it reaches a bottleneck
papers.abstract: A colony migrating into a passage narrower than itself but wider than individuals must adapt its density distribution to pass. Powders, colloids and crowds driven through such an opening jam, since contact interactions provide no pathway for constituents to respond to the constriction before reaching it. Exploring whether a cohesive living tissue can reorganize in advance, we image MDCK epithelial monolayers migrating through microchannels in which a wide channel narrows, and locate response at the taper mouth, a transition zone in which we identify upstream responses. At locations where the local channel width is still unchanged, the monolayer detaches from the side walls and reduces its lateral extent. Particle image velocimetry shows that this is not passive compression; the axial velocity alternates aperiodically in sign, velocity divergence is positive in the transition zone, and tracking the positions of cell nuclei confirms that cells leave the crowded inlet region in both directions. Fluorescence imaging shows a belt of co-enriched E-cadherin, F-actin, and myosin-II at the edges that detach before the inlet, which laser ablation shows to be under elevated tension but dissolves once the tissue passes into the narrow inlet; {beta}-catenin is not co-enriched, indicating that junctions differ in composition in the core and at the edge of colony. This advance proceeds over hours, far more slowly than the viscoelastic reorganization reported for MDCK monolayers, and switches in sign repeatedly, which a linear viscoelastic sheet under sustained constraint cannot do. E-cadherin knockdown abolishes narrowing, flow reversal, density redistribution, and belt assembly.

papers.title: Environment-Aware DNA Language Model for Stress-Responsive Genomic Prioritization in Maize
papers.abstract: Abiotic stresses such as heat and drought severely reduce the productivity of major crops including maize, with adverse implications for agricultural sustainability. Despite progress in characterizing stress resilience, identifying genomic regions associated with stress response remains challenging due to complex genotype-by-environment interactions. Genomic Foundation Models (GFMs), inspired by advances in Large Language Models (LLMs), leverage large-scale self-supervised pre-training on DNA sequences to capture regulatory patterns; however, their adaptation to plant stress-response analysis remains underexplored. In this work, we propose an environment-aware DNA-LLM framework that incorporates stress-specific prompt tokens into AgroNT, a transformer-based plant GFM, using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). The model learns stress-conditioned genomic representations that exhibit distinct structures across environmental contexts. We further formulate a prioritization method that uses stress-induced shifts in these representations relative to the control condition together with stress-token-associated transformer attention patterns to identify putative stress-responsive genomic regions. The framework was evaluated on the Genomes-to-Fields (G2F) dataset, comprising over 4,000 maize hybrids grown across 38 locations over 8 years, using grain yield under heat, drought, and combined heat-drought stress. Flowering traits were used to assess generalizability of the stress-conditioned representations across phenotypes. The prioritized regions were assessed using spatiotemporal differential gene-expression profiles, stress-associated quantitative trait loci, and transcription-factor characterization. Regulatory motif analysis further revealed stress-associated motifs enriched within the prioritized sequences as well as model-emphasized high-attention regions. Functional annotation of genes proximal to prioritized regions highlighted roles in transcriptional regulation, signaling, and metabolic pathways relevant to abiotic stress adaptation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of stress-conditioned transformer-based sequence modeling for environment-aware genome-to-phenome analysis in crop improvement.

papers.title: Maternal diet and genetics shape the human milk metabolome
papers.abstract: Human milk contains a diverse array of metabolites that contribute to infant nutrition, immune development, and microbial colonization. The maternal factors shaping the milk metabolome, and the relative contribution of genetics or diet vs. other factors, remain poorly understood. Here, we profiled 458 milk metabolites in 349 one-month postpartum human milk samples and integrated metabolomic data with maternal diet, clinical, transcriptomic, and genomic measurements. Maternal diet was broadly associated with milk metabolite composition, with significant correlations identified between dietary features and 323 metabolites. Coffee consumption strongly predicted milk quinic acid and 1,3-dimethyluric acid abundance, while high-fiber dietary patterns were associated with metabolites including proline-betaine and N-acetylornithine. Integration of milk transcriptomic and metabolomic data via machine learning identified biologically plausible gene-metabolite pairs, including associations between QPRT expression and quinolinic acid, and DPEP1 and cysteine-glycine dipeptide. Genome-wide association analyses identified nine study-wide significant metabolite quantitative trait loci, including novel milk-specific associations near PDE6A affecting purine metabolites and near GNE affecting free sialic acid. Comparison with plasma metabolite studies demonstrated both shared and milk-specific genetic regulation of metabolites. Finally, we found that of all tested maternal features, diet explained the largest proportion of variation in the milk metabolome. Together, these findings demonstrate that the human milk metabolome reflects both maternal exposures and mammary gland-specific biology. This work establishes a framework for understanding how genetic and environmental factors shape milk composition.

papers.title: AdaGeneBudget: Cell-Adaptive Gene-Token Allocation for Efficient Single-Cell Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models (scFMs) represent each cell using sequences of gene-associated tokens, making embedding extraction increasingly costly as the number of cells and expressed genes grows. Existing input policies typically rely on fixed input budgets, with retained genes determined by random subsampling, model-native ranking, or a dataset-level highly variable gene (HVG) panel. However, they do not jointly determine, for each cell, which genes to retain and how many tokens to allocate. We introduce AdaGeneBudget, a training-free gene-token selection method that combines each gene's expression with reference-derived inverse detection frequency and retains the shortest ranked prefix that captures a target fraction of the cell's expression-specificity score mass. The resulting cell-specific budget is bounded by minimum and maximum lengths, requires no cell-type labels, and leaves the pretrained backbone unchanged. We evaluated AdaGeneBudget in a frozen-backbone inference setting using pretrained scGPT and Geneformer models on Kang and PBMC reference-mapping tasks, with an additional scPRINT comparison against its official HVG policy and an expressed-only HVG control. Across four scGPT and Geneformer backbone-dataset pairs, AdaGeneBudget substantially reduced mean gene-token counts and peak GPU memory while increasing embedding-extraction throughput by up to 4.63x. Despite this compression, it preserved native-level aggregate annotation utility and numerically outperformed token-matched random and Top-Expression baselines. AdaGeneBudget also preserved fine-grained and low-support cell identities and retained lineage-marker programs and stimulation-associated pathway genes under compression. In scPRINT, both HVG controls achieved higher annotation macro-F1, whereas AdaGeneBudget more faithfully preserved the stimulation-induced embedding direction. These results establish biologically informed, cell-adaptive gene-token allocation as a practical complement to architectural and systems-level efficiency methods for applying existing scFMs to new datasets. They also suggest that cell-adaptive input allocation may be a useful design principle for future models operating under finite token budgets.

papers.title: Characterization of the frameshift c.515dupC knock-in mouse model of HSPB8-associated myopathy (MFM13) and evaluation of Trehalose as autophagy modulating therapy.
papers.abstract: Heat shock protein family B member 8 (HSPB8) is a chaperone involved in the chaperone-assisted selective autophagy (CASA) complex. HSPB8 in conjunction with cochaperone Bcl2-associated athanogene 3 (BAG3), promotes autophagy-mediated removal of misfolded proteins associated with various neurodegenerative diseases. Mutations in HSPB8, previously associated with Charcot Marie Tooth disease type 2L, have recently been linked to an autosomal dominant rimmed vacuolar myopathy (MFM13), and is considered a multisystem proteinopathy. Patients have distal and proximal limb girdle myopathy with muscle biopsy showing fatty replacement, endomysial fibrosis, and rimmed vacuoles leading to muscle atrophy and early demise. We have demonstrated reduced expression of HSPB8, altered autophagy, and TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) accumulation in patient fibroblasts. Overexpressed murine Hspb8 frameshift mutant (c.515dupC, fs) displays insolubility and aggregation propensity in Murine Neuroblastoma X Spinal Cord 34 (NSC-34) cells. Using clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) technology, we generated a knock-in Hspb8 mouse model of the c.515dupC hot spot frameshift variant to study disease pathology. Mutant Hspb8 mice developed late onset muscle weakness beginning at 15 months. Muscle biochemical analyses revealed reduced HSPB8 levels, increased TDP 43, and altered autophagy markers, partially recapitulating the human phenotype. Fiber type analysis, neuromuscular junction integrity, and motor neurons show mild myopathy without neurodegeneration. Given the lack of available treatments, we evaluated trehalose, a natural disaccharide that is known to induce HSPB8 and enhance autophagy as a potential therapy. Administration of 2% trehalose in the drinking water restored HSPB8 expression; however, it did not significantly ameliorate autophagic dysfunction or TDP-43 pathology in mutant mice. These findings support the value of our preclinical models for translational studies, and autophagy enhancement as a potential therapeutic strategy for HSPB8-related myopathy.

papers.title: Reversible chromatin remodeling enables Prosopis cineraria survival under recurrent heat extremes.
papers.abstract: Climate warming is intensifying seasonal heat and drought, raising urgent questions about how long-lived desert plants sustain physiological function across recurrent extremes. In Prosopis cineraria, a native Arabian desert legume tree, we used seasonal Hi-C, transcriptomic, histone-mark, and DNA-methylation profiling at six time points to uncover the underlying mechanisms. We found that during peak heat, chromatin boundaries are selectively weakened and candidate topological domains merge, activating clusters of heat-protective genes enriched for H3K4me3 and H3K27ac. In the cool season, immune and developmental gene regulation is coupled with flowering, consistent with a bet-hedging strategy that shifts reproduction away from lethal heat. At the same time, promoter CHH methylation near transposable elements and reduced H3K4me3/H3K27ac hint at a proactive developmental phase rather than just surviving the stress. Integrating physiological data, we connect chromatin activation to an SA-ABA reciprocal seasonal profile, MIZ1-associated hydrotropism, and Stay-Green-mediated delayed senescence through chlorophyll retention. With Landscape genomics and phylogenetics, we further identified a housekeeping PEPC with a high predicted melting temperature that could sustain a malate-derived carbon supply, buffering metabolism under heat. Together, these findings reveal that reversible epigenetic gating enables desert trees to survive and recover from extreme seasonal stress.

papers.title: Turning an object into a scene: buildings activate scene-selective visual cortex independently of visual features
papers.abstract: Human visual cortex contains regions that selectively respond to both scenes and large objects, particularly buildings. The cortical overlap between buildings and scenes has been attributed to shared visual features (e.g., cardinal orientations, rectilinearity). Alternative accounts propose that buildings may also activate scene representations indirectly, independently of specific visual features, for example because buildings evoke a sense of space. Here, we tested for such feature-independent activation by comparing EEG and fMRI responses in human participants (both sexes) to buildings and visually-matched boxes, and relating these responses to scene-selective responses. Buildings and boxes were matched using image-based metrics, deep neural networks, and a perceptual similarity task. Time-resolved EEG decoding showed that buildings and boxes evoked discriminable responses from 360ms post-stimulus onset, incompatible with feedforward visual feature processing. Importantly, the building-box classifier generalized to discriminate scenes from chairs, providing the first EEG evidence for a representational overlap between buildings and scenes. Temporal generalization analyses further showed that the late building-selective response corresponded to an earlier scene-selective response, with a temporal offset of ~130ms. Finally, ultra-fast fMRI (TR=140ms) revealed that the scene-selective parahippocampal place area (PPA) similarly showed a feature-independent building-selective response that was delayed and prolonged relative to the scene-selective response. These results clarify the nature of building selectivity in visual cortex by showing that this selectivity is feature-independent and delayed relative to scene selectivity. We propose that intrinsic associations between object categories (e.g., buildings and scenes, tools and hands) may account for part of the categorical organization of ventral temporal cortex.

papers.title: Gonadal histology and variation in gonadosomatic index in captive moonfish Mene maculata
papers.abstract: The moonfish Mene maculata (Bloch and Schneider, 1801), the sole extant species of the family Menidae, is widely distributed in the Indo-West Pacific. Although its spawning season has previously been inferred from seasonal variation in the gonadosomatic index (GSI), the histological basis for interpreting GSI as an indicator of spawning-capable status remains limited. Here we describe the gonadal structure of male and female M. maculata and evaluate how GSI and standard length relate to spawning-capable status based on germ cell development. The testis was lobular and exhibited an unrestricted spermatogonial distribution, a structure widely observed among neoteleosts, indicating that the phylogenetic distinctiveness of M. maculata was not associated with a distinctive testicular structure. In the spawning-capable female, oocytes at multiple developmental stages, from primary growth to oocyte maturation, co-occurred within the ovary, indicating asynchronous ovarian development. This finding suggests that M. maculata may be a batch spawner rather than a total spawner as previously inferred. The spawning-capable female had a GSI consistent with previously inferred spawning season estimates. By contrast, histologically examined males were spawning capable at GSI values lower than those previously associated with the inferred spawning season, suggesting that male spawning-capable status may persist beyond the period inferred from elevated GSI alone. This study provides preliminary histological information on gonadal development in captive M. maculata and context for interpreting previously published field measurements of GSI.

papers.title: Surprisal contributes little beyond contextual embeddings in high-gamma ECoG encoding
papers.abstract: Surprisal and contextual embeddings are both derived from large language models and are widely used to predict neural responses during language comprehension, but it is unclear whether surprisal adds information beyond embeddings. We test this directly: does word surprisal improve out-of-sample prediction of high-gamma ECoG responses after GPT-2 XL contextual embeddings are included? Using public ECoG recordings from natural speech, we fit word-aligned ridge encoding models with baseline stimulus features, GPT-2 XL embeddings, and GPT-2 XL surprisal. Adding one surprisal predictor left held-out correlation essentially unchanged at the primary response window, and the increment stayed within an equivalence margin across alternative lags, residualized surprisal, and frequency-band targets; it did not uniformly meet the same criterion under banded ridge regularization or within labeled temporal subsets. This small increment suggests that surprisal does not act as an independent predictor. It is better understood as a compressed readout of the same broader predictive state that the embeddings already capture.

papers.title: Learning complex temporal dependencies via local synaptic plasticity
papers.abstract: The ability to extract and exploit temporal structure across diverse tasks is central to human cognition. Neuroscientists have typically relied on recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT) when modelling neural and behavioural processes such as decision-making and motor control. However, this algorithm has limited biological plausibility, hence the computational principles underlying efficient learning of temporal dependencies remain unresolved. Here, we investigate temporal predictive coding (tPC), a recently proposed framework that extends predictive coding to the temporal domain while preserving local Hebbian update rules. We analyse and extend tPC to establish its relationship with several influential computational models of learning in RNNs, including BPTT, reservoir computing, and eligibility propagation (e-prop). We first demonstrate structurally equivalent weight update rules between tPC and tBPTT1, a variant of BPTT in which gradients are propagated only one time step into the past. We then show that tPC can leverage reservoir dynamics to encode short-range temporal context, and simultaneously sculpt neural trajectories in state space to support downstream readout. We further demonstrate that hierarchical recurrent dynamics can facilitate learning of more complex temporal dependencies, while additionally conferring robustness to strong distractors. Finally, we show that tPC networks can be augmented with biologically inspired eligibility traces to solve temporally extended context-dependent tasks. Together, these results reveal that relatively simple recurrent networks governed by local plasticity can support temporal learning in more complex settings than previously appreciated.

papers.title: AAV delivered lysosome-targeting chimeras mediate sustained antibody depletion in vivo
papers.abstract: Immunoglobulin G (IgG) is a critical effector of the adaptive immune system, but IgG autoantibodies against self-antigens drive pathology across a wide range of autoimmune diseases. Lowering circulating IgG is a validated and promising therapeutic avenue. Here we developed genetically-encoded lysosome targeting chimeras (GELYTACs) that target circulating IgGs for clearance and degradation. The GELYTACs comprised two protein modules derived from insulin-like growth factor 2 (IGF2) and an IgG-binding nanobody, respectively, and mediated clearance of plasma IgG via the lysosomal trafficking receptor IGF2R. To achieve long-lasting IgG depletion, we encoded GELYTACs in an AAV gene therapy vector and established continuous expression in mice. We also developed conditional GELYACs that are activatable with disease-specific proteases or small molecule drugs and show that GELYTACs can be secreted from cellular therapies. This work establishes GELYTACs as a possible therapeutic modality that is deliverable using genetic medicine approaches.

papers.title: Biomarkers indicate altered outer retinal fluid homeostasis in the absence of Kv2.1/Kv8.2 channels.
papers.abstract: Purpose: Photoreceptor Kv2.1/Kv8.2 voltage-gated potassium channels carry an outward potassium current, helping to set the resting membrane potential and to shape dim light responses. Because potassium flux in the outer retina influences extracellular osmolarity and fluid distribution, we hypothesized that Kv2.1/Kv8.2 channels also contribute to fluid homeostasis in this region of the retina. Methods: OCT imaging was performed in Kv8.2 heterozygous (Het) and knockout (KO) mice aged ~5 weeks under dark- and light-adapted conditions. Light-dark differences in the distance between the external limiting membrane (ELM) and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) ({Delta}ELM-RPE) were calculated to quantify light-evoked outer retinal expansion, a biomarker associated with changes in subretinal space (SRS) fluid handling. As a secondary outcome, outer nuclear layer (ONL) thickness was also measured under both lighting conditions. Retinal gene expression was assessed by RNA-seq and droplet digital RT-PCR. Retinal protein expression was determined by western blotting and immunolabeling. Results: {Delta}ELM-RPE was significantly reduced in Kv8.2 KO mice compared with Het controls, indicating altered light-evoked outer retinal dynamics compatible with changes in subretinal space fluid handling. ONL thickness exhibited a small but significant light-dark change that was different between genotypes. Transcriptomic analyses revealed upregulation of osmosensitive genes, including osmolyte transporters and aquaporins. AQP1 protein expression in photoreceptors increased. Conclusions: These findings are consistent with altered outer retinal fluid homeostasis following loss of Kv8.2 and support a model in which photoreceptor potassium efflux contributes to osmotic water movement into the subretinal space.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolite analyses link DMSP cleavage to acetate overflow in the coral symbiont Endozoicomonas ruthgatesiae
papers.abstract: Endozoicomonas, a dominant bacterial symbiont of corals, degrades dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP) and produces dimethylsulfide (DMS), a key compound in the global sulfur cycle. By contrast, the carbon backbone of DMSP has received far less attention. Using Endozoicomonas ruthgatesiae strain 8E as a model, we exposed cultures to DMSP at 25 and 31, simulating an ambient condition and thermal stress, respectively. Using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) to monitor DMS and acetate production, we observed a significant increase in acetate efflux from 8E during DMSP metabolism in a growth phase-dependent manner. This increase in acetate was not observed when the native compound was replaced with 13C-labeled DMSP, suggesting that the additional acetate originated from DMSP. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that DMSP exposure upregulated dddD expression and triggered a reconfiguration of 8E's central carbon metabolism, with upregulation of genes associated with the glyoxylate shunt-associated genes, and down-regulation of the TCA cycle and the Pta-AckA pathway. These findings suggest that DMSP-derived acetate overflows when its assimilation into biomass is restricted. Notably, elevated temperature diminished DMSP cleavage activity of 8E, indicating thermal sensitivity of this bacterial metabolic activity. Together, our results indicate that exposure to DMSP redirects carbon flow in Endozoicomonas, resulting in overflow of DMSP-derived acetate.

papers.title: Disambiguation of two-tone images aligns object representations in the EEG
papers.abstract: Electrophysiological responses to visual objects carry information about stimulus identity and semantic category, but it remains difficult to know whether such information represents conceptual knowledge or merely regularities in physical image features. Here, we presented two-tone images before and after disambiguation via corresponding photographs to seventeen healthy participants while recording EEG to dissociate the learned image concept from its physical properties. After disambiguation, EEG responses to learned two-tone images became more similar to the responses of their photo counterparts. This effect emerged approximately 100 ms after stimulus onset and peaked at 350 ms. However, we found no evidence for a generalization of the response pattern to the stimulus semantic category. Furthermore, alignment to the photo counterparts was only detectable after explicit visual disambiguation rather than spontaneous recognition. Together, these findings indicate that EEG can capture specific learned conceptual modulations of responses to visually degraded stimuli, while also showing that low-level visual properties dominate the representational structure.

papers.title: Iconic Sound-Shape Correspondences in Aphasia
papers.abstract: Purpose: To examine speech iconicity for shape in aphasia, we compared shape iconicity ratings from people with aphasia to those from neurologically intact individuals and evaluated how these ratings relate to phonological and semantic processing profiles in aphasia. Method: Twelve people with aphasia and twelve age- and gender-matched neurologically intact participants rated how rounded or pointed 50 auditory pseudowords sounded, using a 5 point scale. Ratings from participants with aphasia were compared to predicted shape iconicity ratings derived from reference ratings from prior work and to ratings from neurologically intact participants. For participants with aphasia, correlations between individual ratings and predicted ratings were related to measures of phonological and semantic processing. Results: Ratings from people with aphasia were significantly correlated with both the predicted ratings and the ratings from neurologically intact participants. Relative to ratings from neurologically intact people, ratings from people with aphasia had weaker correlations to predicted ratings. There were indications that greater language impairment was associated with greater disruption of iconicity ratings; in particular, deficits in phonological segmentation and semantic processing were associated with reduced sensitivity to shape iconicity. Conclusion: These findings suggest that sensitivity to shape iconicity is preserved to varying degrees in individuals with aphasia. Disruption of phonological and semantic processing appears to affect shape iconicity processing in aphasia.

papers.title: PhoPQ is an upstream regulator of quorum sensing in small colony variant subpopulations of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
papers.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic human pathogen that is hospital-endemic, forming biofilms on medical equipment and causing thousands of hospital-acquired infections each year. The success of P. aeruginosa as an opportunistic pathogen is linked to its phenotypic and genotypic adaptability. Relatedly, P. aeruginosa forms a small colony subpopulation in response to stresses like oxygen limitation and antibiotic exposure. Additionally, P. aeruginosa coordinates population-level decisions using a mechanism of cell-cell communication called quorum sensing. P. aeruginosa is notorious for these signaling pathways to control virulence factor production and biofilm formation in the host. We show that certain quorum-sensing mutations promote phenotypic switching; specifically, deletion of lasR and autoinducer modulating mutations in rhlI enhanced small colony formation in a time course-dependent manner. Using transcriptome analyses of isogenic small and large colony variants, we show that small colony formation is driven in part by the PhoPQ two-component signal transduction system in quorum-sensing mutant backgrounds. Specifically, our data show that unphosphorylated PhoP represses rhlR gene expression, and that subsequent de-repression of quorum sensing contributes to the production of virulence factors and the small colony phenotype. In total, these findings provide insight on how mutations evolved by clinical strains might serve as a bet-hedging strategy to promote the formation of a small colony phenotype and alter quorum-sensing signaling within a subpopulation of a given community.

papers.title: Reduced enteric Bdnf expression and TrkB-dependent regulation of Vip in a Mecp2-null mouse model of Rett syndrome-associated gastrointestinal dysmotility
papers.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) dysmotility is a highly prevalent and clinically significant feature of Rett syndrome (RTT), yet its underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated these mechanisms of GI dysmotility in a Mecp2null mouse model of RTT. First, we observed that MeCP2 was expressed in murine myenteric ganglia, including in enteric neurons and that Mecp2null males developed maturation associated functional regression in their GI motility. In dysmotile mice, longitudinal muscle myenteric plexus tissue showed marked reductions in enteric Bdnf isoforms IV, VI, and II, whereas expression of the BDNF receptor isoforms TrkB.FL and TrkB.T1 was not significantly altered, consistent with reduced enteric BDNF TrkB signaling. Despite impaired GI motility, Mecp2null mice showed no significant changes in total enteric neuronal density, nitrergic neuronal abundance, or expression of Nos1, Chat, and Uchl1. In contrast, Vip expression was significantly reduced, while expression of VIP receptor genes: Vipr1 and Vipr2 was increased, indicating disrupted VIPergic signaling. Integration with publicly available enteric single-cell/nucleus datasets and targeted qRTPCR further suggested altered inhibitory neuronal subtype composition, with reduced Vip+ Cartpt+ signatures and increased Nfia expression, suggesting that MeCP2 loss differentially affects distinct inhibitory neuronal subpopulations. Finally, conditional loss of TrkB.FL in neural crest-derived cells reduced Vip expression without recapitulating the full Mecp2null VIPergic phenotype, indicating that impaired BDNF TrkB signaling contributes to, but does not completely explain, the GI dysmotility in this model of RTT. Together, these findings identify enteric BDNF TrkB and VIPergic dysfunction as key mechanisms underlying GI dysmotility in RTT.

papers.title: AI-Guided Structure-Aware Modeling and Thermal Proteomics Reveal Direct Demethylzeylasteral-ACLY Interaction
papers.abstract: Identifying the direct molecular targets of bioactive natural products remains a central challenge in chemical biology. Here we present an integrated experimental-computational framework, that combines matrix-augmented thermal proteomics with HoloGNN, a holistic graph neural network, to systematically prioritize and validate protein-ligand interactions. Benchmarking with PDBbind datasets HoloGNN achieves state-of-the-art performance. Applying this framework to 50 structurally diverse natural products identified Demethylzeylasteral as a direct interactor of ACLY. Orthogonal biochemical assays confirmed micromolar binding and enzymatic inhibition. In an imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like mouse model, Demethylzeylasteral reduced disease severity and inflammatory cytokine expression. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that Demethylzeylasteral reverses keratinocyte hyperproliferation and suppresses ACLY-dependent lipid metabolic reprogramming. Together, this scalable, closed-loop strategy integrates thermal proteomics and machine learning to uncover direct targets of natural products and provides mechanistic evidence linking ACLY inhibition to therapeutic modulation of inflammatory pathology.

papers.title: Integrated metabolomics and proteomics from voxelated cortical hemispheres of adult rhesus monkeys
papers.abstract: The spatial organization of molecular networks across cortex likely contributes to differences in local circuit vulnerability in aging and Alzheimer's disease; yet many existing molecular datasets sacrifice spatial structure, sampling only a handful of regions per brain. Here, we present a framework for generating spatially registered, paired metabolomic and proteomic maps across an entire cortical hemisphere of an adult rhesus monkey, at millimeter resolution. One hemisphere each from two animals was harvested under controlled conditions, approximately flattened, and hand dissected at different sampling resolutions (roughly 2.5 and 4 mm/side) into tissue voxels. Each voxel was split after homogenization and extraction to provide matched aliquots for targeted metabolomics and deep untargeted proteomics. To handle these high dimensional data, we developed PChclust, a principal component guided feature clustering algorithm. For cross omic integration, we developed a spatially regularized sparse canonical correlation analysis (sr-sCCA), which incorporates spatial neighborhood structure via graph Laplacian smoothing. We recover meaningful biology: Molecular similarity between neighboring voxels decayed with distance in both modalities, confirming that voxelation captures spatially organized biological variance. The sr-sCCA identified joint proteome-metabolome components with coherent cortical gradients that were conserved across animals. Pathway enrichment analysis recovered brain relevant ontologies and reconstructed complete metabolic circuits from single voxels.

papers.title: Human and mouse cerebellar inhibitory circuits in dystonic crisis and their modulation with therapeutic stimulation
papers.abstract: Dystonia is a neurological movement disorder characterized by abnormal muscle contractions that, at their most severe, lead to a life-threatening condition - dystonic crisis. Yet, therapeutic options remain limited by our incomplete understanding of what neural circuits underly the condition. Although cerebellar nuclei neurons are implicated in the origin of baseline dystonic symptoms, it is unclear whether their activity drives dystonic crisis. To explore this role, we found that cerebellar abnormalities and neural inhibition were recurring targets in patients with dystonic crisis, implicating cerebellar inhibitory neurons in its development. We devised a mouse genetics approach to test whether inhibitory cerebellar nuclei neurons (iCNNs) induce dystonic crisis. Directional optogenetic modulation of iCNNs induced dystonic crises on-demand and alleviated spontaneous crises in mice that mimic spontaneous dystonic crises. To investigate whether iCNNs interact with other motor areas during dystonic crisis, we identified monosynaptic iCNN projections to the centrolateral nucleus of the thalamus (CL). Deep brain stimulation of the CL alleviated dystonic crises induced by iCNN photoactivation. Our data uncover a cell type-specific cerebellar origin of dystonic crisis and highlight its therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Predicting Drosophila Body Orientation from a Translational Trajectory using an Artificial Neural Network
papers.abstract: Body yaw orientation is a key variable in the analysis of insect flight behavior, yet it remains difficult to measure across the full extent of a trajectory in most experimental settings. Although modern tracking systems reliably capture the position and velocity of the center of mass, resolving body yaw orientation typically requires dedicated hardware confined to a small, purpose-built volume, and is impractical for large-scale or long-duration studies. Here, we develop a data-driven estimator that predicts body yaw orientation for Drosophila directly from translational flight trajectory data. We trained a fully connected feedforward artificial neural network (ANN) on a dataset in which both flight trajectory and body yaw orientation were recorded simultaneously in freely flying Drosophila, using ground velocity and air velocity vectors as input features. We show that the ANN predicts body yaw orientation with a median error of 5.0 degrees, and substantially outperforms linear and Mobius regressions when flies are moving crosswind or downwind. The estimator may be a practical tool for recovering body yaw orientation information from existing trajectory datasets in which only center-of-mass motion was recorded, extending the behavioral and computational analysis of insect navigation to previously inaccessible data.

papers.title: A single dose of the antipsychotic drug clozapine has long-term behavioral and functional effects in mice
papers.abstract: Antipsychotic dosing regimens, commonly daily or via slow-release compounds, are designed to maintain steady-state plasma concentrations. They are guided by their plasma half-life, which is typically in the range of several hours. This schedule contrasts with the slow time course of therapeutic efficacy, which takes days to weeks to develop fully. This discrepancy led us to hypothesize that the effects of a single dose of an antipsychotic drug might be detectable well beyond the time window predicted by receptor occupancy. To test this, we administered a single dose of the antipsychotic drug clozapine to mice. We observed long-term behavioral effects and changes to cortical activity patterns up to several days after administration. Specifically, clozapine induced a decorrelation of activity in the dorsal cortex observable up to 9 days post administration. This effect was driven by a genetically and functionally distinct subset of layer 5 intratelencephalic neurons and was accompanied by an increase in the reliability of long-range inhibitory functional influence on a similar timescale. Thus, a single dose of clozapine triggers changes in the function of specific circuits that outlast the presence of the drug. If antipsychotic action depends on slower processes involving plasticity, longer dosing intervals may warrant further clinical exploration.

papers.title: Temperature-dependent performance scales with maximum heat tolerance across ectotherms
papers.abstract: Temperature fundamentally shapes ectotherm biology, from continuous changes in sublethal performance to acute functional failure at upper thermal limits. Sublethal performance is commonly characterized using thermal performance curves (TPCs), which describe continuous changes in performance across temperatures, whereas acute heat tolerance is often quantified by the critical thermal maximum (CTmax), the temperature marking organism-level functional failure. Whether these dimensions of thermal physiology vary independently or covary as components of a coordinated warm-end thermal phenotype remains unclear. Synthesizing data from more than 100 ectotherm species, we tested how CTmax scales with two key warm-end TPC traits: the thermal optimum (Topt) and the upper limit of performance (TPCmax). Across diverse taxa, both Topt and TPCmax scaled approximately 1:1 with CTmax, and these relationships were broadly consistent across the biological, experimental, and environmental contexts represented in our dataset. Although both slopes were individually consistent with 1:1 scaling, when Topt and TPCmax were compared directly, TPCmax increased more steeply with CTmax than did Topt, such that the declining portion of the TPC widened as CTmax increased. Species with greater acute heat tolerance therefore tended to retain positive performance across a broader range of supra-optimal temperatures before reaching the upper performance limit. Together, these relationships show that sublethal warm-end performance and acute heat tolerance covary systematically across species, supporting their interpretation as broadly coordinated components of the thermal phenotype rather than independent axes of thermal biology.

papers.title: Common variation of cell abundances and gene expression in the human striatum
papers.abstract: The cellular and molecular bases of inter-individual variation in the human brain are not yet understood, particularly beyond the neocortex. Here we describe cellular and gene-expression variation in the striatum and prefrontal cortex from single-nucleus RNA-seq analysis of 3.9 million nuclei from 178 adult brain donors. People with more astrocytes, microglia, or oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) in any one brain region tended to have this property in all gray matter regions sampled. OPCs proportions declined by 40% across ages 30-80 in cortex and striatum. Age-associated gene-expression changes differed substantially across cell types. Donor age was predicted from RNA-expression patterns with a median absolute error of 6.6 years across cell types. Common genetic variants were associated with expression of nearly 10,000 genes; these effects were mostly cell-type-specific and distinguished striatal from cortical neurons. These open-access data provide a foundation for future studies of human brain variation and vulnerabilities.

papers.title: New perspectives in assessing environmental risks for birds: a simple TKTD framework to link growth and reproduction energy budget to chemical stress
papers.abstract: Assessing the risk of pesticides to birds requires models that can extrapolate laboratory data to realistic exposure scenarios. In this work, we propose a new modeling framework BIRDkiss (Bird - Impact on Reproduction via Diet, keep it simple and suitable). This framework integrates a simplified Dynamic Energy Budget (DEBkiss) of organisms and the toxicokinetic-toxicodynamic (TKTD) of chemical substances according to a trait-based approach, thereby reducing the number of parameters to identify and strengthening the statistical robustness of the critical endpoints. The BIRDkiss model describes how food intake and toxicant exposure affect growth and egg production in birds over time. The model is fully embedded within an R package, including routines for calibration, validation and prediction under single-compound scenarios performed via Bayesian inference using standard data from the OECD avian reproduction tests. The BIRDkiss model also allows the simulations of scenarios under both varying food availability and multi-compound exposures based on the two classical mixture-toxicity paradigms: Concentration Addition (CA) and Independent Action (IA). The results of calibration for single compounds show good results matching with observed weights and egg counts. From these calibrations, predictions for new exposure scenarios can be readily generated. For mixtures, the IA algorithm is simpler and does not require to scale variables as in CA. Simulations indicate that high food levels do not further increase egg production (saturation), whereas substantial food reductions markedly decrease reproduction because energy is reallocated to maintenance. Exposure to chemicals combined to low food availability amplify the decline in reproductive output. The ready-to-use mechanistic, open-source BIRDkiss tool enables predicting the impact of pesticides on avian reproduction under realistic dietary exposure profiles. The implementation of CA and IA models is a first step toward mechanistic assessment of chemical mixtures, although validation still requires empirical mixture data. The model highlights the importance of food availability and shows that chemical stress can exacerbate the negative effects of nutritional stress. Integrating such models into regulatory frameworks could improve the ecological relevance of risk assessments.

papers.title: Benchmarking DNA Foundation Models: Biological Blind Spots in Evo2 Variant-Effect Prediction
papers.abstract: DNA foundation models such as Evo2 and DNABERT-2 show promise for variant-effect prediction (VEP), yet rigorous benchmarks assessing their ability to capture established biological constraints remain limited. Here, we introduce controlled benchmarks based on well-characterized nuclear and mitochondrial sequence features. Although Evo2 achieves strong aggregate performance on mitochondrial variants (AUROC = 0.927), our analyses reveal systematic blind spots in short-range signals, including codon usage bias, as well as spurious sensitivity to biologically neutral sequence context. Notably, changes in flanking sequences can cause pathogenic tRNA variants to be misclassified as benign. These findings suggest that Evo2's predictive performance may rely more heavily on learned sequence regularities than on the biological constraints governing variant function, raising concerns about the clinical utility of zero-shot genomic foundation models.Our framework provides a principled basis for standardized model evaluation and for guiding the development of architectures better aligned with biological constraints.

papers.title: Betrayal is worse than loss during cooperation
papers.abstract: Cooperative behavior refers to activities that benefit another individual or benefit both the person performing the behavior and the recipient. Although both betrayal aversion and loss aversion (the financial detriment incurred from betrayal) are established determinants of cooperative behavior, their relative potency remains undetermined. Here, we investigated these effects by integrating computational modeling and event-related potential (ERP) techniques. In two tasks involving risk and cooperation, participants decided whether to take financial risks or to cooperate under possible betrayal. Our results showed that betrayal aversion had a stronger effect on reducing cooperation compared to loss aversion. Furthermore, ERP data demonstrated a temporal pattern consistent with sequential processing: betrayal was encoded early in decision-making, reflected by increased P3 with weaker betrayal aversion, whereas loss aversion manifested later, marked by increased LPP. By dissociating the contributions of betrayal and loss, our finding provides novel insights into the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying cooperative behavior.

papers.title: Genomic identification and multi-tissue transcriptomic profiling of vitamin D3-related genes in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar)
papers.abstract: The metabolic pathway of vitamin D3 is well characterized in mammals, but its genetic basis in teleost fish remains poorly defined. We identified 16 vitamin D3-related genes in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), 14 orthologs of pathway genes and two albumins as candidate carriers, and profiled their expression in a 14-tissue atlas and in seven independent RNA-seq studies. Phylogenetic analysis resolved seven paralog pairs from the salmonid whole-genome duplication. Atlantic salmon and three other euteleost fishes lacked a gc gene, and the genes that flank gc in other fishes were adjacent in their genomes. The proteins annotated as GC in three Oncorhynchus species were albumins. Skin expression of dhcr7, which converts the precursor 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholesterol, was low and differed between studies. The activating enzyme cyp27b1 was barely expressed in five kidney and 21 head kidney samples, including those of the atlas, whereas cyp27b1.a was expressed in the brain and cyp27b1.b in the liver.
