I introduce PV_lo, an index of proportional variability relative to lower abundances, based on all pairwise comparisons and bounded between 0 and 1. Zero counts are handled without data transformation. A sorting-based algorithm reduces the computation from O(n^2) to O(n log n), making the index applicable to long time series. In example series and simulations (Gaussian, Cauchy, rare-crash, bimodal and gradual-decline regimes), PV_lo remained sensitive to crashes and to the contrast between abundance levels, whereas PV_hi levelled off, but PV_hi was more robust against heavy-tailed extremes. In a comparison with series of ordinary fluctuations, PV_lo and SDL separated crashes better than PV_hi and the CV only if the ordinary variability of a population was unknown, and PV_lo did not outperform SDL; during a sustained decline the indices differed little. PV_lo is a computationally efficient index that responds to deep lows on an interpretable ratio scale without transformation of the data, an alternative to SDL that is relevant for screening many populations in a conservation context.

papers.title: Superior Frontal Gyrus Cortical Thickness Mediates the Association Between Openness to Experience and Theory of Mind: Evidence from the Human Connectome Project
papers.abstract: Background: Theory of mind (ToM), the capacity to infer the mental states of others, varies considerably across healthy adults. Openness to experience has been linked both to social-cognitive abilities and to thinner prefrontal cortex, but whether cortical structure statistically accounts for the association between openness and ToM is unknown. We tested whether bilateral superior frontal gyrus (SFG) cortical thickness mediates this association. Methods: Data from 1,049 healthy young adults with complete data were drawn from the Human Connectome Project. ToM was indexed by accuracy on the Heider-Simmel social animation task, openness by the NEO Five-Factor Inventory, and SFG thickness by FreeSurfer. Models adjusted for age, sex, intracranial volume and fluid intelligence; indirect effects were tested with 5,000 bootstrap resamples, and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction was applied. Results: Openness showed a positive total effect on ToM accuracy (beta = .081, p = .009). Higher openness was associated with thinner left and right SFG (beta = -.085 and -.084), and thinner SFG with higher ToM accuracy (beta = -.082 and -.075). Indirect effects were significant (left: .0069, 95% CI [.0010, .0158]; right: .0063, 95% CI [.0007, .0146]), accounting for approximately 8.5% and 7.8% of the total effect, and remained significant after rank-based normalisation of the ceiling-affected ToM scores. Conclusions: SFG cortical thickness partially and statistically mediates the association between openness to experience and social cognition. Because the data are cross-sectional and effects are small, the findings do not establish a causal mechanism, neural efficiency or synaptic pruning, but they identify a candidate structural pathway for longitudinal testing.

papers.title: Enhancing Germination and Assessing the Longevity of Native Plants' Seeds with Dormancy through Different Priming Techniques
papers.abstract: Vachellia pachyceras and Convolvulus oxyphyllus are native species of arid and semi-arid desert regions, including Kuwait. They are inherently adapted to extreme conditions characterized by high temperature, prolonged drought and limited rainfall. They contribute significantly, to restore the ecosystem by providing food and shelter for wildlife. Despite their ecological importance, seed germination in both species is constrained by dormancy, and natural recruitment of seedlings is limited by narrow and unpredictable rainfall windows, severely restricting opportunities for establishment. In this context, seed priming is an effective pre-sowing technique that enables uniform and rapid germination within the short window of favorable conditions. This study aims to identify the optimal seed-priming techniques for these two keystone native species and to assess the effect of priming on seed longevity. The seeds were scarified to remove the physical dormancy prior to priming treatments. Relative seed longevity was measured for primed seeds through artificial ageing and analyzed using probit analysis and analysis of variance. Results showed that hormonal priming [(mechanical scarification + 100 ppm gibberellic acid (GA3)] for six hours and hydropriming (mechanical scarification + soaking in water) for 8 hours (h) were effective treatments among the tested priming treatments for V. pachyceras. The estimated p50 value (i.e., number of days to lose seed viability to 50%) was 22 days for hormonal priming and 21 days for hydropriming. Mechanical scarification followed by one and half hour of hydropriming was the most effective in C. oxyphyllus (p50 = 74 days). Based on these results, the longevity of V. pachyceras and C. oxyphyllus could be considered medium. Further studies are needed to determine the effectiveness of seed priming on additional ecologically and economically important native species to achieve success in revegetation programs.

papers.title: Pycea: a scverse toolkit for single-cell lineage tracing analysis
papers.abstract: Lineage tracing enables reconstruction of cellular histories in development, regeneration, and disease, but integrating lineage data into single-cell analysis workflows remains challenging. We introduce Pycea, a Python toolkit for lineage analysis and visualization, and TreeData, an extension of AnnData that stores lineage trees alongside cellular measurements. TreeData is compatible with Scanpy and other scverse tools, enabling integrated analysis without converting between formats. Pycea provides scalable methods for tree visualization, clade identification, distance comparisons, ancestral state inference, and lineage statistics. This software is open source and available at https://github.com/YosefLab/pycea.

papers.title: Low-pass filtering revisited: ramped phase randomization for cryo-EM map comparison and data augmentation
papers.abstract: Conventional low-pass filters attenuate or remove high-frequency Fourier amplitudes but leave the phases intact wherever the amplitude response stays above zero. As a result, fine-scale detail of the original signal can persist beyond the target resolution. A sharp cutoff removes this detail but produces ringing artifacts. To address both limitations, this work introduces ramped phase randomization, which extends a conventional low-pass filter by adding random offsets to Fourier phases that increase smoothly with spatial frequency. For cryo-EM maps, the correlation between a map at the target resolution and an ideal, noiseless map sets the levels of the phase offsets, with a correction for the finite resolution of the input map. On three published map pairs, ramped phase filtering reduced the higher resolution parent's fine detail to a level similar to that of independently determined maps at the lower target resolution, whereas amplitude-only filtering kept the parent's sharp features. The FSCs between the filtered maps and their parents closely resembled those of the experimental maps. The same filter also serves as a data augmentation approach for neural network-based machine learning. With ramped phase randomization, each augmented copy keeps the power spectrum and low-frequency content of the original example but has a different high-frequency pattern. For simulated CryoBench particles of 16 ribosome assembly states, phase augmentation raised mean test accuracy in all 20 combinations of training-set size and latent dimension, by 20.8 percentage points on average (range from 3.3 points to 44.2 points). On two general deep learning benchmarks, mean test accuracy rose from 92.15% to 96.99% with 60 labelled UCI Synthetic Control traces and from 53.44% to 74.27% with 500 labelled noisy MNIST images. The ramped phase randomization is implemented in an open-source Python package, with a companion browser application for interactive visualization of cryo-EM maps and filtering effects.

papers.title: The human-specific gene FRMPD2B couples postnatal experience to the expansion of cortical connectivity
papers.abstract: The human neocortex is characterized by its uniquely prolonged postnatal developmental period during which experience sculpts neuronal circuits, a process essential to human cognitive abilities. Yet whether human-specific genetic innovations have shaped the activity-dependent mechanisms regulating circuit assembly remains unknown. Here, we identify the human-specific gene FRMPD2B as an activity- and experience-regulated modifier of cortical connectivity. FRMPD2B is primarily expressed in cortico-cortical projection neurons postnatally and throughout childhood. It promotes dendritic, axonal and synaptic development, and is required for proper morphogenesis in xenotransplanted human cortical neurons. FRMPD2B expression is bidirectionally regulated by neuronal activity and experience. This activity-responsiveness was gained after FRMPD2B arose through partial gene duplication, when a retrotransposon insertion remodeled its promoter. Our findings highlight how a series of genetic innovations have led to the emergence of a human-specific activity-regulated developmental program through which postnatal experience drives cortical connectivity expansion, linking genome evolution to human brain plasticity.

papers.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS
papers.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

papers.title: Cortical long-range dynamics track excitation-inhibition balance across cognitive states and organizational principles
papers.abstract: A fundamental question in systems neuroscience is how the brain's excitation-inhibition (E/I) balance shapes the temporal structure of neural activity and whether we can non-invasively recover this relationship from neural scaling properties. We show that MRS-derived E/I balance is expressed in long-range temporal dynamics and constrained by cytoarchitecture. The laminar organisation of inhibitory circuits, spanning agranular to granular cortex, determines how faithfully regional dynamics reflect E/I balance. This neurochemical signature is state-dependent: its relationship with cortical dynamics reverses during task engagement, consistent with traversal of dynamical regimes around a critical point. It extends beyond fMRI to arousal-linked dynamics, indexed by pupil diameter and microsaccades, indicating a global mode of cortical state rather than a regionally isolated property. The imprint of E/I balance on long-range dynamics follows the sensory-association axis at rest, and is reconfigured during task engagement. These findings establish E/I balance as a neurochemical quantity with structured, scalable signatures across the temporal and spatial organization of the human cortex.

papers.title: A Unified World Model in Human Posterior Parietal Cortex
papers.abstract: How does the brain understand the physical world, predict future events, and plan actions? Are these problems solved by a unified world model, as hypothesized by cognitive scientists and artificial intelligence researchers? Posterior parietal cortex has been implicated in all these functions, but whether the same neurons support each of them is unknown. We recorded from the superior parietal lobule (SPL) of two tetraplegic participants implanted with microelectrode arrays. SPL units preferentially engaged by intuitive physics, judging block-tower stability and viewing naturalistic physical events, also predicted whether moving objects would collide hundreds of milliseconds before contact, generalizing between different physical scenarios. These populations also encoded which hand action the participant intended to perform. These findings identify SPL as a substrate for physical world modeling.

papers.title: Twenty-five new microsporidian genomes: Insights into ploidy, reproduction, and the group's pangenome
papers.abstract: Microsporidia are single-celled, obligately intracellular eukaryotic parasites of growing importance. Many aspects of their biology remain enigmatic, partly because of difficulties in sampling, culturing, and experimentally manipulating them. Here, we continue efforts to generate microsporidian genomes from serendipitously infected organisms sequenced for biodiversity genomics initiatives, such as the Darwin Tree of Life Project. We present 25 new microsporidian genomes: 14 biologically complete, including several at (near-)chromosome level, and 11 partial. Using RNA-seq data for three published genomes we identify Prokka as a suitable ab initio annotation approach for Microsporidia. Consistently annotating all available genomes, we investigate gene-content diversity across microsporidian clades. We find that the microsporidian pangenome exhibits extreme diversity, and that current genomic data substantially undersample the group's proteome space. Neither GC content nor genome span consistently explains orthogroup number across lineages, suggesting different evolutionary pressures. We find few one-to-one orthogroups in Microsporidia, as well as few orthogroups that are both lineage-specific and conserved across most species within a given lineage. Finally, Hi-C data confirm that tetraploid Amblyosporida microsporidia occur as two equivalent diploid units. In contrast, one Enterocytozoonida tetraploid genome suggests that all four genome copies occur within a single nucleus (a 'monokaryon'), confirming a previous proposal.

papers.title: Validating static food web model diet matrices using stable isotope simulation
papers.abstract: End-to-end ecosystem models, such as Ecopath with Ecosim (EwE), are valuable tools for resource management. Within these frameworks, trophic interactions, typically derived from stomach contents analyses, govern system-wide energy flow via consumption. However, stomach contents data may be unrepresentative of long-term average diets and assimilated consumption due to factors including differential digestion rates and identifiability of prey, introducing model uncertainty. Because trophic interactions define model structure, variation in modeled diets can alter predictions and management conclusions. Consequently, evaluating and reducing uncertainty in diet matrix compositions is critical for operational acceptance of ecosystem models. Stable isotope analysis provides complementary, time-integrated insight into average diets, but its application for EwE validation has largely been limited to evaluating trophic levels and isotopic niche space. Here, we present a quantitative framework for simulating consumer stable isotope signatures across food webs from parent ecosystem models using a matrix-based mixing model. Using a published Northern Gulf of Mexico EwE model as a case study, we demonstrate Monte Carlo simulation to propagate uncertainty from basal source signatures and trophic discrimination factors. Comparison of predicted signatures with empirical {delta}13C and {delta}34S measurements enables validation of primary carbon sources and benthic-pelagic pathway contributions, revealing agreement in isotope space alongside mismatch in energy pathways. Diagnostic residuals identify discrepancies in diet composition. Model scoring provides a reproducible framework for ranking alternative diet configurations. Redundancy analysis further identifies within-group species coverage differences between stomach contents and isotope datasets as a primary driver of mismatch, highlighting an important consideration for sampling design.

papers.title: Human iEEG recordings during audiovisual speech violations support and extend predictive routing models
papers.abstract: Rather than constantly reconstructing the world solely through sensory input, predictive processing theories posit that the brain utilizes predictions maintained as internal representations to guide sensory processing. An emerging model, predictive routing, proposes that an interplay between neuronal gamma (40-150 Hz) and alpha-beta (10-30 Hz) rhythms implements a dynamic mechanism for predictive processing. Namely, predictions enhance alpha-beta oscillations that suppress gamma activity during the processing of predicted inputs. While this model is supported by animal studies, its validity has not been fully explored within the human brain. The present study addresses this by leveraging human intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings across superior temporal and prefrontal/premotor areas of seven presurgical epilepsy patients during an audiovisual speech paradigm. We calculated iEEG power in the theta, alpha-beta, and high gamma bands during simple auditory deviance, multisensory integration, and a condition where an incongruent visual cue (lip movements) clashed with an auditory stimulus (a syllable), creating audiovisual incongruence that can elicit the McGurk illusion. Results revealed increased high-gamma and decreased alpha-beta power in the superior temporal cortex in response to auditory deviance and the McGurk condition, while frontal areas, despite reflecting a similar decrease in alpha-beta power, did not present this high gamma prediction error signal. Instead, the theta band revealed a strong prediction error signal in the McGurk condition, consistent with theories on the role of theta in reorganizing cortical networks. These results both support and extend existing predictive routing models for human-specific forms of predictive processing.

papers.title: Differentiable Spin-Center Diffusion Model Enables DEER-Guided Generative Pipeline of Weighted Protein Ensembles
papers.abstract: Biological function entails the interconversion of a protein between distinct conformations, an equilibrium modulated by ligands and other physicochemical conditions. Double electron-electron resonance (DEER) spectroscopy captures these ensembles as distance distributions, P(r), between spin label pairs. However, the width of P(r) convolves protein conformational heterogeneity with the rotameric flexibility of the label. Because current spin label models overestimate this contribution, translating P(r) into ensembles has remained indirect and predominantly qualitative. Here, we developed spin-center (SC) diffusion, a differentiable model of the spin label with a tunable spin label rotameric width. Coupled to a frozen Boltz-2 structure generator, SC diffusion enables the entire experimental P(r) to guide ensemble generation at inference time. We demonstrate the robustness of this pipeline on synthetic P(r) of known composition, recovering the ensemble populations, including both components of a bimodal profile. Guided by experimental P(r) measured under different biochemical conditions, ensembles of the transporters PfMATE, LmrP, MhsT and P-glycoprotein were modeled and free energy differences derived from the ensembles in a condition-dependent manner. By embedding a differentiable label model in structure generation, our approach interprets DEER distributions as weighted conformational ensembles, adding a missing thermodynamic grounding to generative protein structure prediction methods.

papers.title: Gene Embedding Hub: a standardized resource for human gene representations
papers.abstract: Gene embeddings are vector representations of gene identity that provide machine-learning models with information from diverse biological sources. However, their use is hindered by a lack of standardization: inconsistent identifiers, formats, and preprocessing conventions. In this work, we present a unified resource of 67 human gene-embedding sets derived from protein, DNA and RNA sequences, biomedical text, bulk expression data, single-cell expression models, functional data, biological networks, knowledge graphs, regulatory genomics and multimodal models, covering up to 20,097 GENCODE-annotated protein-coding genes. The collection includes both published precomputed embeddings and representations generated or extracted from publicly available models and biological data. Each embedding set is organized in a folder containing the embedding matrix, the Ensembl gene identifiers, machine-readable metadata, and processing documentation. We validate the resource by measuring global and local similarity, cross-embedding consensus, and cross-embedding predictability. The collection is designed to allow community-contributed embeddings that meet predefined technical and documentation requirements, enables comparison of gene representations across modalities and provides standardized embeddings for training and downstream applications.

papers.title: A synthetic phageome reveals widespread and diverse human antibody responses to bacteriophages
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages colonize humans, yet their recognition by humoral immunity remains unclear. We developed PhageScan, a PhIP- Seq platform comprising 277,051 phage and 49,630 human viral oligopeptides. Profiling sera from 192 healthy donors without prior phage therapy characterized anti-phage response specificity and revealed widespread, strong IgG reactivity to phages, comparable in prevalence and magnitude to that against human viruses. Recognition patterns were however highly individualized. Among phage sequences, 12,576 peptides were significantly enriched in at least two individuals. Strongly immunogenic epitopes preferentially originated from phages infecting pathogenic bacteria, whereas widely shared ''public'' epitopes were enriched among phages of environmental and food-associated bacteria. ImmE, a lactococcal phage endolysin recognized in 59.9% of individuals, showed reduced antibacterial activity in the presence of sera identified as ImmE-reactive by PhageScan, demonstrating functional relevance. These findings establish phage-directed antibodies as a widespread component of human immunity and PhageScan as a scalable platform for defining phage--antibody interactions.

papers.title: ScanFold3: a robust and rapid approach for identifying structured RNA targets in genomes and transcriptomes
papers.abstract: Background. The rapid expansion of high-throughput transcriptomic datasets has created a critical need for scalable tools to identify functional RNA secondary structures. While thermodynamics-based folding is a well-established method, most algorithms lack the scalability required for genomic-scale datasets due to O(n3) time complexity. Methods. We present ScanFold3, an enhanced version of the ScanFold pipeline that optimizes the "Fold" step for modern computing needs. This version models consensus structure generation as a minimum perfect weighted matching problem on a graph. To ensure maximum scalability, we implemented a Greedy Approximation Algorithm and optimized performance-critical components in C++. Results. Benchmarking on sequences up to 128 kb demonstrates that ScanFold3 achieves a 38-fold to 129-fold increase in speed over ScanFold2. Validation against annotated human RNAs shows that ScanFold3 offers improved positive predictive value (PPV). Most significantly, when ScanFold3 outputs are used as structural constraints for global refolding, it outperforms previous versions across all metrics, including the F1 score. Conclusions. ScanFold3 provides a robust, speedy, and user-friendly method for characterizing the thermodynamics of novel RNA and DNA sequences. It is designed as an efficient first step for high throughput bioinformatic pipelines, capable of paring down chromosome-scale transcriptomic data into stable structures amenable to advanced analysis.

papers.title: A network of bZIP transcription factors and inhibitors enforces differentially proliferative and cytotoxic states in T cells
papers.abstract: The bZIP family of transcription factors (TFs) plays a central role in regulating T-cell exhaustion. Their complex dimeric interactions obscure the roles of individual members, which genetic knockout or overexpression alone poorly resolve. Here, we use overexpression of full-length bZIP family TFs alongside genetically encoded, protein-based inhibitors to probe the effect of increased or decreased bZIP TF activity on CAR T-cell expansion under exhausting conditions. Enrichment of inhibitors of pro-exhaustion TFs (CREM, NFIL3) illustrated the utility of this approach. The screen enriched full-length TFs of established anti-exhaustion relevance and identified underappreciated bZIP TFs such as BATF2. Detailed comparison of several bZIP TFs and inhibitors revealed distinct effects on proliferation, persistence, and cytotoxicity. We investigated combinations of pro-cytotoxic JUN, pro-proliferative BATF2, and a novel inhibitor (AEL-CREM) of pro-dysfunction CREM. Distinct pairs were more advantageous for maintenance of cytotoxicity or proliferation, revealing relationships between BATF2, JUN-, and CREB1-family bZIPs. Using a combination of epistasis, transcriptome, proteome, and AP-MS interactome analyses of BATF2 and AEL-CREM, we discovered functional overlap in their inhibition of pro-dysfunction CREB1-family activity, potentially driven by unexpected binding of CREB1-family members by overexpressed BATF2. Their function diverged in BATF2's early promotion of pro-proliferation AP-1 activity and later physical and functional interactions with BACH2, contributing to persistence. These findings were mirrored in murine chronic viral infection and syngeneic tumor models, where BATF2 or AEL-CREM overexpression were notably pro-proliferative and anti-exhaustion. Together, these results illuminate new connections and functional roles enabled by bZIP family perturbations, with implications for modulating T-cell state.

papers.title: LIMBER: A Hybrid RNA Foundation Model for Predicting and Understanding RNA Structure and Function
papers.abstract: RNA foundation models offer a promising route to decoding the relationships between RNA sequence, structure and function, yet how model shapes the acquisition and organization of biological information remains poorly understood. Here we introduce Layer-Interleaved Mamba-Bidirectional Encoder for RNA (LIMBER), a hybrid foundation model integrating bidirectional self-attention with selective state-space modeling, pretrained on 40.5 million non-coding RNA sequences. Through task-specific fine-tuning, LIMBER achieves leading performance on secondary-structure prediction and non-coding RNA classification benchmarks, while demonstrating strong transferability to translation-related tasks and RNA--small-molecule interaction prediction. Beyond model development, we establish a unified, task-agnostic framework to systematically evaluate and interpret the biological knowledge intrinsically acquired by RNA foundation models. This framework validates LIMBER's strong capabilities in recovering RNA structures and predicting mutational effects, while uncovering a hierarchical, task-dependent organization of different biological information across model layers. By further systematically training and evaluating a broad panel of model variants spanning model capacity, training duration and dataset size, we uncover distinct scaling behaviors across structural, evolutionary and functional capabilities. Together, these findings establish LIMBER as a versatile RNA foundation model and provide broader insights into how architectural design, internal representations and scaling shape the learning of RNA sequence-structure-function relationships.

papers.title: Improving Molecular Docking Pose Recovery through Targeted Side-Chain Monte Carlo Sampling of an Apo Structure
papers.abstract: Receptor flexibility complicates molecular docking when only an unbound (apo) protein structure is available. Local side-chain rearrangements can alter binding-pocket accessibility and ligand complementarity, motivating approaches that sample these motions efficiently. Here, we evaluate a targeted Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) protocol that combines local and larger side-chain torsional proposals with periodic molecular dynamics (MD) relaxation under harmonic backbone restraints. Receptor ensembles generated from an apo structure were evaluated against 859 experimental complexes from the OpenBind 2A protease benchmark and compared with the apo receptor and ensembles generated by restrained and unrestrained MD. With regular-space representative selection, MCMC recovered a ligand pose within 2 [A] of the experimental pose for 74.4% of complexes, compared with 51.0% for apo and 59.5% for restrained MD. Median minimum ligand heavy-atom RMSD decreased from 1.96 [A] for apo and 1.82 [A] for restrained MD to 1.62 [A] for MCMC. The largest gains occurred for complexes with greater side-chain displacement relative to pocket backbone displacement, consistent with the motions targeted by the protocol. MCMC representatives retained pocket geometries within the experimentally observed range, whereas unrestrained-MD representatives exhibited reduced pocket free volume and poor recovery. These findings support targeted side-chain sampling as a practical approach to generating apo-derived docking ensembles. The reported improvements measure best-case pose coverage across generated poses and receptors; their extension to prospective pose ranking and virtual screening remains to be established.

papers.title: EMBER: Contextualized gene representations enable compositional prediction across cellular perturbations
papers.abstract: Predicting the effects of individual and combined perturbations is central to identifying context-specific vulnerabilities and designing targeted interventions. Yet learning gene representations that integrate functional relationships with cellular state and transfer across perturbation tasks remains challenging. Here, we present EMBER, a gene-centric foundation model that learns context-dependent functional representations of genes. EMBER combines interaction-guided contrastive learning with masked expression reconstruction during pretraining on a single-cell corpus curated for diversity and balanced sampling across cell types and experimental batches. EMBER decouples gene representation learning from task-specific prediction through a composable embedding framework: the pretrained encoder remains frozen, while lightweight probes combine contextualized gene embeddings to predict individual and combined perturbation effects. The same pretrained representations support single-gene perturbation-response prediction, digenic interaction prediction, and multi-target drug-response prediction. EMBER improves cross-context perturbation-response prediction and genetic-interaction ranking relative to evaluated baselines. EMBER also prioritized SCFD1, a mediator of autophagosome-lysosome fusion, as a candidate dependency during mTOR inhibition. Together, these results establish contextualized gene embeddings as reusable building blocks for modeling genetic and pharmacological perturbations, supporting the prioritization of genetic interactions and context-specific interventions for experimental testing.

papers.title: The Findings Workflow: An agentic, collaborative, provenance-tracked framework for scientific data analysis with Claude Code
papers.abstract: Scientists presented with quantitative data often face two related problems: confidence that an analysis is statistically and computationally correct, and provenance sufficient to reproduce the resulting figures and conclusions. Large language models (LLMs) can make sophisticated analyses accessible through a collaborative, conversational interface, but unstructured use can worsen both problems by producing plausible but incorrect results and obscuring the steps that produced them. Here we present the Findings Workflow, a free, open-source Claude Code plugin designed to retain the flexibility of conversational LLM-assisted analysis while placing it within a structured, verifiable, and reproducible environment. The workflow uses staged, gated progression to ensure the science, metadata, and data are understood and tested data loaders are built before downstream analysis begins. Specialized subagents perform statistical analysis, programming, visualization, research, reporting, and validation, with independent review incorporated throughout. The plugin also provides vetted analysis templates, conventions, and methodological guidance that serve as trusted sources of opinion when deciding how analyses should be performed. Scientists remain actively involved throughout, exploring their data and directing the analysis through natural-language conversation, while the workflow supplies structure, verification, and persistent state around that collaboration. Findings are recorded automatically together with the data, code, methods, figures, and provenance needed to reproduce them. We demonstrate the workflow with a worked example that reproduces central findings from a published plasma extracellular vesicle proteomics dataset examining Alzheimer's disease (Mag-Net). Together, these features are designed to make LLM-assisted scientific analysis easier to trust, inspect, and reproduce without sacrificing its conversational and exploratory nature.

papers.title: NMR assignment and functional characterization of biotechnologically modified xanthan
papers.abstract: Xanthan gum is one of the most important industrial microbial polysaccharides, yet comprehensive molecular-level structural characterization remains limited because of its high molecular weight, conformational rigidity, and severe spectral overlap in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Here, we present a near-complete 1H/13C NMR chemical shift assignment of the xanthan repeating unit by combining multidimensional NMR spectroscopy with targeted glycosyltransferase knockout strains and controlled enzymatic depolymerization. Comparative analysis of wild-type xanthan and{Delta} gumI and{Delta} gumK variants enabled the unambiguous assignment of {beta}-mannose and glucuronic acid resonances, and, by extension, of the remaining sugars, supporting future structural studies of engineered xanthan variants. In addition, we investigated how side-chain composition affects xanthan properties by analyzing genetically modified variants lacking specific acetyl, pyruvyl, or sugar residues. Temperature-dependent 1H NMR determined order-disorder transition temperatures and revealed that removing pyruvate or negatively charged side-chain components increased thermal stability, whereas losing the terminal {beta}-mannose destabilized the ordered conformation. Together, these results establish a robust NMR assignment for xanthan and provide new insights into how individual side-chain substituents influence the structural stability of this polysaccharide, facilitating the rational characterization of engineered xanthan variants and structurally closely related polysaccharides.

papers.title: Microbead-Based Heterodimer Assay for Amplification-Free Detection of Single-Stranded DNA
papers.abstract: Direct detection of rare nucleic-acid targets without molecular amplification requires specific recognition events to be made observable while remaining distinguishable from nonspecific interactions. Here, we introduce a microbead-based heterodimer assay (MBHA) that converts two-site recognition of single-stranded DNA into spatially resolved, two-color bead-pairing events for direct nucleic-acid detection. Two spectrally distinct microbead populations are functionalized with partially double-stranded DNA probes exposing target-binding domains complementary to separate regions of the target. Target-mediated bridging produces heterotypic bead pairs that are classified by fluorescence identity and an interparticle-distance criterion, while residual background is evaluated relative to blank measurements. Under the tested conditions, 166 fM was the lowest target concentration exceeding the blank-derived detection threshold. A sequence-scrambled synthetic non-target DNA remained below threshold across the tested concentration range, and detection at 166 fM was retained in the presence of 1 uM non-target DNA, corresponding to an approximately six-million-fold molar excess. Probe redesign further extended the assay to a second 60-nucleotide synthetic DNA target derived from the SARS-CoV-2 ORF1ab sequence. This proof-of-concept study establishes heterodimer counting as an amplification-free measurement strategy in which rare molecular-recognition events are made directly observable and individually classifiable without increasing target copy number.

papers.title: Laminin-Derived Peptides Bind Neuropilin-1 at the VEGF-A165 Binding Pocket
papers.abstract: Neuropilin-1 (NRP-1) is associated with glioblastoma progression and contains a b1-domain pocket that binds the C-terminal region of VEGF-A165. Whether laminin-derived peptide fragments can associate with this site is unknown. AlphaFold 3 complex prediction followed by 15 s of all-atom production molecular dynamics simulation, trajectory-based pocket occupancy and interaction analyses, and FoldX energetic scoring was performed to compare binding of the laminin-derived pentapeptide Ac-Tyr-Ile-Gly-Ser-Arg-NH2 (peptide 1) with its retro (Ac-Arg-Ser-Gly-Ile-Tyr-NH2, peptide 2) and retro-inverso (Ac-arg-ser-Gly-ile-tyr-NH2, peptide 3) analogs. Peptide 1 showed the highest mean equilibrated occupancy of the canonical VEGF-A165 pocket (60.3 +/- 34.6%) compared with peptide 2 (25.9 +/- 32.7%) and peptide 3 (21.4 +/- 29.5%), while sampling interactions with canonical pocket residues including Asp320, Tyr297, and Tyr353; FoldX binding-energy estimates were similar across peptides despite their differing pocket persistence. Complementary nanoDSF measurements using recombinant NRP-1 and synthetic peptides yielded apparent dissociation constants in the low micromolar range for all three peptides (12.7 M - 33.3 M), providing experimental support for the predicted interactions. These results support persistent, sequence-dependent association of peptide 1 with the VEGF-A165 binding site of b1-NRP-1 and identify peptide analogs as a candidate for further optimization as an NRP-1-binding peptide.

papers.title: Follistatin-like 1 Promotes Neutrophil-mediated Host Defense against Klebsiella pneumoniae
papers.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a leading cause of pneumonia and highly burdensome etiology of antibiotic-resistant infections constituting an urgent public health threat. Follistatin-like 1 (FSTL-1) is implicated in many processes including lung development and homeostasis, tissue remodeling, and inflammation though its role in antibacterial immunity remains poorly defined. We have observed that FSTL-1 is elevated in the lungs of both humans and mice during bacterial pneumonia. Using an inducible Fstl1 knockout mouse model, we demonstrate that FSTL-1 is required for pulmonary bacterial clearance and neutrophil recruitment during K. pneumoniae infection. Recombinant FSTL-1 rescues Fstl1-deficient susceptibility and enhances clearance of K. pneumoniae in wild-type mice. Mechanistically, FSTL-1-mediated protection was lost upon neutrophil depletion and in Cd14-deficient or Nr4a1 deficient mice, components of a lung-specific neutrophil transcriptional program. These findings identify FSTL-1 as a lung-derived factor that licenses neutrophil-mediated antibacterial defense via a novel FSTL-1/CD14/NR4A1-dependent signaling pathway critical for protection against bacterial pneumonia.

papers.title: Unravelling genomic and environmental contributions to nitrogen-use efficiency in tropical maize through Bayesian causal forests
papers.abstract: Nitrogen fertilisation is one of the largest variable input costs in maize production, and genotypes differ in how efficiently they convert added nitrogen into yield. Breeding for nitrogen-use efficiency therefore depends on knowing not only the average response of the crop to nitrogen but how that response varies across genotypes and environments. We frame this as a problem of causal inference and estimate the effect of an ideal versus low nitrogen regime on three maize traits jointly (grain yield, plant height and ear height) using a multivariate Bayesian causal forest. To our knowledge, this is among the first studies to quantify the effect of nitrogen in a genotyped breeding panel as a formally identified causal quantity, estimated from a designed contrast within the potential-outcomes framework, rather than as the genotype-environment association that genomic selection and association mapping report. The trial suits a causal reading: 614 single-cross hybrids were grown under both nitrogen levels in adjacent plots sharing weather and soil, so nitrogen was assigned by design rather than confounded with genotype or environment, and the estimated propensity score was close to 0.5. The leading principal components of the additive genomic relationship matrix were placed in the moderator set, so that both the baseline outcome and the treatment effect could vary with genomic background. Ideal nitrogen raised all three traits (grain yield +0.59, 95% credible interval 0.51 to 0.67; plant height +0.095; ear height +0.044, in adjusted-phenotype units). The heterogeneity of the effect was almost entirely environmental, with a small genotypic component and negligible genotype-by-environment interaction; the posterior credible interval of the effect was wider than the spread among genotypes, so differences in responsiveness among hybrids were only weakly resolved. Reading the two tree ensembles separately indicated that genomic background governs the yield level while climate governs the response to nitrogen, the leading genomic contribution being a single axis. A reaction-norm variance decomposition and cross-validated prediction corroborated this reading. A multivariate causal forest with genomic moderators, read through its two ensembles and reported with posterior uncertainty, is a suitable and transparent tool for studying nitrogen response in breeding material.

papers.title: Genetic diversity of endangered Acropora spp. corals in Bonaire: implications for restoration and gene banking
papers.abstract: Species restoration is a valuable tool to combat biodiversity loss. However, maintaining genetic diversity in species restoration is challenging, particularly for species that can reproduce asexually, such as plants and corals, because a seemingly diverse collection of individuals could be composed of many clones of a few genotypes. Caribbean elkhorn and staghorn corals (Acropora palmata, A. cervicornis) are critically endangered reef-building corals that are a major target for restoration. To better understand the genetic diversity of an Acropora spp. restoration program and interpret local population genetic structure, we conducted microsatellite genotyping on the gene banks of 35 A. palmata lineages and 25 A. cervicornis lineages maintained by Reef Renewal Foundation Bonaire (RRFB) in the Caribbean Netherlands. We found that RRFB had high genotypic richness for A. palmata (0.971) and A. cervicornis (1.0) and estimated that they captured 88.9% and 74.7% of Bonaires microsatellite asymptotic allelic diversity, respectively. Compared to populations of Acropora spp. studied in other locations across the Caribbean, A. palmata in Bonaire had relatively low expected heterozygosity, while A. cervicornis was greater than approximately half of other populations. Across Bonaire and for both coral species, we did not find evidence for genetic structuring among spatially separated subpopulations, indicating that both species are likely well-connected around the island. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of RRFBs strategies to capture high genetic diversity and can be used to inform future initiatives on coral sexual breeding and assisted gene flow beyond Bonaire.

papers.title: RNA assignment and segmentation geometry in Visium HD profiles of fibrostenotic Crohn's disease
papers.abstract: Retrospective reuse of spatial transcriptomics often starts from a deposited bin-level Seurat object rather than the inputs needed to revisit upstream molecular processing. We tested whether image segmentation could support a defensible cell-like reconstruction under this constraint in two complete H&E-stained intestinal sections from a Visium HD study of Crohn's disease-associated fibrostenosis (GSE302569). The available data comprised 18,085 genes, 988,942 original 8 {micro}m bins and 179,596,575 UMIs. We evaluated 20 segmentation configurations in the preserved image coordinate system using a common bin-centre assignment rule, without restarting Space Ranger or introducing higher-resolution expression. RNA assignment ranged from 0% to 74.68% in CD1 and 0% to 64.05% in CD2. Expansion increased recovery but did not eliminate merged regions, straight boundaries or within-bin ambiguity; approximately 70-73% of InstanSeg brightfield nuclear regions received no assigned RNA. All 38 non-empty configuration-slice combinations underwent native full-mode RCTD against the same nine-group scIBD reference. Mean slice-level RNA recovery was negatively associated with primary-component dominance across 19 configurations (descriptive Spearman {rho} = -0.77). Neither dominant-call agreement nor concentrated RCTD support validates boundaries or cell identity. The observed limitations in RNA recovery, region geometry, and compositional support did not establish any tested configuration as a reliable single-cell reconstruction from these inputs. The findings identify limitations of retrospective single-cell reconstruction from the available binned inputs, not the impossibility of cell-resolved analysis from suitable original data.

papers.title: Neuronal and glial transcriptional states vary with proximity to tangle-bearing neurons in the human entorhinal cortex
papers.abstract: More neurons die in Alzheimer's disease than form tangles, and tangle-bearing neurons can persist for decades, so tangles alone cannot explain degeneration. We combined 6,000-plex spatial transcriptomics with PHF1 immunofluorescence (167,176 cells; 9 donors) and imaging mass cytometry (170,195 cells; 62 donors), measuring each cell's distance to the nearest tangle. Tangle-bearing layer 2-3 excitatory neurons were enriched late along a trajectory of increasing microtubule-associated, synaptic and V-ATPase expression, with elevated p62 and K48-ubiquitin. Tangle-free neurons shared more of this state the closer they lay to a tangle, including higher chaperone and autophagy scores, p62 and nuclear size. Nearby glia had higher disease-associated scores, with astrocytes expressing less GFAP. Excitatory, but not inhibitory, neuron loss was greatest in subtypes closest to tangles and cortical depths richest in phosphorylated tau. Selective neuronal vulnerability may reflect not only a neuron's susceptibility to forming a tangle but also where it lies relative to one.

papers.title: Ascorbate and TET2 couple balanced hematopoiesis to disease tolerance
papers.abstract: Infections stimulate myelopoiesis but this comes at the cost of reduced production of other lineages. It is unclear if this imbalance is protective or damaging, and if factors that promote balanced hematopoiesis can impact infection pathology. Here we show that the ascorbate-TET axis limits excessive myelopoiesis, promotes balanced hematopoiesis, and is essential for surviving malaria. Hematopoietic-specific ascorbate depletion promoted myelopoiesis. The effects of ascorbate were mediated by TET2/TET3 activity in myeloid progenitors. Combined ascorbate and TET2 depletion markedly skewed hematopoiesis to the myeloid lineage and impaired erythropoiesis. Ascorbate is commonly depleted in infections, but the functional significance of this remains unclear. In the absence of ascorbate and TET2, mice infected with Plasmodium parasites could clear the pathogen, but had exacerbated myeloid and impaired erythroid response, anemia, and tissue damage and they succumbed to infection, indicating compromised disease tolerance. Therefore ascorbate and TET2 promote balanced hematopoiesis to impart tolerance to malaria.

papers.title: Batch Effect Correction to Enhance Utility of a Publicly Available ALS Proteomics Dataset
papers.abstract: Large, publicly available databases of patient data have been successful in identifying associations between neurodegenerative diseases and biological features that might otherwise go unnoticed. The Answer ALS Consortium is one such database that has generated a rich repository of multi-omic data from people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). However, large studies can suffer from batch effects that obscure genuine biological signal and prevent experiment reproducibility. In this study, we identified a batch effect in the Answer ALS 1-2 proteomic dataset (508 samples x 3,643 proteins) and corrected the effect using both the internal controls provided by Answer ALS and the batch effect-correction algorithm (BECA) ComBat. We identified a batch effect in the Answer ALS Dataset 1-2 proteomic dataset that, uncorrected, may obscure biology. Proteins MOS and H4 were outliers of expression in the dataset that correlated with the batch effect. Removing MOS and H4 did not correct the effect fully but did reveal new principal component (PC) contributing proteins related to motor neurons and potentially ALS: AINX, NFL, and NFM. The batch differential controls (BDCs) provided by Answer ALS were used to correct samples in their respective batches. ComBat, a well-characterized BECA, was applied to the dataset both before (ComBat-BDC) and after (BDC-ComBat) correction with the BDCs. BDC-ComBat was the only method that successfully reduced batch effect across the entire dataset. This method also preserved four of the top six PC-contributing proteins from the original dataset, including three neuronal proteins, suggesting that the corrected dataset recapitulates biology as well as the variability of the original dataset. Altogether, we produced a version of the Answer ALS proteomic dataset (354 samples by 3,641 proteins) with globally reduced batch effect and protein-level reduced batch effect. This version of the dataset recapitulates the individual protein variability and important neuronal proteins of the original. We also created a workflow for identifying and correcting batch effects that can be applied to other large data repositories.

papers.title: Computational Repurposing of FDA Approved Drugs Against Cyclin Dependent Kinase (CDK2)
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing is an approach for identifying new therapeutic with existing FDA approved drugs. Cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) is an important regulator of cell cycle progression. The present study aimed to identify FDA-approved drugs with potential binding activity against CDK2 using a Computational drug-repurposing approach. The crystal structure of Human CDK2 (PDB ID: 3PY0) was used for Molecular docking, followed by Protein Ligand Interaction Profiler (PLIP) analysis to evaluate Protein Ligand interactions. Further for drug-likeness and pharmacokinetic properties using Swiss ADME and for Predicted toxicity using ProTox Was done. Based on this docking affinity, interaction profiles, drug-likeness, pharmacokinetics and toxicity, the best target was selected. Carteolol demonstrated the most balanced overall computational profile and was selected as the primary candidate for potential computational finding to provide repurposing against CDK2. Experimental studies are required to validate its direct binding and inhibitory activity against CDK2.

papers.title: Development of a mouse model to investigate the effect of exertional heat stress on skeletal muscle
papers.abstract: Increased body temperature during exercise is considered a risk factor for skeletal muscle injury. There are various murine models of heat exposure-induced organ injury. The present study has attempted to develop a mouse model of skeletal muscle injury associated with exercise-induced whole body hyperthermia. C57BL/6J male mice were randomly assigned into control (CON) and exercise (EX) groups (n = 6 per group). EX group exercised on a programmed, motorized wheel, while CON group remained in a mouse cage in an environmental chamber at 35 degree C for ~3 hours. EX group showed a significantly higher average body core temperature (38.5 degree C +/- 0.3) compared to CON group (37.3 degree C +/- 0.3). Plasma myoglobin levels were significantly higher in EX group than in CON. Additionally, exercise significantly impaired skeletal muscle and mitochondria, as evidenced by elevated TBARS and caspase-3 levels and reduced ATP and Complex IV levels in gastrocnemius muscles in EX group. We developed a mouse model of exercise-induced mild whole body hyperthermia that recapitulates many key features of heat stress-induced skeletal muscle injury. This novel model will provide a useful tool for future investigation into the mechanisms of and intervention strategies for muscle exertional heat injury.

papers.title: Infection-related images reduce cortical edge metastability: a specification-curve analysis of a block-design fMRI study
papers.abstract: Cues of infection evoke disgust, attentional capture, withdrawal and shifts in social orientation, a set of responses attributed to the behavioral immune system. Responses this varied have to be coordinated, as the effects of inflammation are, so they should be visible in whole-cortex coupling. We predicted that infection-related images hold cortical dynamics in a narrower repertoire, reducing cortical edge metastability, the temporal variability of mean cofluctuation across parcel pairs. In two fMRI runs, 44 adults viewed alternating 18-s blocks of infection-related and neutral images; the primary test was specified before we looked at the data. That test gave Cohen's d = -0.31 (permutation p = .042), and 263 of 480 specifications were significant, all negative (joint p < .001). With global signal regression, the synchrony-based reduction survived removal of the stimulus-locked response, detrending, and motion, white-matter and cerebrospinal-fluid regression (d = -0.47), recurred in the second run (d = -0.44), and was smaller on strictly alternating blocks (d = -0.36). Without global signal regression, the pre-specified effect did not survive white-matter and cerebrospinal-fluid regression. Individual-difference predictions were not supported, and participants' contrasts did not replicate across runs. Infection-related images reduce the variability of residual global cofluctuation at the group level; whether this is specific to pathogen cues remains open.

papers.title: Homoharringtonine targets XPC to inhibit DNA damage repair and sensitize tumors to platinum-based chemotherapy
papers.abstract: DNA damage repair (DDR) is essential for preserving genomic stability and also represents a key targetable axis in cancer drug development. Here, we identify and validate homoharringtonine (HHT), a clinically approved antileukemic drug, as a novel DDR inhibitor using a phenotype-driven, high-content screen based on 53BP1 Tudor-domain foci formation. Mechanistically, HHT directly binds XPC, a critical nucleotide excision repair (NER) factor, with high affinity (Kd = 158.4 nM) in a manner dependent on Thr795 of XPC. HHT disrupts XPC-damaged DNA binding, impairs NER, and reduces non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) efficiency. Consequently, HHT sensitizes tumor cells to platinum-based chemotherapy in vitro and in vivo. These findings establish a phenotype-based platform for DDR inhibitor discovery, identify HHT as a first-in-class XPC inhibitor and uncover a previously unrecognized mechanism of HHT that may be exploited to enhance platinum-based therapy in solid tumors.

papers.title: The Quagmire of Immunogenicity-Guided Antibody Design: Labels Limit Progress
papers.abstract: Generative sequence-based antibody design is increasingly steered by learned property predictors, so a design objective is only as well specified as the labels behind its oracle. Immunogenicity is among the most clinically consequential properties to condition on, and among the least well specified: the supervisory signal is a single anti-drug-antibody percentage (ADA%) per molecule, aggregated from published trials. To analyze that signal, we first extended and corrected the widely used 217-entry dataset to 231 therapeutics with paired sequences, spanning formats from mouse to fully human. Then, we manually reconstructed the clinical evidence for 110 of them from primary sources. We find that an antibody format lookup outperforms every sequence-based learned predictor on the 231-antibody dataset. Apparent accuracy tracks the format composition of the evaluation split rather than sequence signal. Furthermore, the labels understate their own evidence: molecules labeled at [≤]6 ADA% span up to 86% across trials. We recomputed labels from the trial-level measurements and found that the advantage of the format-based approach disappears, while the sequence-based predictors degrade less under the cohort-weighted mean. We conclude that progress is limited by the label itself, and recommend reporting ADA% at the trial level, treating the target as a distribution rather than a point value, and evaluating against a format-based baseline.

papers.title: Pathogenicity of autoreactive TH17 cells is modulated by the TRPM7 kinase
papers.abstract: The melastatin-like transient receptor potential channel, TRPM7, is crucial for signaling in leukocytes. It harbors a channel domain, permeable to divalent cations as well as a serine/threonine -kinase, phosphorylating inter alia SMAD2. TRPM7 kinase activity is essential for the differentiation of non-pathogenic T helper 17 (TH17) cells as well as for T cell colonization and alloreactivity in the gut. As pathogenic TH17 (pTH17) cells drive autoimmune diseases, we studied TRPM7 kinase involvement in pTH17 polarization and function as well as in the development of multiple sclerosis (MS), using human T cells and established murine experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) models. Our results reveal an elevated TRPM7 activity in T effector cells derived from the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of MS patients, in line with higher functional TRPM7 expression on human TH17 cells. Utilizing a mouse line with disrupted kinase activity (Trpm7R/R), we uncovered both impaired differentiation of pathogenic TH17 cells as well as a significantly milder course of TH17-mediated transfer EAE in Trpm7R/R mice compared to Trpm7+/+ controls. In the CNS of Trpm7R/R mice, the number of FOXP3+ T cells (Tregs) was increased, while fewer TH17 cells infiltrated the CNS due to a migration defect of transferred pTH17 cells in the Trpm7R/R hosts and a failure to reactivate in the intestine, due to reduced MHCII signaling. Thus, inactivation of TRPM7 kinase may represent a promising therapeutic strategy targeting both differentiation and reactivation of pTH17 cells while preserving Tregs function and thereby dampening CNS inflammation in MS.

papers.title: FateDriver: Weakly supervised dual-view graph learning for transition-specific prioritization of candidate regulators in cellular reprogramming
papers.abstract: Cellular reprogramming supports regenerative medicine, yet the endogenous regulators of a specified source-to-target transition remain incompletely defined. Existing computational methods rank candidate regulators from network topology, trajectory dynamics, or cell-state labels, leaving unused the factors experimentally delivered to induce the transition. We present FateDriver, a weakly supervised dual-view graph neural network that jointly represents cells and genes from single-cell transcriptomes, treats the delivered factors as sparse gene-level labels, and ranks the remaining genes for a specified transition under a positive--unlabeled formulation. Across two OSKM datasets and one GMT dataset, FateDriver ranked first or second among six methods in recovering externally curated reference genes, exceeded a supervision-matched non-graph model despite weaker co-expression with the delivered factors, and achieved the highest recovery of protein targets of pluripotency-inducing chemical cocktails in both OSKM datasets. Holding either the source or the endpoint fixed yielded distinct candidate programs, including a DDX58--interferon axis associated with cells lacking endogenous pluripotency markers. Applying the same framework to candidate source--target pairs prioritized distinct candidate origins for two in vivo partially reprogrammed intestinal populations. FateDriver converts sparse experimental knowledge into transition-specific hypotheses for regulator prioritization from single-cell trajectories.

papers.title: Plasma untargeted metabolomics reveals distinct metabolic disturbances between sexes following inhalation of ultrafine particles and exposure to aircraft noise in mice
papers.abstract: Traffic noise and air pollution, particularly ultrafine particles (UFP), are significantly associated with health risks. However, the systemic metabolic consequences of the combined effects of UFP and aircraft noise (AN) exposure on health remain poorly understood. We aimed to investigate changes in plasma metabolites in healthy wildtype C57BL/6J mice following whole-body inhalation exposure to UFP (average diameter <40 nm), AN and their combination (UFP+AN). Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based untargeted plasma metabolomics analysis was undertaken for UFP, AN, and combined UFP+AN-exposed mice of both sexes. This study identified a total of 1146 plasma metabolites. Across exposure groups, AN induced the greatest plasma metabolomic changes in both sexes, while UFP significantly altered metabolites only in females, indicating a sex-specific response. The combined UFP+AN exposure produced a modestly enhanced effect in males compared with either single exposure but showed an attenuated effect in females. Pathway analyses revealed that lipid and amino acid metabolism were the most affected, followed by xenobiotics, and cofactors and vitamins, after exposure in both female and male mice. Additionally, in the clean air control group, we identified sex differences in 49 plasma metabolites, which mostly included lipids and amino acids. Following exposure, however, sex-dependent metabolic differences became more pronounced and exposure-specific, suggesting that UFP and AN have distinct effects on plasma metabolome of male and female mice that extend beyond baseline sexual dimorphism observed in unexposed animals. To our knowledge, this study is the first comprehensive characterization of systemic metabolic changes in mice after combination of UFP and AN exposure, providing new insight into the interplay between traffic noise and air pollution health risks.

papers.title: Interpreting graph neural networks reveals microbial association patterns in inflammatory bowel diseases
papers.abstract: Traditional machine learning models trained on gut microbiome abundance profiles can distinguish individuals with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) from non-IBD individuals. However, their interpretation typically considers taxa in isolation, making it difficult to understand how associations between taxa contribute to predictions. Here, we inferred individual-specific microbial association networks from longitudinal metagenomics data of 106 individuals in HMP2/iHMP and used them to train and interpret graph neural network (GNN) models, which we compared with abundance-based models such as Random Forest (RF). Although RF achieved higher predictive performance (AUPRC ~0.59 vs 0.446), interpreting the GNNs revealed that their predictions relied on a densely connected module of co-abundant Bacteroidales species. Unlike the taxa prioritized by RF, these species were not differentially abundant between conditions. In an independent cohort, this module carried most of the predictive signal, and removing its associations reduced performance to near chance. These results show that coordinated association structure, rather than abundance shifts alone, is a feature of the IBD gut microbiome, and that interpreting GNNs can uncover such patterns that complement abundance-based analyses.

papers.title: A conserved cold stress syndrome defines insect chill tolerance
papers.abstract: The ability to withstand cold is arguably one of the most important traits defining the biogeographical distribution of insects. For most species, those classified as chill susceptible, cold tolerance is limited by the ability to maintain vital physiological functions at low temperature. However, there is currently no unified understanding of how physiological failure develops during cold stress or how this process explains variation in cold sensitivity within and among species. Although disruption of ion homeostasis has been implicated in chilling injury, it remains unclear whether it represents a common physiological limit across cold stress intensities and degrees of chill tolerance. Here, we tested whether ion balance disruption represents a unifying physiological syndrome of chill susceptibility by simultaneously quantifying cold mortality and hemolymph [K] in Drosophila. We examined this relationship across i) a broad range of cold stress intensities, ii) 25 species spanning extensive variation in cold sensitivity, biogeography and phylogeny, and iii) acclimation groups of D. melanogaster developed between 12 and 27{degrees}C. Across all comparisons, mortality was associated with the same cold-stress response, characterized by progressive hyperkalemia and mortality following a ~150% increase in hemolymph [K] above baseline ([K]crit). In contrast, adaptive and plastic variation in cold sensitivity was explained by differences in the critical temperature at which ion homeostasis failed (Tc). Extending this framework to published data from other insect orders revealed a remarkably similar [K]crit, suggesting that ionoregulatory collapse represents a conserved physiological constraint defining insect cold survival.

papers.title: Cross-modal transfer enables zero-shot prediction of drug responses across cell types
papers.abstract: Genetic perturbation responses capture the functional consequences of gene-level interventions, providing functional information for drug-response prediction beyond baseline gene expression. Within the same cellular context, genetic and chemical perturbations engage shared regulatory networks, providing a biological basis for transferring response information between perturbation modalities. Here we introduce GRAFT, a framework that combines genetic-to-chemical transfer with cross-context prediction to infer drug-induced transcriptional responses without drug measurements in the target context. Across benchmarked LINCS and external contexts, GRAFT improved response correlation, directional agreement and magnitude reconstruction over competing methods, particularly for drugs with context-dependent responses. GRAFT-Adapt further refines predictions of unmeasured responses using a small number of drug measurements from the target context. GRAFT-Atlas spans 13 cellular contexts and 7,856 drug catalog entries, comprising 102,128 predictions for drug-context combinations. The atlas captured recognizable pharmacological neighborhoods, shared functional programs, context-dependent transcriptional changes and structural-functional associations supported by molecular docking. Across ten iPSC lines from distinct donors, GRAFT identified candidate inter-donor differences, with functional support for selected candidates from measured genetic perturbation responses. Together, GRAFT enables perturbation-informed prediction and comparison of drug responses across cellular contexts.

papers.title: Phenotypic screening in Parkinson's iPSC-dopamine neurons identifies the FASN-SREBP1 axis as a potential therapeutic target
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) remains highly challenging to model in vitro, particularly when seeking robust functional phenotypes for target discovery. Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell dopaminergic neurons (iPSC-DANs) offer a promising platform to address this challenge. Because calcium dyshomeostasis is well-described in PD pathophysiology, it offers a platform for phenotypic screening. We have previously shown that GBA-N370S iPSC-DANs display impaired intracellular calcium release. Here, we used this disease-relevant phenotype to undertake a 4,108-compound phenotypic screen in GBA-N370S (GBA-NS) iPSC-DANs. This screen identified fatty acid synthase (FASN) as the most enriched protein target. The ability of compounds to rescue calcium release correlated with biochemical potency against FASN across multiple chemical series. We confirmed that FASN knockdown increased intracellular calcium release, supporting an on-target effect. Untargeted lipidomics demonstrated broad remodelling of the neuronal lipidome after FASN inhibition, confirming target engagement. FASN inhibition also increased active a-glucocerebrosidase (GCase), reduced extracellular a-synuclein release and ER stress, and altered RASGRF1 expression. Mechanistically, FASN inhibition activated sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 (SREBP1), and SREBP1 overexpression alone was sufficient to increase intracellular calcium release, identifying a FASN-SREBP1-calcium homeostasis axis in human neurons. Finally, the FASN inhibitor BI 99179 achieved brain exposure and reduced brain fatty acid levels while inducing an SRE-associated transcriptional response in a Parkinson's mouse model, providing evidence of in vivo target engagement. These findings establish patient iPSC-neuron functional screening as a tractable discovery platform to identify targets which can be taken in vivo and nominate the FASN-SREBP1 axis as a candidate therapeutic pathway in PD.

papers.title: Molecular MRI of Neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's Disease using a Folate-targeted Nanoprobe
papers.abstract: Background: Neuroinflammation, driven by activated microglia, plays a central role in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Non-invasive imaging of neuroinflammation holds promise for advancing our understanding of disease mechanisms and evaluating anti-inflammatory therapeutic strategies. The folate receptor (FR), specifically its {beta} isoform, has been identified as a marker of pro-inflammatory myeloid cells in peripheral inflammatory diseases; however, its association with AD neuroinflammation remains unknown. In this work, we first determined FR expression in microglia in mouse models of AD and subsequently evaluated molecular MRI (mMRI) using a folate-targeted nanoprobe for in vivo imaging of the folate receptor expression. Methods and results: Microglial activation and FR expression in APP/PS1 and P301S transgenic mouse models of AD was measured using flow cytometry. A FR-targeted nanoprobe for mMRI was prepared by functionalizing high T1-relaxivity liposomal gadolinium nanoparticle with folic acid. Following intravenous injection, localization of the nanoprobe in the brains of aged transgenic and wild-type mice was measured using T1-weighted MRI. Post-mortem microscopy measured nanoprobe localization relative to microglia and amyloid pathology. In both mouse models, FR{beta} was significantly (p < 0.05) upregulated in pro-inflammatory microglia expressing TNF and IL-1{beta}. The folate-targeted nanoprobe demonstrated MR signal enhancement in the cortical and hippocampal regions of transgenic mice but not in wild type mice; non-targeted nanoprobe control did not demonstrate signal enhancement in brain of transgenic mice. Microscopy confirmed colocalization of FR-targeted nanoprobe with IBA1-positive microglia/macrophages and amyloid plaques. Conclusions: Pro-inflammatory microglia exhibit elevated levels of FR, and its measurement by non-invasive mMRI is a promising marker of neuroinflammation in AD.

papers.title: The ViRA-L (Visual Recognition Assessment-Leuven): Development, Validation, and Age Stratified Normative Characterization of a Multi-Category Visual Recognition Battery
papers.abstract: Objective: To develop and validate the Visual Recognition Assessment-Leuven (ViRA-L), a recognition-memory battery assessing ten visual categories within a matched task structure, and provide age-stratified normative data. Method: Healthy Dutch-speaking adults completed a visual recognition task for ten categories. Each category included six targets, 18 Learning trials, and 30 Novel trials requiring recognition across appearance changes. After exclusions, 417 participants remained. We evaluated reliability, score distributions, task effects, demographic associations, and category-specific norms. Results: Battery-level internal consistency was good (Cronbach's = .879; omega total = .901), with lower category-level estimates, broad score dispersion, and minimal floor and ceiling effects. Novel and difficult trials produced lower accuracy and slower responses. Age was the clearest demographic correlate of accuracy; gender and education showed no independent overall associations. Age effects varied by category and were larger in Novel than Learning trials. Model-based differences between ages 50 and 85 were largest for Pseudowords and Hands and smallest for Houses. Conclusions: The ViRA-L supports comparison of recognition-memory profiles under matched procedures. Category-dependent age associations support age-sensitive, category-specific interpretation. The battery provides a foundation for neuropsychological research; further validation is required for clinical diagnostic use.

papers.title: Oleic acid suppresses NLRP3 inflammasome activation to prevent dermal macrophage death and limit imiquimod-induced psoriasis
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is associated with altered lipid metabolism, including reduced expression of fatty acid metabolism genes and decreased circulating oleic acid. Here we report that oral oleic acid supplementation normalized serum oleic acid levels and protected from skin thickening and epidermal hyperplasia in a imiquimod mice model of psoriasis. These effects were associated with preserved skin-resident macrophage numbers and reduced expression of key psoriasis-associated inflammatory markers. Mechanistically, imiquimod induces dermal macrophage death via NLRP3/caspase-1 inflammasome activation, while adoptive transfer of dermal macrophages attenuates psoriasiform inflammation. Oleic acid rescued macrophages from imiquimod and nigericin-induced death in vitro by suppressing NF-{kappa}B and NLRP3/caspase-1 signaling, lowering IL-1{beta} and reactive oxygen species production, and restoring mitochondrial homeostasis, independently of TLR7. Together, our results position dermal macrophage survival as a previously unrecognized checkpoint in psoriasiform inflammation, and suggest that restoring lipid metabolic fitness, rather than solely targeting downstream inflammatory mediators, may offer an additional mechanism-based strategy to limit tissue- damaging inflammation.

papers.title: Impact of RNA modification and IL-12 boosts on mRNA-LNP vaccine-elicited CD8+ T cell responses
papers.abstract: Development of effective HIV-1 vaccines requires strategies for inducing both CD8+ T cell and neutralizing antibody responses. Nucleoside-modified mRNA-lipid-nanoparticles (LNP) induce more potent antibody responses than unmodified mRNA-LNP vaccines, while unmodified mRNA is typically employed for CD8+ T cell-inducing vaccines. Here, we compared the abilities of differing ratios of unmodified versus modified mRNA expressing a SIV conserved-region CD8+ T cell immunogen co-administered with IL-12-encoding mRNA-LNP during boosting to induce CD8+ T cell and humoral responses in non-human primates, assessing responses in ChAdOx1-primed controls in parallel. Serial priming and boosting with fully-unmodified mRNA elicited higher-magnitude, more CD8-biased T cell responses than fully-modified mRNA, that were durably maintained after the IL-12-encoding mRNA boosts. Inclusion of 30% nucleoside-modified mRNA enhanced antibody titers, suggesting potential benefits to a mixed-composition vaccine.

papers.title: Longitudinal persistence of EEG brain fingerprints: phase and complex coherency geometry across sessions and functional states
papers.abstract: Sensor-level EEG coherency can distinguish individuals, although its phase and magnitude patterns may reflect neural activity, source mixing, and recording geometry. We evaluated two geometric representations of complex coherency - unit phasors and full complex coherency - alongside triangle holonomies and magnitude-only descriptors. Using direct enrollment-probe matching without a trained identity classifier, we analyzed three independent longitudinal cohorts: RestCog (N = 60; approximately one month), L-FAME (N = 44; six weeks), and Dortmund (N = 206; approximately five years). In eyes-closed rest-to-rest matching, alpha phasors identified 81.67% of participants in RestCog (AUC 0.9473) and 79.55% in L-FAME (AUC 0.9735); full complex coherency identified 78.33% and 84.09%, respectively. After five years in Dortmund, fixed row-standardized alpha-beta fusion yielded 77.67% rank-1 identification (AUC 0.9744) for phasors and 70.39% (AUC 0.9527) for full coherency. Changes in functional state exposed different strengths: full coherency preserved higher rank-1 accuracy in some monthly RestCog rest-to-task comparisons, whereas alpha phasors retained higher verification AUC. Switching between eyes-closed and eyes-open recordings in Dortmund substantially weakened identification with both representations. Triangle holonomies also retained individual information across visits. An exact factorization of complex cosine shows how magnitude-pattern alignment and magnitude-weighted phase agreement contribute to full-coherency matching.
